GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3750 
FOR ANSWER ON 11.08.2026  
 
INCIDENTS OF THEFT IN DURGAPUR STEEL PLANT 
 
 
3750.  SHRI AZAD KIRTI JHA: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of incidents involving the theft of valuable scrap, 
steel plates and other steel materials from the Durgapur Steel Plant (DSP) of the SAIL, 
if so, the year wise and incident-wise details thereof during the last three years; 
 
(b) the total quantity of material (in tonnes) stolen from the plant during the said period 
and the estimated financial loss caused to SAIL; 
 
(c) whether any inquiry/investigation has been conducted by SAIL, the Ministry, or any 
other agency into these incidents, if so, the major findings of such investigation; 
 
(d) whether the investigation has revealed the involvement of any officials/employees 
of the DSP management, contractors, or the CISF, if so, the action taken against the 
persons found responsible; and 
 
(e) the concrete measures taken by the Government to prevent future theft of valuable 
scrap steel materials, strengthen security arrangements and ensure greater 
accountability? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(e): Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) deploys comprehensive security 
and monitoring systems across its Plants/Units which includes CCTV surveillance, 
with GPS-enabled vehicle tracking system and round-the-clock security at the 
designated entry and exit point to prevent the incidents of theft. As per the information 
available with SAIL, no incidents of theft involving valuable scrap, steel plates, or 
other steel materials have been recorded at Durgapur Steel Plant during the last three 
years.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3751 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 20, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Misleading Mobile Applications  
3751.      Shri P C Mohan: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken by the Government to identify and curb illicit, fraudulent 
and misleading mobile applications, including loan apps, used to defraud 
citizens, and the number of such apps blocked or removed duri ng the last 
two years;  
(b) the coordination mechanism between this Ministry, the Ministry of 
Electronics and Information Technology, the Reserve Bank of India and the 
Department of Telecommunications in this regard;  
(c) the outcomes achieved through platforms such as the National Cyber 
Crime Reporting Portal, helpline 1930, Sanchar Saathi and Chakshu, 
including the amount of money saved for citizens; and  
(d) the awareness campaigns being conducted to educate citizens  on 
identifying and reporting fraudulent apps and cyber fraud? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
 
 
 

 
 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3751 FOR 11.08.2026 
(a) to (d) :    
The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime 
Coordination Centre’ (I4C)  as an attached office to deal with all types of 
cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. 
The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) 
(https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable 
public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with 
special focus on cyber crimes against women and children. 
‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending 
notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency 
under clause (b) of sub -section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to 
facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or 
communication link being used to commit an unlawful act.  Till 30.06.2026, 
a total of 3718 mobile apps including fraudulent loan apps have been 
blocked by I4C under Section 69(A), Section 79(3)(b) of IT Act 2000. 
The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate 
reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the 
fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30. 06.2026, financial 
amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 
lakh complaints. 

 
-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3751 FOR 11.08.2026 
 
A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched 
by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 
30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from 
Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the 
participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth 
Rs. 25,698 crores. Till 30.06.2026, more than 15.75 lakhs SIM cards and 5.77 
lakhs IMEIs as reported by Police authorities have been blocked by 
Government of India. 
To strengthen the operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in 
handling cybercrime complai nts, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive 
Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP -CFCFRMS. The SOP lays 
down a standardized framework for complaint processing, bank 
coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration 
of defr auded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received 
through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of 
defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely 
attending to the grievances relating to freezi ng of the bank accounts and 
lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026. 
To further spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government 
has   taken   steps   which,    inter-alia,    include;   caller    tune   campaign,  
 

 
-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3751 FOR 11.08.2026 
 
dissemination of messages through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. X 
(formerly Twitter) (@CyberDost), Facebook(CyberDostI4C), Instagram 
(CyberDostI4C), Telegram(cyberdosti4c),    SMS    campaign,    TV    
campaign,    Radio campaign, School Campaign, advertisement in cinema 
halls, celebrity endorsement, IPL campaign, engaged MyGov for publicity in 
multiple mediums,  organizing Cyber Safety and Security Awareness weeks 
in association with States/UTs, publishing of Han dbook for 
Adolescents/Students, digital displays on railway stations and airports 
across, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 11th AUGUST, 2026 
 
DISEASE RESISTANT SUGARCANE SEEDS 
 
3753. Shri Rajeev Rai: 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare/ कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the continued cultivation of the red rot-
susceptible sugarcane variety Co.0238 in Uttar Pradesh despite repeated advisories 
for its phased replacement, if so, the district-wise area still under the variety; 
(b) the details of disease-resistant sugarcane seed supplied and the number of 
farmers covered under the replacement programme during the last three years, 
district-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for the slow adoption of 
recommended disease-resistant varieties, including shortages of quality seed, 
extension support and farmer awareness, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the incidence of red rot disease since 2021, district-wise; and 
(e) the outcome of the replacement programme in reducing crop losses and improving 
productivity? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏयमंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) : As per the information received from State Government, the area under Co 0238 
variety of sugarcane in Uttar Pradesh declined from 86% in 2020–21 to 29% in 2025–
26, reflecting the phased replacement of this variety.  
District wise area under Co 0238 variety and total area under Sugarcane in UP during 
2025-26 is at Annexure I. 
 
(b) :  During last three years, the State Government has carried out production and 
distribution of seeds of red rot disease resistant sugarcane varieties in a phased 
manner through breeder, foundation and primary nurseries. District wise details of 
disease resistant seed distributed by State Government in last three years is at 
Annexure II.  
 

(c) : As informed by State Government, the pace of variety replacement was slow in 
the initial phase due to the area under sugarcane variety Co 0238 being more than 
86% of the total coverage and the relatively longer time required for the Seed 
multiplication process of sugarcane seed. However, the pace of variety replacement 
has now accelerated due to the availability of several new early maturing sugarcane 
varieties such as CoS 19231, CoS 17451, CoS 18231, CoLk 16202, CoLk 15466, Co 
15023 and mid and late maturing sugarcane varieties such as CoS 16233, CoS 15233, 
CoLk 16470, CoLk 15206, CoLk 14204, CoLk 15207. 
 
(d) : As per the data provided by State Government, the area affected by red rot 
disease in sugarcane, district wise since 2021-22 is at Annexure III. 
 
(e) : The State Government has informed that, as a result of the varietal replacement 
programme, crop losses due to disease have reduced. The yield per hectare has gone 
up from 81.34 MT in 2023-24 to 81.97 MT in 2025-26.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
PROMOTION OF OIL PALM CULTIVAITON 
 
3754. SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH 
SHRI ANTO ANTONY: - 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the area brought under oil palm cultivation, area under production and 
crude palm oil produced under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-
OP) in the country, State/UT-wise including Kerala since 2021, district-wise; 
(b) the survival rate of oil palm plantations established under the Mission, including area 
replanted or abandoned, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the details of oil palm cultivation promoted in the Southern region of Kerala, including 
the area covered, number of beneficiary farmers, financial assistance provided and 
the present status of plantations; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the suitability of the agro-climatic conditions 
of the region for sustainable oil palm cultivation and, if so, the details and findings 
thereof; 
(e) the number of operational oil palm processing mills in the country, State/UT-wise 
including Kerala, their processing capacity and the arrangements made for 
procurement of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) State/UT-wise; and 
(f) the steps taken or proposed to improve processing infrastructure, farmer support, 
assured procurement and productivity under NMEO-OP in Kerala, particularly in the 
Southern region? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): Since 2021-22, under the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) 2.98 
lakh hectares has been brought under oil palm cultivation. As oil palm is a perennial crop 
with a gestation period of about 4-5 years, most of the area planted under the Mission is 
yet to attain full bearing. From 2021-22 to 2025-26, the Crude Palm Oil (CPO) production 
was 20.10 lakh tonnes. State-wise details of area covered and CPO production are given 
in Annexure-I, while district-wise details for Kerala are given in Annexure-II. 
(b): The survival rate of oil palm plantations varies across States depending on 
management practices, availability of irrigation, and edaphic conditions. Full survival rate 
can be achieved, when the scientific package of practices recommended by ICAR–Indian 
Institute of Oil Palm Research (ICAR-IIOPR) is followed. During the implementation of the 
Mission, no State has reported area being abandoned or requiring complete replantation 
due to plantation failure. Further, the Mission provides assistance for gap filling/replanting 
to maintain the optimum plant population and sustain productivity wherever required. 

(c): During the Mission period, oil palm cultivation has been promoted in the Southern 
region of Kerala covering 312.94 hectares. Financial assistance of Rs. 386.881 lakh has 
been provided benefitting 17 oil palm farmers.  
(d): ICAR-IIOPR Reassessment Committee report (2020) identified 27.99 lakh hectares 
as potential area for oil palm cultivation in the country based on scientific evaluation of 
agro-climatic suitability and land suitability parameters. 
(e): The State wise details including Kerala of operational processing mills and their 
processing capacity are given in Annexure-III. The Oil Palm companies procure Fresh 
Fruit Bunches (FFBs) from farmers in their respective catchment areas as per prescribed 
price assurance mechanism under NMEO-OP.  
(f): The Government is taking several interventions under NMEO-OP, including in Kerala, 
to strengthen the entire oil palm value chain. These interventions include support for 
expansion of processing infrastructure, availability of quality planting material, 
establishment of seed nurseries and seed gardens, assistance for maintenance and 
intercropping during the gestation period, micro-irrigation, farm mechanization, replanting, 
and capacity building of farmers. Efforts are also being made to promote oil palm 
cultivation in scientifically identified suitable areas and strengthen linkages among 
farmers, processing units and oil palm companies to facilitate timely harvesting, 
procurement and processing of FFBs. In addition, the pricing mechanism provides 
assurance to oil palm farmers by protecting them from fluctuations in international crude 
palm oil prices.

3756. SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU:  
          SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY:  
SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI:  
SHRI RAJKUMAR CHAHAR:  
SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN: 
 
Will the MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the details of marine and inland fish exports from the country during the last three years, product-
wise and country-wise; 
(b) the measures taken by the Government to improve quality standards, traceability, certification 
and global competitiveness of fisheries exports; 
(c) whether any sp ecial initiatives have been taken by the Government to promote value added 
fisheries products, if so, the details thereof including shrimp and other aquaculture products, in 
leading fisheries-producing States such as Andhra Pradesh;  
(d) the infrastructure  and financial assistance provided for processing, cold chain, testing, 
certification and export-oriented fisheries infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh during the last three years; 
and  
(e) whether the Government has any proposals for any additional measures to strengthen seafood 
exports from Andhra Pradesh by expanding value addition, diversification of export markets and 
support for exporters under the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) and the 
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), if so, the details thereof?  
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) . As reported by the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), India 
exported 19.72 lakh metric tonnes of seafood valued at ₹73,891 crore during FY 2025 ‑26. The   
product-wise and country-wise export details of seafood products, including marine and inland fish 
exports, for the last three years are provided in Annexure-I and Annexure-II, respectively. 

 
 
 
 
 
The Export Inspection Council (EIC), under the Department of Commerce, is the Competent 
Authority for quality control and inspection of notified export products, including marine products. 
To ensure compliance with importing countries' requirements, EIC co nducts periodic training on 
Food Safety Management System (FSMS) requirements and mandates testing of farmed shrimp for  
prohibited antibiotics during export certification. MPEDA supports these efforts through pre-harvest 
testing, the SHAPHARI certificatio n programme and, together with the Coastal Aquaculture 
Authority (CAA) and EIC, implementation of the National Residue Control Plan (NRCP) to 
strengthen residue monitoring, traceability and adherence to international standards. 
The Department of Fisheries supports quality enhancement and export competitiveness through 
PMMSY by promoting branding, standards and certification, capacity building, post -harvest 
infrastructure, cold-chain facilities and modernization of fishing harbours and fish landing centres. 
The Department has also released the National Framework on Traceability in Fisheries and 
Aquaculture, 2025 , and is facilitating implementation of the Nabhmitra mobile application to 
strengthen digital traceability, transparency and record-keeping in the marine fisheries sector. 
To enhance the global competitiveness of Indian seafood exports, the Government has undertaken 
various policy reforms and ease of doing business measures, including rationalisation of customs 
duties on key aquaculture inputs, enhance ment of the duty -free import limit of specified seafood 
processing inputs from 1% to 3%  of the previous year's FOB ( Free on Board)  export value, 
streamlining of import procedures, reduction of GST on ready -to-eat seafood products, and 
notification of the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 
2025. The Department is also promoting the fitment of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets 
and supporting the Marine Mammal Project to promote sustainable fisheries.  As reported by the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh, the State has also undertaken measures such as implementation of 
the APSADA Act, 2020; promotion of Best Management Practices (BMPs) and biosecurity; 
strengthening of NABL‑accredited testing facilities at the State Institute of Fisheries Technology 
(SIFT), Kakinada; and coordination closely with MPEDA, EIC and ICAR institutes to enhance 
traceability, certification, and food‑safety standards.  
Under the flagship schemes, namely the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), 
Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) and Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Kisan Samridhi Sah -Yojana (PMMKSSY), the Department of Fisheries is promoting processed, 
branded and value -added seafood products to reduce dependenc e on raw seafood exports. India's 
share of value-added seafood products in total seafood exports has increased from 2.5% to 11% over 
the past decade, reaching ₹7,133 crore. The Department has accorded approvals amounting to ₹2,797 
crore under PMMSY and FID F for development of cold -chain, marketing and seafood processing 
infrastructure across the country, while MPEDA has provided financial assistance of ₹118.10 crore 
to 89 seafood processing units under its Technology Development for Specific Value-Added Marine 
Products (TDSVMP) Scheme. The Department, in collaboration with MPEDA, the Department of 
Commerce, the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) and other stakeholders, has also 
organised Seafood Exporter Meets, stakeholder consultations, Chintan Shivirs, Round Table 
Conferences and the National Workshop on Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam to promote value 
addition, market diversification, quality compliance, traceability and export competitiveness. Further, 
during 2020 -21 to 2025 -26, projects amou nting to ₹2,333.61 crore, including a Central share of 
₹683.93 crore, have been approved under PMMSY for Andhra Pradesh for development of cold- 
 

 
 
 
 
chain, value-addition, fish markets, transport, fishing harbours, fish landing centres, Integrated Aqua 
Park and other export -oriented fisheries infrastructure. At present, there is no proposal under 
consideration for introducing any additional Central measures specifically for Andhra Pradesh under 
MPEDA or PMMSY. However, eligible stakeholders in the State continue to receive assistance under 
the existing schemes and programmes in accordance with the applicable guidelines.

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY ¼okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=h½  be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish export promotion and logistics 
infrastructure for MSMEs and agro-based industries in Western Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether districts like Sambhal, Moradabad and Amroha have been identified for 
such initiatives; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the expected timeline for implementation?

okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d) To strengthen India's overall export competitiveness, the Union Cabinet 
approved the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 12 November 2025. The Mission 
provides targeted support to exporters, with a special focus on Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), rural entrepreneurs, artisans, and agro -based 
industries across all States and Union Territories, including Western Uttar Pradesh. 
 
The Mission addresses export development through two integrated sub -
schemes: 
 Niryat Prothsahan: Focused on improving access to export finance through 
Interest Subvention for pre- and post-shipment export credit, Export Factoring 
support, Collateral Guarantees for export credit, Credit Guarantee for e -
commerce exporters, and Support for emerging opportunities for MSME 
exporters. 
 Niryat Disha: Focused on non-financial trade enablers, including export quality 
and compliance support, logistics and overseas warehousing, Market Access  
Support, global branding and packaging, facilitating logistics 
interventions for freight and transport, and trade intelligence. 
Under the Mission, proposals for export -related infrastructure, logistics facilities, 
and value-chain integration are considered in consultation with the concerned State 
Governments and other stakeholders based on export potential, sectoral strengths, 
and readiness of projects. 
 

2 
 
 
Under the Districts as Export Hub (DEH) initiative, exportable products have been 
identified across districts of the country including Sambhal, Moradabad, and Amroha. 
The capacity building programs under the DEH initiative are aimed at creating linkages 
between district-level producers and global markets by leveraging the interventions of 
EPM. 
 
The District Export Promotion Committee (DEPC) have been constituted and the 
District Export Action Plans (DEAPs) have been prepared and adopted for all three 
districts, namely Sambhal, Moradabad and Amroha. The products with significant  
pootential for exports have been identified-Sambhal (Menthol, Horn and Bone Craft); 
Moradabad (Metal Craft, Mentha Oil, Rice); Amroha (Musical Instruments, Articles of 
Iron/Steel/Aluminium) 
 
For the purpose of transforming logistic infrastructure, the Government has launched 
PM Gati  Shakti National Master Plan. This initiative proposes to  transform 
infrastructure planning by enabling a whole -of government approach through 
integrated and synchronized planning across Central Ministries/ Departments and 
States/UTs. The initiative proposes to enhance multimodal connectivity, improved first-
mile and last -mile connectivity to economic centres, industrial clusters, ports and 
logistics hubs, faster project planning and implementation  through better inter-agency 
coordination, and timely identification of infrastructure gaps and bottlenecks.

Pradesh; 
(b) the details of the specific action plans drafted by the District Export Promotion 
Committees to bridge infrastructural gaps in the chosen districts of Bihar and 
Madhya Pradesh during the last one year; 
(c) the total central funds released for creating common facil ity centres, testing 
laboratories and cold storage chains in these export -oriented districts of Bihar 
and Madhya Pradesh; 
(d) whether the Ministry has noted a lack of direct institutional credit and trade

ANSWER 
okf.kT; ,oa m|ksx ea=ky; esa jkT;ea=h ¼Jh ftfru izlkn½ 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (b) The Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative of the Department of Commerce, 
implemented through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), seeks to 
decentralise export promotion by making every district an active stakeholder in the 
country’s export growth. 
The DEH initiative is a pan -India initiative where all districts across the country are 
targeted to promote export participation. 
 
Under this initiative products and services with export potential have been identified 
across all districts, including districts of Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. 
 
The Draft District Export Action Plans (DEAPs) have been prepared and adopted,  in 
consultation with district -level stakeholders, for 38 districts of Bihar and in 52 of 55 

2 
 
districts of Madhya Pradesh, and a re periodically reviewed by the respective District 
Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs) to align with evolving global demand and 
district-specific production strengths. 
 
The Districts as Export Hubs initiative is a collaborative and facilitative framework that 
aims to address export bottlenecks identified at the grassroots. Within this framework, 
the DEPCs prepare the DEAPs, which assess the production and cluster strengths of 
the district, identify gaps relating to aggregation, quality and certification, t esting, 
packaging, warehousing, logistics connectivity and buyer linkages, and set out 
corresponding action points and implementing agencies. The primary focus of DEAPs 
is on export related bottlenecks such as exporter capacity development,  skill 
upgradation, bridging information asymmetries, providing market intelligence and 
others beyond directly targeting infrastructure development. 
 
(c) to (e) The Districts as Export Hubs initiative operates through convergence of 
existing schemes. The DEH framework is a facilitative approach to bring Central 
Ministries/Departments, State Governments, District Administrations and district -level 
stakeholders onto a common platform through the DEPC and leverage ongoing 
schemes of the Central and State Governments — including the financial assistance 
available thereunder and by promoting convergence among them. 
 
To strengthen access to trade finance and e xport credit for small and first -time 
exporters, including those located in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, the Government  is 
undertaking a focused, outcome -oriented implementation of DEH. Through this 
implementation, financial institutions and agencies including ECGC, EXIM Bank, 
SIDBI, NCGTC and NABARD, along with India Post, have been onboarded to facilitate 
access to export finance at the grassroots, and further the Lead Bank nodal officers at 
the district level have been engaged to facilitate access to export credit. 
 
Further, the government has launched the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on  12th 
November 2025, with a total outlay of ₹25,060 crore for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 
2030-31, to strengthen India’s export competitiveness with a focused emphasis on 
MSMEs, first-time exporters, labour-intensive sectors and exporters from interior and 
low-export-intensity regions. Th e Mission operates through two integrated sub -
schemes — Niryat Protsahan, focused on improving access to aﬀordable trade 
finance through instruments such as interest subvention, collateral support for export 
credit, export factoring, credit guarantee for e -commerce exporters and support for 
alternative trade instruments; and Niryat Disha, focused on other trade enablers such 
as export quality and compliance support, international branding and packaging, 
market access, export logistics and warehousing, and t rade intelligence. The Niryat 
Disha sub -schemes address structural logistics constraints faced by hinterland 
exporters. The Logistics Interventions for Freight & Transport scheme provides support 
towards oﬀsetting inefficiencies in  inland connectivity aﬀecting remote and hinterland 
regions, thereby reducing the freight and logistics costs arising from locational 
disadvantages, while the Facilitating Logistics, Overseas Warehousing & Fulfilment 
scheme supports access to overseas logistics, warehousing and fulfilment 
arrangements to improve delivery efficiency in foreign markets.

3760. DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of present status of implementation of the Electric Vehicle (EV) policy in the country;  
 
(b) the details of steps taken to promote battery manufacturing in the country;  
 
(c) the details of current status of EV charging infrastructure;  
 
(d) the details of subsidy policy being implemented to promote adoption of electric vehicles; and  
 
(e) the details of contribution of electric vehicles in reducing pollution? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) to (e): The details and progress of the schemes implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries 
(MHI) for the development of electric vehicles in the country along with charging infrastructure are as under:- 
 
(i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturi ng of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME 
India) Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 
01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided 
demand incentive for e -2Ws, e -3Ws, e -4Ws and grant for e -buses and setting up of EV public 
charging stations (EV PCS).  FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric 
vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws.  In addition, 5,299 electric buses (e-buses) have been 
deployed under the Scheme as on 31.07.2026.  Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated 
under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country.  9,583 EV PCS have been 
installed under this scheme. 
 
(ii)  Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component 
Industry in India (PLI -Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for 
Advanced Aut omotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore.  
 
(iii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced  
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme 
for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore.  The scheme aims 
to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries,  out of 
which, 40 GWh has been awarded to four beneficiary firms.  The 40 GWh capacity is end-use agnostic 
and can be utilized for any application including electric vehicles. 
 
 
 
 

 
-2- 
 
(iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) 
Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024.  This scheme 
supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e -2W, e-3W, 
e-Trucks, e -buses and e -Ambulances.  Further, grant for upgradation of  testing agencies is also 
available under this scheme.  An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for 
deployment of 14,028 e -buses out of which 14,000 e -buses have been allocated.  ₹2,000 crore has 
been allocated for deployment of EV PCS  on pan India basis.  Phased Manufacturing Programme 
(PMP) Mandates the domestic manufacturing of EV components, including battery packs, in a phased 
manner. 
 
(v)  PM e -Bus Sewa -Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 
28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric 
buses.  The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e -bus operators in case of default by 
Public Transport Authorities (PTAs).  As on 10.07.2026, the PM-eBus Sewa – Payment Security Mechanism 
(PSM) Scheme covers 27,555 e-buses.  Of these, 10,000 e-buses are under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme of the 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), 14,000 e-buses are under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme of the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), and 3,555 e -buses under various State Government/State Transport 
Undertaking (STU) initiatives. 
 
 Further, following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the 
use of electric vehicles in the country:– 
i.  GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced to 5%. 
ii.  Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles will be 
given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. 
iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce the initial

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3761 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
 INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT SCHEMES  
 
3761. Shri Anurag Singh Thakur: 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare/ कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of widespread fall armyworm infestation 
affecting maize crops across Kangra, Chamba, Una, Hamirpur, Bilaspur, Mandi 
districts of Himachal Pradesh, with infestation levels reaching up to 15 per cent in 
some blocks; 
(b) the details of financial, technical assistance, including under Integrated Pest 
Management schemes, extended to Himachal to combat this infestation and whether 
any Central team has been deputed to assess situation; 
(c) whether the Government has any plans to provide compensation to                      
farmers who have suffered yield losses or abandoned maize cultivation due to 
recurring fall armyworm attacks through PMFBY;   
(d) the details of advisories, surveillance measures, integrated pest management 
(IPM) interventions, pheromone traps, biopesticides, approved insecticides, 
awareness campaigns, assistance provided by Central Government through ICAR, 
Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other agencies to control the infestation; and 
(e)  the details of other steps taken to strengthen early-warning, pest-surveillance and 
research support for invasive pests? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏयमंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): As per information received from Agriculture Department, Government of 
Himachal Pradesh, a total of 2,54,104 hectares of area is under Maize cultivation 
covering 10 districts of Himachal Pradesh, out of which an area of 19,028 hectares 
(7.48%) has been reported to be affected by Fall Army Worm (FAW). District wise 
details are at Annexure-I. 
(b): Government of India is implementing National Food Security & Nutrition Mission 
(NFSNM) with the objective to increase production and productivity of various crops 
including Coarse Cereals (Maize & Barley). During 2026-27, an amount of Rs. 12.375 
lakhs have been approved for Integrated Pest Management intervention under 
NFSNM – Coarse Cereals for the State of Himachal Pradesh. 

     Technical assistance has been extended through the Integrated Pest Management 
(IPM) programme wherein Central Integrated Pest Management Centre (CIPMC), 
Solan has been conducting regular surveillance, Rapid Roving Surveys, pest 
monitoring and issuing farmer advisories. Joint field surveys are being undertaken by 
CIPMC, Solan and the State Agriculture Department. 
     Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) of Indian Council of Agricultural Research 
(ICAR) has informed that continuous monitoring of FAW were carried out throughout 
the season along with Agriculture Department of State Government and Krishi Vigyan 
Kendras (KVKs) and necessary control measures were communicated to them. The 
updated package of practices (PoP) for management of fall armyworm on maize is 
shared regularly with All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) Maize centres 
including Kangra and Bajaura. 
    Further, as informed by the State Government of Himachal Pradesh, farmers have 
been assisted through organizing various camps, advising them to adopt IPM, 
mechanical, chemical & biological techniques as well as use of pheromones traps, 
Neem based pesticides, Trichoderma & predators etc. to control FAW. State 
Government in consultation with State Agriculture University, concerned KVKs in 
Bilaspur, Kangra, Una, Mandi, Chamba, Hamirpur districts has issued timely advisory 
and supplied the pesticides to the affected areas. Advisory was issued to the farmers 
through pamphlets, newspapers, radio announcements and other social media 
platforms. 
(c): Government has introduced yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance 
Scheme (RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide comprehensive risk insurance against 
crop damage from pre-sowing to post-harvest for crops and area notified by the 
concerned State Government. The scheme is being implemented in Himachal 
Pradesh. All willing farmers are eligible to enroll under the scheme. The yield losses 
or losses due to non-preventable risks are covered under the PMFBY scheme and the 
insured farmers under the scheme, are eligible to receive claims as per the provisions 
of the operational guidelines of the scheme. 
(d) & (e): In Himachal Pradesh including Kangra, Chamba, Una, Hamirpur, Bilaspur, 
and Mandi districts CIPMC, Solan has conducted a total of 105 Farmer Field Schools 
programmes during 2024-25 and 115 programmes during 2025-26 to create 
awareness among farmers regarding FAW. Further, advisories have also been issued 
by CIPMC, Solan for management of FAW reported in Maize crop during 2026-27. 
Details of advisories issued is at Annexure-II. 

CIPMC, Solan carried out regular surveillance in maize-growing areas of Himachal 
Pradesh for early detection and monitoring of FAW. Based on field observations, 
timely advisories were disseminated to farmers emphasizing IPM practices, including 
regular field scouting, installation and monitoring of pheromone traps, collection and 
destruction of egg masses and early instar larvae and periodic release of biological 
control agents for the management of early instar larvae of Fall Armyworm. Further, 
there are 25 different insecticides including biopesticides registered in India for the 
management of FAW in maize (Annexure III) and a need-based application of these 
approved pesticides is recommended during IPM programmes. 
    Following the detection of FAW in India, the IIMR in collaboration with State 
Governments, KVKs and other stakeholders, has developed a comprehensive 
Package of Practices (PoP) for FAW management in maize covering cultural, 
mechanical, biological and chemical control measures, which was disseminated to all 
KVKs, SAUs for adoption.  
     Further, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) has launched 
"National Pest Surveillance System" (NPSS) on 15.08.2024, to enhance real-time pest 
surveillance, crop disease monitoring and AI-based advisory systems across the 
country. The system utilizes latest digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence 
and Machine Learning (AI and ML) to provide quick and instant solution regarding pest 
attacks, crop diseases, crop damages etc. by issuing real time crop protection advisory 
to the farmers. In NPSS, farmers are advised to use bio-control agents or bio-
pesticides and the chemical pesticides as a last resort that too Registration Committee 
(RC) recommended label claim pesticides.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION 3762 
ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
  
E-GRAM SWARAJ AND AUDITONLINE 
 
  
†3762. SHRI BHARAT SINGH KUSHWAH: 
 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
 
(a)  whether the Government has information regarding the number of Gram Panchayats 
across the country integrated with systems and the extent to which these e-Gram SWARAJ and 
Audit Online being utilized in Madhya Pradesh and the Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, if so, 
the details thereof; 
  
(b)  the details of the e-Gram SWARAJ portal in preparing and approving Gram Panchayat 
Development Plans digitally and the number of Gram Panchayats in Gwalior Lok Sabha 
constituency that have prepared their annual development plans through this system; 
  
(c)  whether e-Gram SWARAJ has been integrated with other government digital platforms 
to make the accounts, payments, monitoring of works and financial management of Panchayats 
more transparent, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d)  whether training programmes have been organized for Sarpanches, Panches, Panchayat 
Secretaries and other officials of Madhya Pradesh, especially in Gwalior Lok Sabha 
constituency, for the effective operation of the digital system, if so, the number of participants 
who received training and the major outcomes thereof? 
 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode 
Project (MMP) to strengthen digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions across the 
country. Under the project, eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline have been developed to facilitate 
digital planning, budgeting, accounting, audit, asset management and monitoring of Panchayat 
activities. Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) are prepared through a participatory 
planning process and uploaded on the eGramSwaraj portal. 

2 
 
  
Further, eGramSwaraj has been integrated with various Government digital platforms, including 
the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for online payments and financial 
management, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for procurement, BHASHINI for multilingual 
AI-enabled services, BSNL for BharatNet connectivity monitoring and the India Meteorological 
Department (IMD) for weather-related information. 
 
The State/UT-wise details of implementation of eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, including the 
State of Madhya Pradesh and the Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, are given at Annexure-I.  
  
(d)  Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj conducts capacity-building programmes for 
elected representatives, Panchayat Secretaries and other Panchayat functionaries under the 
Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA). The training programmes include training 
on digital governance, effective utilisation of the e-Panchayat applications, preparation of Gram 
Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), data management and evidence-based planning. 
The State/UT-wise details of participants trained under RGSA, including those relating to the 
Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, are given at Annexure-II. The district/ constituency-wise 
details are maintained by the respective State Government. The training programmes have 
contributed to improved adoption and utilisation of the e-Panchayat applications, enhanced 
digital capacity of Panchayat functionaries and strengthened transparency and efficiency in 
Panchayat governance.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3763 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
VERIFICATION UNDER PM-KISAN 
 
3763.  SHRI JANARDAN SINGH SIGRIWAL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether all eligible farmers in the Maharajganj Lok Sabha Constituency of Bihar 
have been covered under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) Scheme;  
(b)  if so, the details thereof including the number of beneficiaries;  
(c)  whether the Government has received any complaints regarding exclusion of eligible 
farmers, delay in release of instalments, Aadhaar authentication issues or land record-
related discrepancies under the Scheme in the said constituency;  
(d)  if so, the details thereof, along with the number of such complaints received, 
disposed of and pending and the corrective measures taken by the Government in this 
regard; and  
(e)  whether the Government proposes to undertake any special enrolment/verification 
drive to ensure inclusion of all eligible farmers under the PM-KISAN Scheme in the 
Maharajganj Lok Sabha Constituency of Bihar and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Under the PM-KISAN Scheme, land seeding, Aadhaar linking with bank 
accounts and eKYC of the eligible beneficiaries have been made mandatory over the period 
to make the service delivery more efficient and transparent. The fulfilment of mandatory 
requirements by farmers and their validations is an essential condition to qualify as 
beneficiary and receive the benefits under the scheme. The States/UTs are mandated to 
enroll the beneficiaries and validate and verify their data. Funds are released on the basis 
of beneficiaries identified and verified by the States/UTs. Same process is followed in the 

State of Bihar including Maharajganj Lok Sabha Constituency leading to disbursement of 
benefits to eligible farmers in this Constituency. Details of beneficiaries benefitted in Saran 
and Siwan districts of Bihar and amount released to them in 23rd instalment is as follows: 
Districts Beneficiaries benefitted Amount released (₹ Crore) 
Saran 4,83,908 96.78 
Siwan 3,74,988 75.00 
 
(c) & (d): A robust grievance redressal mechanism has been established under the PM-
KISAN Scheme to address the grievances of farmers. Farmers may register their 
grievances through the PM-KISAN portal, where they are promptly examined and resolved 
by the concerned officers of the respective State/UT Governments. In addition, farmers may 
also lodge their grievances through the CPGRAMS portal, and such grievances are 
addressed and resolved in a timely manner. Since inception of the Scheme, 6,151 
grievances have been received on PM-KISAM portal in Saran district all of which have been 
resolved, and in Siwan District, 2,751 grievances have been received on PM-KISAM portal 
out of which 2,749 have been resolved. 
 
(e): In order to ensure that no eligible farmer is left out, the Government of India 
undertakes saturation drives in coordination with the States/UTs, including Bihar. A major 
nationwide saturation drive was undertaken from 15th November 2023 under the Viksit 
Bharat Sankalp Yatra (VBSY), during which, more than 1 Cr. farmers were included under 
PM-KISAN, including 3,44,180 in Bihar. Further, under the Government’s 100 days initiative 
in 2024, over 25 lakh eligible farmers were added under the PM-KISAN scheme including 
25,099 in Bihar. A special drive was also conducted in September 2024 to clear the 
pending self-registration cases, which resulted in the addition of over 30 lakh new farmers, 
including 33,614 in Bihar. A nationwide saturation drive has also been undertaken from 1st 
June, 2026 under PM-KISAN alongwith the “Khet Bachao Abhiyaan” to expand the 
coverage of eligible farmers under the scheme which resulted in the addition of about 17 
lakh new farmers, including 58,556 in Bihar. In addition, States/UTs, including Bihar, also 
undertake saturation drives from time to time to identify and facilitate the enrolment of 
eligible farmers completing all mandatory conditions under the Scheme.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3765 
ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY 
 
3765.  SHRI SRIBHARAT MATHUKUMILLI: 
 
Will the Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of prolonged rough sea conditions, climate 
variability and marine pollution on fish landings and the incomes of fishermen in Andhra 
Pradesh, particularly at Visakhapatnam and other major fishing harbours; 
 
(b) the details of financial assistance, subsidised diesel support, insurance claim settlements 
and other relief measures sanctioned and disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) and other Central schemes during the last three years, State-wise including 
Andhra Pradesh; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the adequacy of such assistance in offsetting 
operational losses incurred by fishermen and mechanised boat operato rs due to prolonged 
weather-induced fishing disruptions; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has any proposal to introduce a dedicated compensation or 
income-support mechanism for fishermen affected by prolonged weather -induced fishing 
disruptions and declining fish catch and the timeline fixed by the Government in this regard, if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) Indian Council of Agricultural Research – Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute 
(ICAR‑CMFRI) undertakes continuous monitoring of fish landings, conducts focused 
biological research, and tracks coastal ecosystem health through real‑time surveys across 
coastal States/UTs, including in Andhra Pradesh. The Fishery Survey of India (FSI) similarly 
conducts systematic exploratory surveys in the EEZ, generating baseline data on demersal and 
oceanic stocks to support assessments of impacts from fishing pressure, climate variability, 
pollution, and hab itat degradation. Available scientific evidence from these institutions 
indicates that while environmental stressors affect the distribution, abundance, and seasonal 
availability of certain species, no direct and conclusive impact on overall marine fish 
production has been established solely due to climate variability and marine pollution. Further, 
as per the Marine Fish Stock Status of India (2022)  of ICAR‑CMFRI, 91.1% of the 135 
assessed marine fish stocks in the Indian EEZ are at sustainable levels.  

 
(b) and (c) The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, A nimal Husbandry and 
Dairying, has been  implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 
across all States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, since 2020 –21. Under 
PMMSY, proposals amounting to ₹21,461.03 crore, with a Central share of ₹9,571.09 crore, 
have been approved for all States/UTs. For Andhra Pradesh, proposals of ₹2,328.89 crore, 
including a Central share of ₹681.38 crore, have been sanctioned. PMMSY also suppo rts 
long‑term resource enhancement measures such as installation of Artificial Reefs and Sea 
Ranching to improve fish availability and strengthen fishers’ livelihoods. Under the Fisheries 
and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), 253 projects  have been approved 
at a total cost of ₹6,657.57 crore, with ₹4,979.04 crore considered for interest subvention, for 
various States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh. 
The Department implements the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) under PMMSY 
through the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). During 2021‑22 to 2026‑27, the 
Central Government released ₹130.68 crore to provide insurance coverage to 167.64 lakh 
fishers, averaging 33.52 lakh fishers per year. State‑wise details of fishers insured and clai ms 
settled are at Annexure‑I. Additionally, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has reported 
provision of ₹150.00 crore as diesel subsidy to 63,840 beneficiaries during 2023‑24 to 2025‑26. 
Further, ₹511.46 crore has been provided to 2,55,731 marine fishers during the fishing ban 
period in 2025‑26 and 2026‑27. 
(d)  Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides livelihood 
and nutritional support to socio‑economically backward active traditional fishers’ families 
during the fishing ban and lean season, with the objective of conserving fish resources. Further, 
to augment fish stocks in coastal waters, the Department is working closely with State 
Governments on a range of resource‑enhancement measures, including establishment of 
artificial reefs along the coastline, conduct of sea ranching, and implementation of a uniform, 
annual fishing closure during the critical fish breeding period.

SUPPORT TO MANGO FARMERS 
 
3767. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी   
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that mango farmers in Andhra Pradesh, 
particularly in the Chittoor and Tirupati districts have been facing recurring distress due to 
the sharp fall in Thothapuri mango prices despite repeated representations; 
(b)  whether the Government has received proposals for establishment of a National 
Mango Board at Tirupati and a National Mango Research Station in Chittoor to strengthen 
procurement, price stabilization, exports, research and farmer support; 
(c)  if so, the reasons for the delay, if any, in taking action on the proposals received; and 
(d)  the time-bound measures proposed to improve mango marketing, processing, 
exports and income security for mango growers in Andhra Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी             (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  Government is aware of the decline in prices of Totapuri mango in Andhra Pradesh 
including Chittoor and Tirupati districts during the marketing season. In view of the request 
received from the State, Government has approved procurement of 2,16,250 Metric Tonnes 
(MT) of Totapuri mangoes under the Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) for the marketing 
season 2026-27 at a Market Intervention Price (MIP) of Rs. 1,747 per quintal. 
(b) & (c):  There is no such proposal under consideration in the Department of 
Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. However, ICAR- Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture 
(CISH), Lucknow and ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Bengaluru are 
involved in development of new high yielding varieties of mango and cultivation 
technologies like high-density planting, canopy management, integrated pest/disease 
management, nutrient management, post-harvest management and extension. 

(d):  A high-level Expert Committee comprising senior scientists from the Indian Council of 
Agricultural Research (ICAR), Dr. Y.S.R. Horticultural University and officers of the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh was constituted to examine the issues affecting Totapuri 
mango growers. The Committee conducted field visits to major Totapuri-growing districts 
including Chittoor and Tirupati and held consultations with farmers, Farmer Producer 
Organizations (FPOs), processors, traders, district administration and other stakeholders. 
The Expert Committee has recommended a number of short, medium and long-term 
interventions for improving mango marketing, processing, exports and farmer income 
security which includes - rejuvenation and top-working of old and senile mango orchards, 
replacement of old varieties with new and improved varieties, blending of 20% pulp in juice, 
RTS, nectar etc. to enhance pulp usage, zonal procurement and storage infrastructure for 
prolonged processing duration and export promotion. 
As informed by ICAR-Central Institute of Subtropical Horticulture (ICAR-CISH), 
Lucknow, the State Department of Horticulture has already completed the selection of 
farmers in Chittoor and Tirupati districts for development of top-working orchards.

TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER 
PMAY-G 
 
3769. Smt. Poonamben Hematbhai Maadam: 
 Shri Kaushalendra Kumar: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and total number of houses sanctioned, completed 
and delivered under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY-G) 
during Financial Year 2025-26, State-wise; 
(b)  the current status and target for completion of remaining 
houses under the scheme; 
(c)  the steps taken to ensure quality construction, timely 
completion and convergence with other schemes such as Jal 
Jeevan Mission, electricity and LPG connections; 
(d)  whether any special focus has been given to particularly 
vulnerable tribal groups (PVTGs), aspirational districts and 
disaster-prone areas; and 
(e)  if so, the details of funds released and utilised under PMAY-G 
during the last two financial years? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): Under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin, a total of 32.47 
lakh houses have been sanctioned and 26.57 lakh houses have been 
completed duringFY 2025-26, inclusive of sanctions issued in 
previous financial years. The State/UT-wise details areprovided at 
Annexure - I. 
  
(b): As on 03.08.2026, against the total target of 4.18 crore houses 
allocated to the States/UTs under PMAY-G, 3.91 crore houses have 
been sanctioned, and 3.12 crore houses have been completed. The 
remaining 79 lakh sanctioned houses are under construction.  
  

Page 2 of 4 
 
(c): Under PMAY-G, the house is constructed by the beneficiary 
himself/herself or under his/her supervision. Further, as per the 
guidelines of PMAY-G, the States/UTs provide the beneficiaries a 
bouquet of options of house designs according to the local climatic 
conditions, using appropriate local material and technology suitable 
to the region of their residence. The State/UT Government can also 
facilitate supply of construction material at competitive rates. The 
Ministry of Rural Development has published a compendium of rural 
housing typologies “PAHAL” which is available on the program 
website of PMAY-G. This can be accessed through AwaasApp. 
Further, to ensure good quality construction of houses under PMAY-
G, the Government of India has rolled out Rural Mason Training (RMT) 
Program with the target to train adequate number of masons for 
house construction in rural areas.  
  
  A number of steps have been taken by the Ministry to ensure 
timely construction of houses in all States/UTs under PMAY-G. These 
include: 
  
(i) Timely allocation of targets to the States/UTs and release of 
adequate funds; 
(ii) Regular review of progress; 
(iii) Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard; 
(iv) Regular Workshops are conducted by the Ministry with the 
States/UTs;  
(v) Rural Mason Training program, etc. 
  
In addition to the unit assistance provided under the scheme, 
PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water 
through convergence with the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Har Ghar 
Nal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and 
Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In 
addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connections 
through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, 
State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan Mantri 
Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
or other relevant schemes. 
  
(d): As per the scheme guidelines, up to 5% of the targets under 
PMAY-G, are reserved for Special Projects. E.g. for Rehabilitation / 
relocation of families whose houses have been completely 
/substantially damaged on account of Natural hazards as categorized 
in the extant National Disaster Management Plan of National Disaster 
Management Authority - Flood, earthquake, fire, etc. 

Page 3 of 4 
 
Further, under PMAY-G, a minimum 60% of the target at the 
national level is earmarked for both Scheduled Caste (SC)/Schedules 
Tribes (ST) households subject to availability of such eligible 
beneficiaries. 
 
Additionally, under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) of Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the provision 
providing pucca houses to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups 
(PVTG) households with basic amenities is one of the interventions 
being implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.  
  
(e): The funds under PMAY-G are allocated to States/UTs, with each 
State/UT treated as a single unit. The distribution of these funds 
among districts is undertaken by the respective State/UT 
Governments. Over the last two financial years, expenditure under 
Special Projects stood at ₹528.04 crore, while Aspirational Districts 
recorded spending of ₹17,281.58 crore, inclusive of both Central and 
State shares. Further, under PM-JANMAN, a Central share of 
₹2,465.38 crore was released for PVTG beneficiaries during FY 2024-
25 and FY 2025-26, against which a total expenditure of ₹6,329.06 
crore was incurred, comprising contributions from both the Centre 
and the States.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details regarding coordination and collaboration efforts spearheaded by the Union 
Government to facilitate adoption of reforms in agricultural marketing; 
(b) the details regarding the current status of implementation of these reforms, in the country, 
state-wise; 
(c) the details regarding issues reported or faced by State Governments in implementing such 
reforms and the measures taken to address the same; and 
(d) the details of the Private and public investment made till date to strengthen agricultural 
marketing in the country, State/UT-wise and year-wise for the past five years? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
 
(a) to (d):  Agricultural marketing is a State subject. The State Governments undertake 
developmental policy measures for Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) in 
accordance with their respective Acts and Rules. The Department of Agriculture & Farmers 
Welfare supports the states through a mix of digital integration as well as infrastructure funding 
and supplements the efforts of the States through appropriate policy initiatives, budgetary 
support and schemes/programmes. So far, Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) 
in 23 States and 4 UTs are integrated on the e-NAM platform. 1.89 crore Farmers and 2.78 lakh 
Traders are registered on e-NAM and cumulative trade of 13.44 crore MT of various agricultural 
commodities with value of Rs.4,91,160.71 crore has been conducted.  
The APMCs are governed by Acts of the respective State Governments. As per local 
conditions various reforms such as establishment of private markets, promotion of direct 
marketing, declaration of warehouses/silos/cold storages as deemed market yards, single-point 
levy of market fee, deregulation of fruits & vegetable markets, rationalization of market fee and 
commission charges etc. are adopted by the States.  
Details of private & public investment in agri marketing are not maintained centrally. 
However, government schemes like Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) & Agricultural 
Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) have supported APMCs to attract capital investment.  Under AIF, 
support has been provided for marketing infrastructure in terms of interest subvention for 18893 
warehouses, 3110 Cold Stores and Cold Chain projects as well as 2105 integrated primary and 
secondary processing units. For 50,249 storage projects, subsidy amounting Rs.4,849.20 crore 
has been released under AMI. Further, 25081 ‘Other than storage infrastructure’ projects have 
also been supported with subsidy release of Rs.2,191.82 crore under AMI.

INCORRECT DEMARCATION OF LAND 
 
  
†3777. SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA: 
MS IQRA CHOUDHARY: 
MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:  
(a) whether there has been an increase in family disputes and litigation due to wrong demarcation 
of 'abadi land' during drone survey under SVAMITVA in many districts of Uttar Pradesh, if so, 
the details thereof; district-wise including Jaunpur and Etah-Kasganj Lok Sabha Constituency;  
(b) whether out of more than 2.75 crore property cards distributed nationally, data is available on 
those cards which banks have refused to accept as collateral on technical grounds and number of 
cases among these where Bank have not accepted the property cards and the reason therefor, 
State-wise including UP and Jaunpur and Etah-Kasganj Lok Sabha Constituency;  
(c) whether the reliability of digital data remains doubtful due to the huge gap between revenue 
records and physical possession even after distribution of Gharauni (ownership certificate) in 
Uttar Pradesh and Jaunpur, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) whether the Government is likely to ensure resurvey of drone in areas where local residents 
have complained about lack of transparency and high-handedness of surveyors, if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a)        The main objective of the SVAMITVA Scheme is to provide Record of Rights to 
property owners in rural inhabited areas. Under the Scheme, rural inhabited land is demarcated 
using drone survey and Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) technology to create 
high accuracy maps of abadi areas of villages. These highly accurate maps help reduce property-
related disputes by clearly demarcating property boundaries and creating Record of Rights. 
Furthermore, transparent process of ground verification and dispute resolution ensures that 

2 
 
ownership records are finalized fairly and accurately. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not 
maintain details of family disputes and litigation.  
(b)       As on 5th Aug 2026, nationally, 2.72 Crore property cards have been distributed, out of 
which 1.04 Crore property cards have been distributed in Uttar Pradesh.  In order to enable bank 
loan on property cards, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, D/o Financial Services, State Revenue 
Departments, are collaboratively working to enable acceptability of property cards for bank 
loans. The State Governments are using the forum of State Level Bankers Committee to 
streamline their efforts on this subject. As on date, as per information available with the ministry, 
11,147 loans worth Rs 1,713 Crore have been disbursed based on SVAMITVA property cards 
(State wise details at Annexure-I). The Ministry does not maintain number of cases among these 
where banks have not accepted the property cards as collateral for loans.  
(c)       Under the SVAMITVA Scheme, drone survey and preparation of Property Cards are 
undertaken by the State Government with the technical support of the Survey of India. Draft 
maps are published by State Government for raising claims/objections as per State Revenue 
Acts. The reliability of SVAMITVA digital data and the Property Cards is ensured through 
accurate drone survey, robust ground verification process and an effective public scrutiny as well 
as resolution of objections by the competent authorities of the State Government before 
finalisation of ownership records.  
d) The SVAMITVA Scheme provides for a transparent mechanism of survey, ground 
verification and disposal of objections before finalisation of Property Cards. In cases where 
genuine technical issues or survey deficiencies are identified by the competent authorities, 
corrective measures, including re-flying of drones, are undertaken as required.

3778. SHRI JAI PARKASH 
 SHRI SATPAL BRAHAMCHARI 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any special scheme or incentive programme is being implemented by the 
Government to promote crop diversification with the objective of water conservation, 
raising the incomer of farmers and promoting sustainable farming in Haryana, particularly 
in Sonipat and Hisar Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the number of farmers benefitted, 
funds allocated and the alternate crops included thereof during the last three years; 
(b) the steps taken to provide financial assistance, training, marketing facilities and 
technical support to farmers under the crop diversification; 
(c) whether the Government has any official data of suicides committed by farmers due to 
reasons related to agricultural loans or indebtedness in Haryana during the last three 
years and if so, the year-wise and district-wise details thereof; 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to prevent said incidents and to provide debt relief, 
availability of institutional credit, crop insurance and psycho-social support to farmers; and 
(e) the details of the impact of these schemes in the Sonipat Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is promoting 
diversification in Haryana through the Crop Diversification Programme (CDP) under 
Pradhan Mantri - Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY), since 2013-14 to divert the 
area from water intensive paddy cultivation to alternative crops such as shree anna, 
pulses, oilseeds, coarse cereals etc. Ten districts in Haryana namely Ambala, Yamuna 
Nagar, Karnal, Kaithal, Jind, Fatehabad, Sirsa, Panipat, Kurukshetra and Sonipat are 
covered under CDP. A Central Share of Rs. 5204 lakhs has been allocated to the State of 
Haryana under CDP in the last three years. CDP being a centrally sponsored scheme is 
implemented by the concerned states covered under the programme and district wise 
beneficiary details are maintained by the state. The state has included Maize, Moong, Urd 
and Arhar as alternate crops for paddy in their annual action plans 
   Under CDP, assistance is provided for alternative crop demonstrations, farm 
mechanization & value addition, site-specific interventions and contingency activities 
related to awareness generation & capacity building. 
   In addition to the above, The Government of India is encouraging crop 
diversification among the farmers through the state governments to grow crops such as 
coarse cereals, Shree Anna (millets) under the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission 

(NFSNM), Pulses under Mission for Atmanirbharata in Pulses, oilseeds under the National 
Mission on Edible Oil (NMEO-OS) and horticultural crops under the Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH). The State Government of Haryana has informed that 
in addition to various other interventions, the state is also implementing its scheme ‘Mera 
Pani Meri Virasat’ (MPMV) to provide incentives and bonuses to farmers for crop 
diversification. 
(c) to (e): The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) under the Ministry of Home Affairs 
compiles and disseminates information on suicides in its publication titled ‘Accidental 
Deaths and Suicides in India’ (ADSI). The report upto 2024 is available on NCRB website 
(https://ncrb.gov.in). 
   The Government has introduced yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to farmers suffering crop 
loss/damage arising out of natural calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize 
the income of farmers etc. This scheme is voluntary for State/UTs as well as farmers. 
Further, it is State Government’s prerogative to notify districts and crops for 
implementation, as per the provisions of PMFBY. The scheme is being implemented in 25 
States/UTs. All willing farmers are eligible to enroll under the scheme.  
   Agriculture is a State Subject. However,  the Government of India is supplementing 
the states through a comprehensive range of Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes and programmes aimed at increasing farmers’ income across all States/UTs 
including Haryana, encompassing  entire spectrum of agriculture, including credit, 
insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops (including horticulture), seeds, 
mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, 
extension, procurement of crops from farmers and digital agriculture.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
  
Implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 
  
 †3779. Shri Ramesh Awasthi: 
            Shri Ananta Nayak: 
            Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor: 
            Shri Mahendra Singh Solanky: 
            Shri Chavda Vinod Lakhamshi: 
            Shri Kanwar Singh Tanwar: 
            Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of measures taken by the Union Government to ensure effective implementation of 
the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 in the country, State and district-wise 
including Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Kachchh district, Dewas– Shajapur, Dahod and 
Keonjhar Lok Sabha Constituencies; 
(b) the details regarding the number of States and Union Territories including that have notified 
rules and established monitoring mechanisms under the RPwD Act along with the status of 
implementation, State and district-wise including the said Constituencies; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding accessibility, employment, 
education and social inclusion for Persons with Disabilities under this Act in the country, State 
and district-wise including such Constituencies; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof, including the key findings, corrective measures taken and funds 
released for improving disability-friendly infrastructure and services during the last three years, 
State and district-wise including such Constituencies?  
  
 

ANSWER 
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment 
(SHRI B L VERMA) 
(a) The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 has been enacted which inter alia, 
provides for equality and non-discrimination, accessibility, inclusive education, skill 
development, social security and participation in society. To facilitate effective implementation 
of the Act, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) implements 
various schemes and initiatives across the country, like Assistance to Persons with Disabilities 
for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP) Scheme, Scholarships for Students with 
Disabilities scheme, Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS). Further, under the 
Scheme for Creation of Barrier Free Environment (CBFE), financial assistance is provided to 
State/UT Governments for creation of barrier-free environment in existing Government buildings 
and establishments. The Department is also implementing the Unique Disability ID (UDID) 
Project to create a homogeneous database. 
(b)  As per the available records in the Department, all the States and Union Territories have 
notified the rules. 
(c)-(d) The Department undertakes periodic assessments and monitoring of its schemes and 
initiatives for persons with disabilities. A third-party evaluation of the ADIP Scheme has been 
conducted. The evaluation has also been done for Pradhan Mantri Divyasha-Vayoshri Kendras 
(PMD-VKs). Further, a third-party evaluation of the Scholarships for Students with Disabilities 
Scheme conducted for continuation of the Scheme found it to be effective in improving the lives 
of students with disabilities and enhancing their employability. Based on the findings of the 
above assessments and evaluations, the Department has taken various measures to strengthen 
implementation of its schemes and improve service delivery. To facilitate implementation of the 
accessibility provisions of the RPwD Act, 2016, the Department has notified Harmonised 
Guidelines prescribing universal design standards for the built environment and digital 
accessibility. Further, to support accessibility audits, the Department has empaneled 60 access 
auditors for the built environment and 16 access auditors for web accessibility, whose services 
can be availed by the appropriate Governments and other authorities.
