GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3781 
ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
  
PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS 
  
†3781. SHRI UTKARSH VERMA MADHUR: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the steps taken by the Government to financially empower and make Panchayati 
Raj Institutions self-reliant in the country during the last three years, along with the State and 
district-wise; 
  
(b) whether the Government has any time-bound plan to establish Panchayat Secretariats for 
enhancing administrative efficiency in the Gram Panchayats of the country and to ensure 100 
percent broadband internet connectivity there, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(c) whether any additional or special budgetary provision has been made for the development of 
infrastructure of Gram Panchayats in affected areas in various States, including Uttar Pradesh 
and if so, the State and district-wise details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
  
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) to (c) “Panchayat”, being a “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of the State List 
of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operated through 
the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts, which may vary from State to State, subject to the 
provisions of the Constitution of India. As per Article 243H of the Constitution, legislature of the 
State may, by law, authorize a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls 
and fees in accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits and assign to the 
Panchayats such taxes, duties, tolls and fees levied and collected by the State Government for 
such purposes and subject to such conditions and limits as may be specified in the law. 
  
However, Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides the basis for the Central Finance 
Commissions to assess the status of finances of the Union, States and their respective local 
bodies and recommend sharing of taxes as well as grants for various purposes to the States and 
Local Bodies. The Finance Commission grant can be used by Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) for 
location-specific felt needs under 29 subjects enshrined in the Eleventh Schedule of the 
Constitution, except for salary or other establishment expenditures. Central Finance Commission 
grants for Rural Local Bodies in the States have continuously increased. Under the 14th Finance 

2 
 
Commission (FY 2015-16), the allocation stood at ₹2,00,29.20 crore, whereas under the 16th 
Finance Commission (FY 2026-31), the allocation has been enhanced to ₹4,35,236 crore — 
representing nearly a two-fold increase over the 14th Finance Commission. 
  
However, the Government has taken significant steps to enhance the revenue-generating 
capabilities of Panchayats in the entire country including Uttar Pradesh, enabling them to 
become self-reliant and less dependent on external funding.  
  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad, has developed a training 
module on Own Source Revenue (OSR) to strengthen the financial self-reliance of Gram 
Panchayats. The module helps elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries understand 
how OSR is generated through tax and non-tax sources. As on 10.07.2026, under the Rashtriya 
Gram SwarajAbhiyan (RGSA), a total of 2,75,893 participants have been trained through the 
Specialised Module on Own Source Revenue (OSR).  
  
In 2025, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award 
(ANPSA) to promote Atmanirbharta through the augmentation of Own Source Revenue (OSR) 
by Panchayats. 
  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) has also developed the 'SAMARTH Panchayat portal', a 
dedicated digital platform that facilitates the generation of tax & non-tax demands and collection 
thereof, maintenance of tax registers, and online tracking of revenue. 
  
With a view to support States and Union Territories in strengthening their legal and institutional 
framework for Own Source Revenue, the Ministry has formulated the Model Own Source 
Revenue Rules as a guiding framework for consideration by the States/Union Territories. These 
Model Rules are advisory in nature and are intended to serve as a reference for strengthening the 
Own Source Revenue framework of Panchayats. States and Union Territories may adopt, adapt 
or modify these Model Rules, either in full or in part, as considered appropriate, keeping in view 
their existing legal provisions, administrative arrangements and local requirements. 
  
The implementation of the SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with 
Improvised Technology in Village Areas) Scheme, launched in April, 2020, lays a robust 
foundation for the growth of property taxes in rural areas, ultimately leading to enhanced OSR 
generation and improved financial self-sufficiency for RLBs. 
  
Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the 
Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj is 
implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan 
(RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The main objective of the scheme is to 
strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected 
Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other stakeholders to develop their 
governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram Panchayats and Local bodies to 
function effectively across all States/UTs. Apart from different trainings, the Scheme also 
supports for the Panchayat infrastructure like Gram Panchayat Bhawan to the States/ UTs on 

3 
 
limited scale for effective functioning of Panchayats. Under the scheme, 6,536 Gram Panchayat 
Bhawans have been constructed in different States/UTs during 2022-23 to 2025-26.  
  
The provision of last-mile digital connectivity to Gram Panchayats under the BharatNet 
programme is being implemented by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to provide 
broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats. As per the information available on the 
BharatNet UNMS Dashboard, under the BharatNet Project, more than 2.21 lakh Gram 
Panchayats across the country have been made service-ready. Further, network upgradation and 
expansion are being undertaken under the Amended BharatNet Programme.

 कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) Yes. Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is implementing 
National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM) a Central Sector Scheme through National 
Bee Board (NBB). The objectives of NBHM are to promote scientific beekeeping for holistic 

growth of beekeeping industry, increasing production of honey and beehive products, income 
& employment generation, providing livelihood support to farm and non-farm households, 
women empowerment through beekeeping, to strengthen beekeepers by developing 
institutional framework through collective approach and to enhance agriculture/ horticulture 
production. Under the scheme project based assistance is provided to eligible Implementing 
Agencies (IAs) for various activities. These include setting up of Integrated Beekeeping 
Development Centers, honey testing labs, bee disease diagnostic labs, Quality Nucleus Stock 
Development Centre, capacity building, technology demonstration, empowerment of women 
through beekeeping etc. NBHM also supports marketing, branding, value addition and 
Research & Development.

under the Mission during the last three years, State-wise including Assam and for Telangana

stakeholders to increase honey production, promote scientific beekeeping, enhancing 
agricultural productivity and farmers income through project based approach, as per 
provisions of NBHM. So far 7 world class honey testing labs, 66 mini labs to check adulteration, 
83 honey processing units and 90 collection, branding & packaging units have been 
established. These support efficient storage and marketing. 81 Quality Nucleus Stock 
Development Centres have been supported for producing quality queen bees and colony 
multiplication so far.  
(d) 24,94,101 bee colonies have been registered by 16,788 beekeepers on Madukranti 
Portal. These include 8,275 registered bee colonies by 65 beekeepers from Telangana. State 
/UT wise information is given at Annexure-I. 
(e) Total number of projects sanctioned,  funds sanctioned and utilized under NBHM State/ 
UT wise is given at Annexure-II. 

(f) NBHM has transformed the largely unorganized beekeeping sector into a technology-
driven, market-oriented industry, enhancing income of small and marginal farmers/ 
beekeepers. Honey production increased from 80,530 MT in 2014–15 to 1,51,690 MT in 2025–
26 (as per Horticulture Crops Statistics, 2nd Advance Estimates 2025–26). During the same 
period, honey exports increased from 29,600 MT in 2014–15 to 114,570.19 MT in 2025–26, 
making India the world's second-largest exporter of natural honey. 
(g) As reported by State government of Assam no project has been sanctioned in Karbi

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3785 
ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
 
STATUS OF REVIVAL OF HMT UNIT AT KALAMASSERY 
 
3785. SHRI HIBI EDEN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has taken any concrete steps to revive HMT Ltd., Kalamassery, Kerala;  
 
(b) whether HMT is facing a severe shortage of working capital;  
 
(c) whether the Government is aware that HMT is losing tenders under the Small-Scale Industry (SSI) 
preference clause, despite being a competitive Central PSU;  
 
(d) whether the Government has any plan to protect HMT’s land assets in Kalamassery and use them 
for new industrial or employment-generating projects in Kerala;  
 
(e) whether the expansion plans include introducing new manufacturing technologies or product lines 
in the Kalamassery unit; and  
 
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): HMT Limited (HMTL) is the holding company of HMT Group of Companies.  It has two 
Manufacturing Units, Food Processing Machinery Unit, Aurangabad and Auxiliary Business Division, 
Bengaluru. HMT Limited does not have manufacturing Unit at Kalamassery, Kerala , however, one 
of its two subsidiaries, namely HMT Machine Tools Limited has an operational manufacturing unit 
at Kalamassery, Kerala.  
 
(b)&(c): Yes. On account of old plant and machinery, poor productivity, etc., the net  
worth of HMT Machine Tools Limited has got eroded over the years and is facing severe financial 
crisis. 
 
(d): The Government has designated appropriate employee(s) of the HMT Ltd and its subsidiaries 
as Estate Officers vide Statutory Order 222 dated 14.01.2011 under the Public Premises (Eviction of 
Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971. 
 
(e) & (f): HMT Machine Tools Limited, which has several units, including the Kalamassery 
unit, being a CPSE registered under the Companies Act, operates as per the provisions of the 
Companies Act and the guidelines issued by the Government of India in respect of CPSEs and takes 
its appropriate investment decisions as per its operational requirements.

3786.  ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री

(a) the details of the number of upgraded looms distributed, worksheds constructed and lighting 
units installed under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) which are currently

उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a): Under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) need based financial support 
is provided for various interventions like upgraded looms & accessories, construction of 
worksheds, lighting units, product & design development etc. State/UT -wise details of upgraded 
looms & accessories, worksheds constructed, lighting units provided under NHDP across the 
country during last three years are at Annexure-A.  
  
(b): The Government promotes the formation and strengthening of Handloom Producer 
Companies (HPCs) as a key institutional mechanism for organizing handloom weavers into 
professionally managed, member -owned enterprises. 237 Handloom Producer Companies are 
formed under NHDP during 2020-21 to 2025-26.  
  
(c) & (d): Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme is a component of National Handloom 
Development Programme (NHDP) to provide adequate and timely assistance from the 
Banks/financial institutions to the handloom sector to meet their credit requirement for term loan 
& working capital in a flexible and cost -effective manner across the country. Margin money 

assistance is provided @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of Rs.25,000/ - to individual 
handloom weaver/weav er entrepreneur and @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of 
Rs.20.00 lakh (@ Rs.2.00 lakh for every 100 weaver/worker) to handloom organization. 
However, only handloom organizations are eligible for getting loans at concessional interest rate 
of 6% for a period of 3 years subject to interest subvention capped upto 7% by the GoI. Credit 
guarantee fee on loan to handloom organization only is also provided for a period of 3 years.  
  
For timely disbursal of financial assistances i.e. Margin money, Interest Subsidy and Credit 
Guarantee Fee by participating banks, a centralized online claim disbursement system 
“Handloom Weaver Mudra Portal” has been developed in association with Punjab National 
Bank. Margin money is transferred directly to the loan account of beneficiaries and interest 
subsidy is transferred directly to concerned banks through the Portal.  
  
For availing loan under the scheme, eligible handloom weaver/worker is required to approach 
participating bank concerned with the filled -up application and  submit it in the bank with 
necessary documents. It is for the bank concerned to satisfy itself with the eligibility of the 
applicant for grant of loan to the beneficiary. State -wise number of loan and amount of loan 
sanctioned under Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme under NHDP during 2021-22 to

ASSESSMENT OF IMPACT OF PM-KISAN 
 
3787. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA: 
SHRI RAHUL KASWAN: 
SMT. SANJNA JATAV: 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any independent or institutional evaluation 
to assess the impact of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Scheme on farmers' 
income, agricultural investment, productivity and cost of cultivation particularly in 
Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency during the last three years;  
(b) if so, the major findings thereof;  
(c) the details of the farmers benefited, beneficiaries declared ineligible, Aadhaar and 
land records verification and cases pending particularly in the said Constituency under 
the Scheme, State-wise;  
(d) whether the Government has conducted any analysis particularly with regard to the 
actual role of the Scheme in enhancing the income and agricultural investment of small 
and marginal farmers;  
(e) if so, the major findings thereof;  
(f) whether the Government proposes to take measures such as regular updation of 
land records, eligibility verification, artificial intelligence-based risk analysis, time-
bound grievance redressal and periodic re-verification of beneficiaries to make the 
Scheme more effective and better targeted; and  
(g) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): An independent impact evaluation study of the PM-KISAN Scheme has 
been conducted by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) of NITI 
Aayog in the country, including in Rajasthan. The study suggested that the scheme is 
successfully fulfilling its primary function of providing direct financial assistance to 
farmers holding agricultural land, thereby enhancing their economic stability and 
agricultural productivity. The study also shows that over 92 percent of beneficiary 
farmers utilized the financial assistance for essential agricultural inputs such as seeds, 
fertilizers, and pesticides, which are particularly important in the face of rising input 
costs and weather-related uncertainties. It further found that around 85 percent of 
beneficiaries reported an increase in agricultural income. 

  
The evaluation also observed that PM-KISAN has contributed to reducing the 
financial distress of farmers, lowering their dependence on informal credit, and 
improving their socio-economic well-being. The study further found that beneficiaries 
who utilised the assistance primarily for agricultural purposes reported significantly 
higher agricultural incomes, particularly among small and marginal farmers, 
highlighting the Scheme's role in strengthening agricultural productivity, enhancing 
financial resilience, and supporting sustainable rural livelihoods. 
 
 Under the PM-KISAN Scheme, the funds are released through DBT directly into 
the Aadhaar seeded bank accounts of the beneficiaries. The States/UTs verify and 
approve the beneficiaries after validating their data. The validation and checks of land 
seeding, Aadhaar linking with bank accounts and eKYC of the applicants have been 
made mandatory over the period to make the service delivery more efficient and 
transparent. The fulfilment of mandatory requirements by farmers and their validations 
is an essential condition to qualify as beneficiary and receive the benefits under the 
scheme.  
The details of beneficiaries benefitted in Alwar, Bharatpur, and Deeg districts of 
Rajasthan and amount released to them in 23rd instalment is as follows:

The state-wise details of beneficiaries benefitted under 23rd instalment and 
amount released to them is at Annexure. 
 
(f) & (g): Linking of land records of beneficiaries, eligibility verification, time-bound 
grievance redressal, and periodic re-verification of beneficiaries through eKYC is a 
routine process under PM-KISAN Scheme. These are assessed, reviewed, and 
monitored regularly through the State review meetings. 
Further, the Government of India undertakes saturation drives in coordination 
with the States/UTs. A major nationwide saturation drive was undertaken from 15th 
November 2023 under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra (VBSY), during which, more 
than 1.0 Cr. farmers were included under PM-KISAN. Further, under the Government’s 
100 days initiative in 2024, over 25 lakh eligible farmers were added under the PM-
KISAN scheme. A special drive was also conducted in September 2024 to clear the 
pending self-registration cases, which resulted in the addition of over 30 lakh new 
farmers. A nationwide saturation drive has also been undertaken from 1st June, 2026 
under PM-KISAN alongwith the “Khet Bachao Abhiyaan” to expand the coverage of 
eligible farmers under the scheme which resulted in the addition of about 17 lakh new 
farmers under PM-KISAN. In addition, States/UTs also undertake saturation drives 
from time to time to identify and facilitate the enrolment of eligible farmers completing 
all mandatory conditions under the Scheme.

GI TAGGED JARDALU MANGOES  
  
3788. SHRI AJAY KUMAR MANDAL:  
  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्री) be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the export of Jardalu mangoes (GI 
 tagged) from Bhagalpur in Bihar has been adversely affected by weather 
 uncertainties, global restrictions logistics costs;  
(b) whether unseasonal h eat and rainfall have led to crop losses and a decline in 
 exportable surplus;  
(c) the challenges associated with phytosanitary norms, quarantine regulations 
 and pesticide residue limits in Gulf and European countries;  
(d) whether farmers are impacted by high air  freight rates and a local shortage of 
 Vapor Heat Treatment or cold chain infrastructure and if so, the details of 
 corrective steps taken in this regard; and  
(e) the concrete steps taken by APEDA towards export promotion, exploration of 
 new markets, infrast ructure development and provision of financial subsidies?  
 
ANSWER 
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a) & (b) The Government has not received any official input regarding the export of 
Jardalu mangoes (GI tagged) from Bhagalpur in Bihar being adversely affected by 
weather uncertainties, global restrictions logistics costs and regarding unseasonal heat 
and rainfall having led to crop losses and a decline in exportable surplus of Jardalu 
Mangoes. 
 
(c) to (e) To comply with the phyto -sanitary norms and quarantine regulations for 
mitigating the pest risks associated with fruits such as mangoes, treatment protocols  
such as Vapour Heat Treatment (VHT), irradiation and Hot Water Treatment (HWT) are 
being followed as per agreed protocol with the importing country. 
  
Vapour Heat Treatment (VHT) is not a mandatory prerequisite for export of mangoes to 
all destinations. A t present, Jardalu mangoes are being exported to the Gulf 
Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, wherein compliance is confined to general 
phytosanitary measures, therefore, supplementary mitigation measures such as VHT 

2 
 
or Hot Water Treatment (HWT) are not required for regulatory adherence for exports to 
these markets.  
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) has 
not received any non -compliance notification related to Jardalu mangoes, from the 
European Union or the Gulf Countries, on Pesticide residue limits. 
  
The Airports Authority of India Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Company Limited 
(AAICLAS) is facilitating the movement of domestic air cargo at Patna, through its newly 
constructed Domestic Air Cargo Terminal al ong with a Cold Storage Facility at Patna 
Airport, operational w.e.f. 25.02.2025, having an annual cargo handling capacity of 
21,900 MT. 
  
The Department of Commerce through the Agricultural and Processed Food Products 
Export Development Authority (APEDA) provides financial support to stakeholders 
across the country, including Bhagalpur, for export promotion of its Scheduled products, 
including mangoes, through its Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), under three 
components viz., Development of Export Infrast ructure, Quality Development and 
Market Development, which works towards strengthen export compliance infrastructure, 
enables market access, and facilitates expansion of exports to new destinations. 
  
Specifically, for the export promotion of Jardalu Mango es, APEDA has taken the 
following initiatives, in coordination with the Government of Bihar such as display and 
promotion of Jardalu mangoes in overseas markets and mango -promotion events, 
training and capacity building of farmers and exporters, trial and commercial export 
consignments of GI-tagged Jardalu mangoes to international destinations including the 
UK and Middle Eastern markets in 2026.

3789.    SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the financial assistance provided under the e-NAM scheme for the 
development of infrastructure such as the establishment of digital platforms, 
weighbridges and quality testing facilities in Maharashtra; 
(b)  the steps taken to ensure that farmers in Maharashtra, particularly in rural and remote 
areas, are able to utilize e-NAM services to sell their produce and realize remunerative 
prices; 
(c)  the impact of the e-NAM scheme on improving market linkages, price discovery and 
transparency in agricultural markets in Maharashtra, particularly for small and marginal 
farmers; and 
(d)  the plan to bring more commodities under the ambit of e-NAM particularly in 
Maharashtra in the near future? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
(a):  Under the National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) Scheme, one-time financial 
assistance of up to ₹30 lakh per eligible Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) 
mandi is provided for creation and upgradation of e-NAM infrastructure, including 
hardware, internet connectivity, electronic weighbridges, assaying (quality testing) 
equipment and other related facilities. Additionally, one time grant @Rs.40 lakhs and 
Rs.5 lakhs for “A” and “B” class mandis as decided by SLSC is provided respectively for 
cleaning, grading and packaging & related infrastructure facilities and compost unit.    
In Maharashtra, so far 181 APMC mandis have been integrated with e-NAM for 
which an amount of ₹50.48 crore has been released.   
  

(b) & (c):  Integration of Mandis with e-NAM portal is done based on the proposal received 
from State Governments. As per the information received from State of Maharashtra, to 
facilitate utilization of e-NAM by farmers in the State, including those in rural and remote 
areas, several steps have been taken. These include capacity-building programmes for 
farmers, traders, commission agents and mandi officials on e-NAM operations, 
awareness building in gramsabhas, workshops, seminars and monthly magazines etc.  
In the state of Maharashtra, 13,02,006 farmers and 23,844 traders have been 
onboarded on eNAM. So far, 62.28 lakh MT of various agricultural commodities have 
been traded through e-NAM portal worth Rs.23,156.38 crores since inception. The State 
has also reported intermandi trade of 34,700 MT & inter State trade of 15,100 MT. e-
Payments of Rs.541.98 cr. have been reported. These three indicators show improved 
market linkages & transparent pricing for farmers, including small & marginal. 
 NITI Aayog carried out evaluation of various Central and Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes including e-NAM Scheme in the country including State of Maharashtra in 
2020. The evaluation highlighted the potential of e-NAM in promoting transparent 
markets, efficient price discovery, better contract negotiations and improved access to 
institutional finance.   
(d): The e-NAM platform facilitates trading in agricultural commodities notified by the 
respective State Governments under the relevant APMC Acts and Rules. Additional 
commodities are onboarded based on proposals received from the concerned State 
Government/APMCs, subject to availability of assaying protocols, market readiness and 
compliance with the Scheme guidelines. So far, tradable parameters for 247 commodities 
are available for online trading through e-NAM platform in the country including 
Maharashtra.

3792.  SHRI MANI A: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has identified Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu for 
the establishment of large -scale, labour -intensive industries to generate 
employment and reduce migration of youth to other States, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  whether any proposals have been received for setting up of industrial parks, 
manufacturing clusters or MSME-based industrial estates in Dharmapuri during 
the last three years, if so, the present status thereof; 
 
(c)  the incentives proposed by the Government to attract investments in sectors 
such as  textiles, food processing, leather, renewable energy, electronics 
assembly and agro-based industries in the district; 
 
(d)  the e stimated employment likely to be generated through such industrial 
projects, particularly for local youth and women; and 
 
(e)  the measures being taken by the Government to promote balanced regional 
industrial development and reduce unemployment and distress migration from 
Dharmapuri district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (e): Industry is primarily a State subject. States adopt diﬀerent policy measures to 
promote industrial development. The Government of India supplements the 
eﬀorts of the State Governments through a number of policies  and schemes. 
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) supports 
the overall development of industrial sector through schemes  such as 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, National Industrial Corridor 
Development Programme, Startup India, Footw ear, Leather & Accessories 
Development Programme and Initiative for Promotion of Geographical 
Indication and undertakes measures for Ease of Doing Business. 

 
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA) Scheme has been notified on 
10.04.2026 for development o f investment -ready industrial parks to enable 
investors to ground investment with ease, thereby adding to the manufacturing 
capacity in the country. Under the Scheme, financial assistance is to be 
provided for development of 100 industrial parks. In the first phase, 50 projects 
are to be taken up, with one or more rounds of selection. Government of Tamil 
Nadu has submitted seven project proposals in Round 1, including one in 
Dharmapuri district. 
Under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme ( NICDP), two 
projects were identified for development in the State of Tamil Nadu as part of 
the Industrial Corridor Programme namely, Dharmapuri–Salem Node under the 
Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor Extension (CBIC -Extension) and 
Ponneri Node under the  Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC). The 
State Government conveyed that the proposed sites would be taken up for 
development by the State. Further, no alternate land parcels have been 
identified or communicated by the State Government under the NICDP. 
The Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that Dharmapuri district has been 
identified for industrial development through the establishment of SIPCOT  
Industrial Park, Dharmapuri  in an area of 1733.40 acre, with the objective of 
promoting balanced regional industrial development, attracting large -scale 
investments, generating employment opportunities for local youth and reducing 
migration to other States. The park has an estimated  employment potential of 
18,300 persons during the operational phase, comprising 16,470 direct  
employment and 1,830 indirect employment. Till date, 11 industries have been 
allotted a total extent of 48.96 acres in SIPCOT Industrial Park, Dharmapuri, 
with a committed direct employment potential of 575 persons. 
The Government of Tamil Nadu has also accorded administrative sanction 
for acquisition of land for formation of SIPCOT Adhagapadi Industrial Park, 
Phase – II in the district. 
Further, the State has classified Dharmapuri District as a “C” Category District 
for the purpose of industrial incentives. To attract investments in sectors such 
as textiles, food processing, leather, renewable energy, electronics assembly, 
agro-based industries and other eligible manufacturing activities, a front-ended 
Land Cost Incentive of 50% of the plot cost is available for eligible industries 
that are allotted land in SIPCOT Industrial Parks.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3794 
ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS 
 
3794. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of licensed/registered slaughter houses, including modern/mechanised  abattoirs 
conforming to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001 in the country, 
State-wise;  
(b) whether the Government estimates the number of unlicensed or unregulated slaughter  houses 
operating in the country and, if so, the details thereof, State-wise;   
(c) whether any data have been maintained by the Government on livestock slaughtered in licensed 
and unlicensed premises in the country, if so, the details and figures during the last three years;   
(d) the deployment of veterinary officers for mandatory inspections and instances of slaughter without 
inspection or of diseased, unfit or pregnant animals in the country, State-wise;   
(e) the Central assistance released for establishment/modernisation of slaughter houses during the said 
period; and   
(f) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen disease surveillance, enforce humane 
slaughter and waste-management norms, curb illegal slaughter and inter-State transport of animals, 
and the timeline therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) & (b) The State wise number of registered/unregistered slaughter houses as per 20th Livestock census 
2019: All India Report is annexed (Annexure-I).  
(c) The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD) does not estimate data on livestock 
slaughtered in licensed or unlicensed premises in the country separately. However, as per 20th Livestock 
Census, 2019: All India Report , the State-wise estimates of number of cattle, sheep, goat, pig & poultry 
slaughtered for meat production during 2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25 is annexed (Annexure-II). 
 
(d)  The deployment of veterinary officers and State-wise information regarding slaughter witho ut 
veterinary inspection or slaughter of diseased, unfit or pregnant animals are maintained by the concerned 
State Governments/UT Administrations and Local Authorities and are not maintained by the DAHD.  
(e) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has not released any 
financial assistance for establishment or modernization of slaughter houses during the last three years. 

(f) The Government has taken several measures to strengthen disease surveillance, promote humane 
slaughter practices, regulate animal transport and prevent illegal slaughter. These include: 
(i) Disease Surveillance:  Government of India (GoI) has strengthened surveillance of animal diseases 
by adopting the following measures: 
 Financial support provided to Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL) Indian 
Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Bareilly, five Regional Disease Diagnostic 
Laboratories (RDDLs) of States for strengthening disease surveillance and other activities.  
 Financial assistance provided to Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Institutes 
namely National Institute of Foot and Mouth Disease (NIFMD) Indian Veterinary Research 
Institute (IVRI) Bengaluru, IVRI Bareilly and National Institute on Veterinary Epidemiology 
and Disease Informatics (NIVEDI) Bengaluru for carrying out animal disease surveillance 
and other related activities. 
 ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal undertakes 
surveillance of emerging and exotic trans-boundary animal diseases through laboratory-based 
surveillance.  
 Financial assistance provided to states for training and awareness on Good Animal Husbandry 
Practices, Biosecurity/Sanitary measures, vaccination against animal diseases, disease 
surveillance and monitoring and capacity building.  
 To strengthen the early warning system, ICAR -NIVEDI has developed National Animal 
Disease Referral Expert System (NADRES) 2.0 which provides district -level forecasts of 
potential animal disease risks around two months in advance. 
 Bharat Pashudhan portal has been developed for various activities including surveillance of 
livestock diseases. 
 ICAR has strengthened the surveillance for livestock diseases through the National Animal 
Disease Epidemiology Network (NADEN). 
(ii) Humane Slaughter: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001, notified 
under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, prescribe standards for slaughter houses and humane 
slaughter of animals. Pursuant to the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Writ Petition 
(Civil) No. 330 of 2001, Common Cause Vs Union of India & Others, the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest & Climate Change had issued a Compendium of Rules and Regulations relating to slaughter  
houses to facilitate compliance with the applicable statutory provisions. The Animal Welfare Board 
of India issues advisories from time to time. 
(iii) Waste Management: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Ministry of Environment, Forest 
and Climate Change has also notified discharge standards for slaughter houses, meat processing units 
and seafood industry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The Slaughter houses are required 
to comply the discharge standards and consent conditions stipulated in Consent to Establish and 
Consent to Operate issued by State Pollution Control Boards/Pollution Control Committees. CPCB 
also issued directions on 13.01.2022 under Section 18(1)(b) of the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 
1981 for installation of rendering plants by slaughterhouses. 
(iv) Prevention of Illegal Slaughter and Regulation of Animal Transport: The Transport of Animals 
Rules, 1978, notified under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, prescribe standards for 
transportation of animals to prevent cru elty during transit. Prevention of illegal slaughter and 
enforcement of applicable laws relating to slaughter houses and transport of animals are primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

(c): In addition to the Zaheerabad Industrial Area under National Industrial Corridor

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3796 
ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
POST-HARVEST LOSS AND BYCATCH FROM MARINE FISHERIES 
 
3796. SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the estimated post-harvest loss and bycatch from marine fisheries in coastal Karnataka; 
(b) the projects supported for ice, cold chain, processing and conversion of bycatch into food, 
feed or other products; 
(c) the number of beneficiaries, capacity created and utilisation thereof; and 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to improve value realisation and reduce waste at 
Mangaluru fishing harbour and adjoining centres? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a):  The Department of Fisheries, Government of India  (DoF, GoI) during the year 2023-24 
carried out a comprehensive study through the National Productivity Council of India (NPC), an 
autonomous organization under Ministry of Commerce and Industry to assess post-harvest losses 
in fisheries and aquaculture sector. The study estimated post-harvest loss in marine fisheries in 
Karnataka between 6.21% to 10.13%.  Further, Government of Karnataka has also reported that 
as per the studies done by the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology(CIFT)  the 
estimated post-harvest loss is around 6%. It is also reported by Government of Karnataka that as 
per the studies done by the ICAR -Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) the 
bycatch was reported around 20-40% based on the type of gear and craft used in marine fisheries.     
(b) to (d): The DoF, GoI, under its schemes and policy accords high priory towards strengthening 
cold chain facilities, reduction of bycatch and efficient utilization of fish harvested. The Pradhan 
Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), implemented by the DoF, GoI envisages support 
towards creation and modernization of post-harvest and cold chain infrastructure to reduce post-
harvest losses, improve value realization, enhance shelf life of fishes harvested. The DoF, GoI 
encourages adoptio n of sustainable measures to minimize marine bycatch. Concurrently, 
States/Union Territories (UTs) are also encouraged towards optimal and value-added utilization 

of all harvested resources, thereby reducing post -harvest losses and promoting a circular 
economy in the fisheries sector.  
During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has 
accorded approval to the fisheries development proposal s of Government of Karnataka  with a 
total project cost amounting to ₹ 1053.60 crore. The approved activities inter-alia also included 
cold chain facilities like establishment of Ice plants/c old storages (126 units.), post -harvest 
transportation units (1065 units) which included refrigerated vehicles, insulated vehicles, motor 
cycle with ice boxes, cycle with ice boxes, three wheelers with ice boxes etc.,  live fish vending 
centres (46 units), fish kiosks (100 units), fish retail market (1 unit), matsya vahini mobile eco-
friendly fish kiosks (300 units) and state of art whole sale fish market (1 unit). Under PMMSY, 
identification and selection of beneficiaries are carried out by the respective State Governments. 
The Government of Karnataka has informed that 171 beneficiaries have been supported under 
the cold chain infrastructure component of PMMSY.    
Under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has approved modernization and upgradation of Mangaluru 
Fishing Harbour at project cost of ₹ 37.47 crore which envisages improved berthing facilities, 
modern fish landing and auction infrastructure, hygienic fish handling areas, upgraded water 
supply, sanitation and waste management facilities, and upgraded harbour utilities to minimize 
handling losses and improve fish quali ty. In addition, in the adjoining areas projects namely 
modernization of Gangolli Fishing Harbour (₹ 22.18 crore) and Malpe Fishing Harbour (₹ 12.52 
crore) has also been approved for providing similar facilities. Government of Karnataka has also 
informed that fishermen are encouraged to use Square-mesh cod-end trawl nets (35 mm) to allow 
juveniles to escape, and to install Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets to allow turtles 
to escape; both measures aimed towards conservation and sustainable fisheries.

  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
PENSIONS FOR IGNOAPS 
 
3797. Shri Sunil Bose: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that close to 6 crore elderly 
in India fall in the poorest wealth quintile, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government has any plans to increase the current 
non-contributory pension amount of Rs 200 under the Indira 
Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) to meet 
rising living costs, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure economic security 
for economically vulnerable elderly populations; 
(d)  whether the Government has conducted assessments of the 
adequacy of existing pension amounts to meet the basic needs 
of the elderly, if so, the findings and recommendations thereof; 
and 
(e)  the number of beneficiaries whose pensions have been 
cancelled under IGNOAPS, if so, the details thereof and if not 
the reasons for cancellation? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): As per the population projections based on the Census 
2011, brought out by the Technical Group on Population Projections, 
National Commission on Population, Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare around 11.5 per cent of the country’s population is estimated 
to be aged 60 years and above in 2026.  
 
Under the National Old Age Pension Scheme, a component of 
the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), central 
assistance of ₹200 per month is provided to eligible elderly persons 

Page 2 of 3 
 
aged 60–79 years belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households. 
On attaining the age of 80 years and above, the rate of central 
assistance is enhanced to ₹500 per month per beneficiary. The 
States/Union Territories may supplement the central assistance by 
providing additional financial support from their own resources. At 
present, the top-up assistance provided by the States/UTs ranges 
from ₹50 to ₹3,800 per month per beneficiary under the old age 
pension scheme. Around 5.7 crore beneficiaries are receiving old age 
pension under NSAP and similar State-specific schemes. 
At present, no proposal to revise the rate of assistance under 
NSAP is under consideration of the Government. 
 
(c): Financial assistance in the form of pension is provided to 
eligible elderly beneficiaries under NSAP.  Further, as per information 
received from Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, the 
Department is implementing an umbrella scheme Atal Vayo 
Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) Scheme for the welfare of senior citizens 
as per details given at Annexure. 
 
(d): From time to time, various impact assessment and evaluation 
studies have been carried out to assess the impact of NSAP schemes 
by the Ministry and NITI Aayog. The assessments indicate 
satisfactory implementation at the grassroots level, with most 
beneficiaries expressing overall satisfaction with the processes of 
selection, sanction, and disbursement of pensions. The studies also 
find that pension support has helped beneficiaries meet essential 
expenses such as food, healthcare, etc., thereby reducing their 
dependence on family members for these needs. At the same time, 
they have recommended further strengthening of the programme 
through measures such as improving adequacy of assistance, 
ensuring timely and regular payments, enhancing beneficiary 
verification and monitoring systems etc. 
(e): As per the guidelines of NSAP, the responsibility for 
identification/selection of beneficiaries, verification of applications, 
sanctioning, maintenance/deletion of beneficiary data and last mile 
disbursal of pension to the beneficiaries vests with the respective 
States/UTs. The beneficiary database under NSAP is reviewed and 
updated periodically by the respective States/UTs. Accordingly, 
pension payments may be discontinued and beneficiary records may 
be modified or deleted on account of reasons such as death, 
migration, duplication, non-traceability of the beneficiary, or other 
reasons identified during verification and periodic validation 
undertaken by the respective States/UTs.

PENSIONS FOR IGNOAPS  
   
Components of Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) Scheme being 
implemented by Department of Social Justice and Empowerment:   
S.No Components of Scheme 
1 Integrated Programme for Senior Citizen (IPSrC) - Grant in aid is 
provided to Non-Governmental/ Voluntary Organisations for running 
and maintenance of senior citizen homes (old age homes), continuous 
care homes, etc. Facilities like shelter, nutrition, medicare and 
entertainments are provided free of cost to indigent senior citizens.  
2 State Action Plan for Senior Citizen (SAPSrC) - Under State Action Plan 
for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC), the State Government implements the 
State Action Plan for welfare of senior citizens. Grant in aid is provided 
to States/ UTs for activities like awareness generation, sensitization, 
cataract surgeries and State specific activities.  
3 Elderline - The National Helpline for Senior Citizens is to generate 
awareness about the Act, schemes & programmes being executed by 
different Central & State Governments and to provide platform to 
redress grievances of Senior Citizens across the country. 
4 Rastriya Vayoshree Yojana(RVY) - The objective is to provide senior 
citizens, belonging to BPL category or the senior citizen with the 
monthly income not more than Rs. 15000/- and suffering from age 
related disabilities/ infirmities, with such physical aids and assisted 
living devices which can restore near normalcy in their bodily 
functions. The Scheme is implemented through the ‘Artificial Limbs 
Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO)’, (a Central Public Sector 
Undertaking under the M/oSJE) as the sole implementing Agency.  
5 Senior care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) – SAGE scheme is to 
promote out-of-the-box and innovative solutions for the commonly 
faced problems. Innovative start- ups would be identified and 
encouraged for developing products, processes and services for the 
welfare of the elderly. The selection of the start-ups is made through 
a transparent process and the fund would be provided as equity, 
subject to the Government investment not exceeding 49% of the total 
equity of the Firm.  
6 PM-SPECIAL - The main objective is to bridge the gap in supply and 
increasing demand in the field of geriatric caregivers so as to provide 
more professional services to the senior citizens and also to create a 
cadre of professional care givers in the field of geriatrics.  
7 Other Initiatives for Senior Citizens: In order to solve the problems of 
healthy and productive ageing, several initiatives are being done 
across the country. The proposed initiatives are aimed at involving the 
elders in building up knowledge which can be useful for the society as 
a whole.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3799 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
COST NORMS UNDER MIDH 
 
3799. SHRI G. LAKSHMINARAYANA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the cost norms under Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH), if so, the year of the latest revision and the existing 
cost norms for major interventions, category-wise; and 
 
(b)  whether the Government maintains data on empanelled vendors/agencies 
implementing MIDH interventions and the units established through them, if so, the details 
thereof, State/UT-wise and category-wise? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): Yes. The Government has reviewed the cost norms under Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for various interventions aimed at promoting the 
adoption of modern horticulture technologies by farmers. The review indicated that the cost 
norms for various components, including protected cultivation, micro-irrigation, mulching 
and other horticulture development technologies, required revision in view of the escalation 
in the cost of inputs and materials over time. Therefore, the Operational Guidelines of the 
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) were revised in 2025. Under the 
revised guidelines, the cost norms for various interventions have been enhanced and 
provisions have been made for supporting the latest technologies in the horticulture sector. 
Detailed MIDH Operational Guidelines alongwith revised cost norms are available on MIDH 
web portal i.e. www.midh.gov.in 
 
(b): Under MIDH, assistance is provided on the basis of Annual Action Plans (AAPs) 
received from the States/UTs. The AAPs are prepared by the States/UTs in accordance 
with their assessed requirements, existing infrastructure, priority areas and availability of 
resources. The Operational Guidelines of the Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH) do not contain any specific provision for empaneling vendors/agencies 
for implementing MIDH interventions. However, under Mission Management component of 
MIDH, 2.5% of total annual allocation is provided to State Horticulture Missions for 
managing various activities at State & District level.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3800 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 20, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
ANTI NARCOTICS CAMPAIGN AND DRIVE 
 
3800.      SHRI M K RAGHAVAN: 
      ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken a note of the successful anti -
narcotics drive ‘Operation Toofan’ launched by the State of Kerala recently; 
 
(b) whether the Government will take initiative for a s imilar anti-narcotics 
drive nation-wide and will provide special assistance for States and UTs and 
if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government noted that as per National Crime Record Bureau 
(NCRB) data  the number of cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs & 
Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act are comparatively lower in some states 
which are having large drug seizures and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) the details of drug seizure, the number of cases registered and the 
number of convictions  during the last three years and the current years, 
State wise; 
 
(e) whether the Government is aware of the low conviction rate in the drug 
seizure cases and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(f) whether the Government has any proposal to launch a nationwid e multi-
agency operation involving State Police, Narcotics Control Bureau, Customs, 
Coast Guard and other enforcement  agencies on the lines of these 
campaigns to identify, arrest and prosecute drug traffickers and  dismantle 
organised narcotics networks? 
 
 
 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3800 FOR 11.08.2026  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) Government is aware about launching the Statewide anti -narcotics 
campaign, “Operation Toofan – The Narco Hunt”, on 2nd  June, 2026 by the 
State of Kerala, with the objective of curbing the drug menace across the 
State.  
 
(b) To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, 
Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026 -2029) has been released on 
26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned 
Central Ministries/ Departments/ Agencies and the State Governments/UTs 
as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each 
Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency in a timespan o f three years. It is 
further envisaged that States and Districts would prepare their vision for 3 
years Road Map to control drugs in consonance with the National Road Map 
outlined in the Vision Document. The four key focus areas outlined in the 
vision document are as under: - 
 
(i) Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations) 
(ii) Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control 
(iii) Demand & Harm Reduction 
(iv) Capacity Building & Coordination 

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3800 FOR 11.08.2026  
Further, the Government of India through Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) 
provides financial assistance to the States and UTs under the scheme 
"Assistance to States and UTs for Narcotics Control". The financial 
assistance to the extent of Rs. 24.42 crore were released to the States/UTs 
during the last five years under the scheme. 
 
(c) to (e) National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) collects data from State/ 
UTs and publishes. Before compilation and publication of the data, it is duly 
validated and certified by th e concerned Additional Director General/ 
Inspector General in -charge of the State Crime Records Bureau (SCRB)/ 
Crime Investigation Department (CID) of respective States/ UTs.  
 
As per latest data published by NCRB pertaining to the year 2024; ‘State -
wise/ UT-wise drug seizures’ and ‘State -wise/ UT -wise number of cases 
registered (CR), number of convictions (CON) and conviction rate (CVR)’ 
under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 
during the 2022-2024 are at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively.  
 
(f) The Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026 –2029) released on 
26.06.2026 envisages intelligence-driven, network-centric enforcement with 
enhanced inter -agency coordination to identify, investigate and dismantle 
organised    drug    trafficking    networks.   Under    the   Vision    Document, 
 

-4- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3800 FOR 11.08.2026  
enforcement agencies, including NCB, State Police, Customs, Coast Guard 
and other concerned agencies, are working in close coordination through 
institutional mechanisms such as NCORD, the Joint Coordination Committee 
(JCC), intelligence sharing platforms and joint op erations. The strategy 
focuses on identifying and dismantling major drug cartels, targeting 
traffickers at the transnational, interstate, state and district levels, 
undertaking mandatory financial investigations in commercial quantity 
cases, disrupting proceeds of crime and effectively prosecuting offenders.

PLUG-AND-PLAY SCHEME FOR INDUSTRIAL PARKS 
 
3801.  SHRI GIRIDHARI YADAV: 
SHRI KAUSHALENDRA KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the current status of the Plug -and-Play scheme for industrial part project as 
announced in the Union Budget for the year 2024-25; 
 
(b)  the details of the twelve industrial parks set up/proposed to be set up in 
accordance with the announcements made in the Union Budget for the year 
2024-25, location-wise; 
 
(c)  the present status of all the said twelve industrial parks; and 
 
(d)  whether any of the said twelve industrial parks is being set up in Bihar, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA) Scheme has been notified on 
10.04.2026 as a Central Sector Scheme for development of investment -ready 
industrial parks to enable investors to ground investment with ease, thereby 
adding to the manufacturing capacity in the country. 
 
The total financial outlay for the Scheme is ₹ 33,660 crore and the duration of 
the Scheme is for a period of 6 years. 
 
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is to be provided for development of 
100 industrial parks. In the first phase, 50 projects are to be taken up, with one 
or more rounds of selection. The online portal for receiving the applications for 
the first round of first phase closed on 31 .07.2026, and the second round for 
applications is open from 01.08.2026. 
 
(b): The Union Budget 2024 -25 announced the development of 12 investment -
ready, industrial smart city projects under the National Industrial Corridor 
Development Programme (NICDP). T hese cities are being established with a 
total project cost of ₹ 28,602 crore. The location -wise list of approved projects 
is placed at Annexure-I. 

(c): The present status of these 12 industrial projects is placed at Annexure-II. 
 
(d): Government of India, as part of Amritsar Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC), has 
approved the development of Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) in Gaya, 
admeasuring 1,670 acres in the state of Bihar under the National Industrial 
Corridor Development Programme (NICDP), wit h a total project cost of Rs. 
1,339 crores. Till now, Rs. 135 Cr. has been released to SPV as equity 
contribution. Shareholder Agreement & State Support Agreement were 
executed and Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)—Bihar Integrated Manufacturing 
City Gaya Ltd.  (BIMCGL) was incorporated on 6th January, 2025. 
Environmental clearance for the project was granted on 18th March, 2025. The 
Programme Manager for New Cities appointed in July 2025 by the SPV. 
Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) contractor has been 
appointed in February 2026.

(a)  the current status of implementation of the PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and

under the Scheme, State-wise;

उत्तर

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (d): To develop integrated large scale and modern industrial infrastructure facility for 
entire value-chain of the textile industry, the Government has approved setting up of 7 (Seven)

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 20, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
ACTS ENACTED BY PUNJAB AND HARYANA 
 
3803.      SHRI MANISH TEWARI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Acts enacted by the States of Punjab and Haryana that are 
presently applicable in the UT of Chandigarh, separately, along with the 
subject matter of each such Act; 
 
(b) the legal framework and criteria adopted by the Central Government for 
extending or adapting laws enacted by the State Legislatures of Punjab and 
Haryana to Chandigarh; 
 
(c) the details of the Acts of Punjab and Haryana extended to Chandigarh 
during the last five  years, like the Punjab Right to Business Act, 2020, that 
was extended recently along with the reasons therefor; and 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to formulate a uniform policy or 
framework governing the extension, amendment and repeal of Punjab and 
Haryana laws applicable to Chandigarh, and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) and (c): As per the information provided by the Union territory of 
Chandigarh, 238 Acts enacted by the State of Punjab and 7 Acts enacted by 
the State of Haryana are presently applicable in the Union territory of 
Chandigarh.  The  Act-wise  details,  including  those  Acts  extended  to  the

I. 
 
(b): Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 empowers the Central 
Government, to extend to the Union territory of Chandigarh, any enactment

Administration on the basis of local requirements.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA                                            
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3804 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO THE FAMILIES OF DECEASED FARMERS 
 
3804. SHRI GOVIND MAKTHAPPA KARJOL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS कृ ͪष और ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be pleased 
to state: 
 
(a) the details of the financial assistance, relief, compensation provided by the Government 
to the families of farmers who died by suicide due to indebtedness and to the families of 
farmers who died due to snakebite in the country during each of the last five years, State-
wise; 
(b) the number of cases of farmer suicides and snakebite-related deaths reported during the 
said period along with the number of families that received financial assistance and the 
amount sanctioned and disbursed during the last five years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(c) whether any data is being maintained on small and marginal farmers, women farmers and 
SC/ST farmers who died due to suicide or snakebite, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(d) the details of the steps that have been taken to provide a uniform relief package, insurance 
and livelihood support to the affected families; and 
(e) the measures that have been taken to prevent farmer suicides and snakebite-related 
deaths and strengthen social security for farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष और ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (e):  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) under the Ministry of Home Affairs 
compiles information on suicides and accidental deaths including snakebite in its publication 
titled ‘Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India’ (ADSI). The Report till 2024 is available on 
NCRB website (https://ncrb.gov.in). Further, Agriculture is State subject and ex gratia or relief 
in such cases of death is provided by the State Governments as per their respective policies 
and rules.  
  

       However, the Government of India implements a comprehensive range of Central Sector 
and Centrally Sponsored Schemes and Programmes in the agriculture sector aimed at 
increasing production, productivity and farmers’ income across the country. These schemes 
encompass entire spectrum of agriculture including credit, insurance, income support, 
infrastructure, crops (including horticulture), seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and 
natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, extension, digital agriculture and procurement 
of crops. The list of schemes is placed at Annexure-I. Further the  Government has 
substantially increased the budget allocation of Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 
from ₹27,662.67 crore BE during 2013-14 to ₹1,40,416.57 crore BE during 2026-27. 
       In addition, the Government of India has put in place a social-security and insurance 
architecture to provide financial protection to vulnerable households, including farming 
families. The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) and Pradhan Mantri 
Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provide affordable life and accident insurance coverage. 
PMJJBY provides life insurance protection against death due to any cause, while PMSBY 
provides insurance protection against accidental death and disability, subject to the 
prescribed eligibility and conditions laid down in the respective schemes. 
         Other social-security measures of the Government, include Atal Pension Yojana (APY) 
that provides social security to workers of unorganized sector with provision of guaranteed 
monthly pension. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) is a voluntary and 
contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers which provides guaranteed 
monthly pension of ₹3,000. National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) provides 
financial support and pension to poor and vulnerable section of the society. Ayushman 
Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides free and cashless 
healthcare coverage to poor and vulnerable families. Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) 
is a central sector umbrella scheme for the welfare and empowerment of senior citizens aged 
60 and above. It provides financial security, healthcare, shelter, and a life of dignity. These 
programmes provide different layers of protection against old age, death, disability, health 
expenditure and livelihood vulnerability. 
  

        Further, in order to prevent snakebite-related deaths, the Ministry of Health & Family 
Welfare has launched the National Action Plan for Prevention and Control of Snakebite 
Envenoming (NAPSE) on 12 March 2024. The Action Plan is aligned with the objective of 
reducing snakebite-related deaths and disabilities by 50% by 2030. Under the programme, 
specific interventions include capacity building of healthcare professionals for first aid, 
diagnosis and management of snakebite; improving accessibility to treatment; strengthening 
emergency care at District Hospitals and Community Health Centres, including ambulance 
services; strengthening surveillance of snakebite cases and deaths; 
establishment/strengthening of Regional Venom Centres; operational research on anti-

3806. Shri Rajesh Ranjan: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that several cooperative societies in the country are lying dormant or 
incurring losses due to financial irregularities, weak management and lack of timely audits; 
(b) if so, the details of cooperative societies audited during the last three years, State -wise 
including the number of societies in which irregularities were detected along with the action 
taken against them; and 
(c) the reformative steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure transparency, 
accountability and protection of members' interests in cooperative societies? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) & (b) As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), out of a total 8. 53 lakh 
Cooperative Societies across the country, 6. 63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh are non -functional 
and 49,177 are under liquidation. Among 6. 63 lakh functional cooperative societies, 5.9 5 lakh 
societies are audited and 0.68 lakh societies are not audited. The State-wise details of functional 
and audited c ooperatives societies are attached as Annexure-1. The details of cooperative 
societies lying dormant due to financial irregularities, weak management and lack of timely audits 
is maintained by respective State / UTs. 
 
Further, Cooperative Societies registered under the provisions of the Multi -State Cooperative 
Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 function as autonomous cooperative  organisations and accountable 
to their members. In case of irregularities including financial embezzlement, winding up 
proceeding u/s 86 of the MSCS Act, 2002 are initiated against such MSCSs and liquidator is 
appointed under the provisions of Section 89 of MSCS Act, 2002 to liquidate the assets of Society 
and to ensure payment to investors/members under the provisions of section 90 of the Act. So far, 

Page 2 of 4 
 
115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are put under liquidation. The State-wise number of such 
societies is attached as Annexure-2. 
 
(b) The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several 
initiatives to ensure transparency, accountability and protection of members' interests in 
cooperative societies under the vision of "Sahakar-se-Samriddhi."  Key initiatives include: 
• The Multi -State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 was amended in 2023 to 
strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform 
electoral process, etc. in the Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS). 
• A Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund was established 
under section 63A of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act, 
2023 to revive sick Multi -State Cooperative Societies and provide financial assistance 
for meeting their infrastructure requirements. 
• Circulation of Model Byelaws of PACS, enabling diversification of activities such as 
storage, processing, LPG distribution, and common service centers, ensuring better 
governance standards and promoting member-centric operations. 
• Strengthening of PACS through Computerization of PACS project by bringing 
functional PACS onto a common ERP -based national software, thereby improving 
transparency, efficiency, record management and service delivery.  
• Capacity building and skill development programmes through National Council for Co-
operative Training (NCCT) for members, Board of Directors, employees of cooperative, 
state officials and aspiring youth across the country with a network of 20 training 
institutes.  
• Development of the National Cooperative Database (NCD)  which serves as a  
comprehensive digital repository of 8.53 lakh cooperative societies across the country, 
having approximately 32 crore members. 
• Inclusion of Rural Cooperative Banks under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme to 
bring greater transparency and accountability.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
LOK SABHA

TRADITIONAL FISHING COMMUNITY 
3808. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the impact of industrial projects, 
port development, coastal infrastructure, power projects, mining activities and other large -scale 
developments on traditional fishing communities across coastal States; 
 
(b) the details of studies, consultations or impact assessments undertaken regarding changes in 
fishing grounds, marine biodiversity, fish catch, livelihood opportunities and income of 
fishermen due to such projects during the last five years; 
 
(c) whether the Government has received representations or grievances from fishing communities 
regarding loss of access to traditional fishing areas, coastal pollution, declining fish availability 
and displacement due to industrial activities, if so, the d etails thereof including Kallakurichi 
constituency of Tamil Nadu; and 
 
(d) the measures taken by the Government in coordination with coastal State Governments and 
concerned Ministries to protect the livelihood rights of traditional fishermen, provide 
rehabilitation and compensation where applicable, and ensure sustainable fisheries management? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) and (b): The Government mandates assessments of  environmental and social impacts for  
major infrastructural projects to evaluate ecological and socio -economic effects including on 
traditional fishing communities across the coastal states before granting clearances  to such 
projects. Conducted by project proponents and appraised by authorities, the Environmental 
Impact Assessment (EIA) process covers a comprehensive range of investigations, including 
baseline marine and ecological studies, topographic, bathymetric, and oceanographic surveys, 
shoreline and sediment transport analyses, water, air, and soil quality assessments, and 
hydrodynamic modeling. It also features specialized evaluations such as mangrove and coral 
assessments, dredging and navigation impacts, pollution and oil spill risks, climate vulnerability, 
coastal regulation zone (CRZ) mapping and compliance study, disaster risk assessment and 
emergency response study, and Social Impact Assessments (SIA). To ensure sustainable 
planning, construction, and operation, these projects incorporate mandatory public consultations, 
cost-benefit analyses, and the formulation of robust Environmental Management Plans (EMPs), 
Environmental Monitoring Plans (EMOPs), and Environmental Mitigation Measures. 

 
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has informed that the ICAR‑Central Marine 
Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR‑CMFRI) has undertaken many consultancy projects during 
the last five years for assessing the impacts of such initiatives on fishing grounds, marine 
biodiversity, fish catch, livelihood opportunities, and the income of fishermen. The details of the 
consultancy projects completed during this period are placed at Annexure.  
(c): Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that 6 representations and grievances have been 
received in Chennai District from fishing villages in North Chennai, related to pollution in the 
Kosasthalaiyar river, adverse impact on the livelihood of fishers al ong Ennore Creek and the 
north Chennai coast. In Thoothukudi district , fishers in 6 villages have represented livelihood 
loss and sea erosion due to Udangudi Thermal Power Project . To prevent sea erosion, 
breakwaters have been established in the villages o f Allanthalai, Manapad, and Periyathalai. In 
Tirunelveli district , a  grievance has been received from the 7 fishing villages regarding sea 
erosion due to the extension of the bait arch at the Kudankulam Atomic Power Project, affecting 
the berthing of fishi ng crafts and shifting of fishing grounds to long er distances. In 
Kanniyakumari district, 3 grievances have been received from stakeholders regarding coastal 
pollution (Radiation) due to industrial activities such as mining by Indian Rare Earths (India) 
Limited (IREL)  in Manavalakurichi, Kanniyakumari district. In respect of Kallakurichi 
constituency, no representation or grievance has been received so far from fishing communities. 
(d): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), in coordination with the 
coastal states has undertaken comprehensive measures for the sustainable harnessing of marine 
fisheries resources and the welfare of small‑scale and traditional fishers. The Government has 
notified the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone Rules , which 
mandate key conservation measures, including a uniform fishing ban during fish breeding 
seasons; minimum legal size for fish capture and adoption of bycatch‑reduction measures; 
prohibition of destructive and juvenil e fishing practices; and promotion of best practices to 
minimise post‑harvest losses.  
For sustainable fishing, enhancement of fish stocks, and sea‑safety considerations, a uniform 
61‑day fishing ban is implemented annually in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). Coastal 
States/UTs also enforce corresponding bans within their territorial waters in alignment with the 
EEZ‑wide ban. Livelihood and nutritional support for socio‑economically backward active 
traditional fishers during the fishing ban/lean period, as well as group accident insurance for 
active fishers, is provided under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).  
Under PMMSY, the Government of India has, for the first time, extended support for activities 
by the coastal states such as sea ranching and installation of Artificial Reefs (ARs) along the 
entire coastline to prevent h abitat degradation, enhance fish stocks, and support fishers’ 
livelihoods. Activities such as mariculture, including seaweed cultivation and open‑sea cage 
culture, are also promoted to reduce fishing pressure in nearshore waters and augment marine 
fisheries production in a sustainable manner.    
PMMSY further includes the component “Development of 100 Coastal Fishermen Villages as 
Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV)”, aimed at transforming 100 villages 
selected jointly with the coastal Stat es/UTs into economically vibrant and climate‑resilient 
villages through need -based interventions including infrastructure and livelihood‑enhancing 
activities.
