(a) the manner in which the proposed University relating to cooperative societies is expected 
to contribute particularly to the modernization of training systems, development of domain 
experts in various fields of cooperation, and the growth and professionalis ation of the 
cooperative sector in the country; 
(b) the steps being taken to promote the participation and leadership of women in cooperative 
societies particularly in the State of Rajasthan; 
(c) the measures being taken to ensure that the cooperative sector remains competitive in the 
digital era, including the use of technology to increase transparency, efficiency and 
member services; and 
(d) the process adopted for designing the curriculum of the proposed University to ensure 
practical training and research in cooperative management by incorporating the latest best 
practices and innovations in the cooperative sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) The “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University Act, 2025, mandates the University  to provide 
qualified and trained manpower to meet the present and future needs of the co-operative sector 
by establishing its own schools and through affiliating institutes and also to standardise the 
course design and content, pedagogy, course delivery in co -operative education and training 
for professionalisation of workforce in the cooperative sector. In terms of modernization of 
training systems, the University uses digital contents, simulations, games and other modern 
techniques. 
(b) So far as the participation and leadership of women in cooperative societies, particularly 
in Rajasthan, is concerned, National Cooperative Development Corporation ( NCDC), a 
statutory body under the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India, is mandated to 
promote economic development through cooperatives by strengthening farmer institutions, 
enhancing productivity, and supporting pre- and post-harvest infrastructure. 

Page 2 of 18 
 
The NCDC has been providing financial assistance to the cooperative sector under its 
corporation-sponsored schemes as well as various schemes of Government of India , covering 
a wide range of notified commodities and services, as amended from time to time. In recent 
years, NCDC has introduced sector -specific schemes and focused products to align with the 
evolving needs of the cooperative sector, with special emphasis on new cooperatives, women 
empowerment, rural healthcare etc. thereby strengthening the cooperative infrastructure. 
Details of the activities supported and schemes implemented are provided at Annexure-I 
NCDC, to promote the participation and leadership of women in cooperative societies , is 
implementing the following schemes exclusively for women led  self-help group and 
cooperatives on pan india basis: 
i. Swayam Shakti Sahakar Yojna 
ii. Nandini Sahakar 
iii. Yuva Sahakar Yojana 
 
The schemes are fully funded and supported by NCDC. 
The detail of Swayam Shakti Shahakar Yojna is at Annexure-II. 
The detail of Nandini Sahakar is at Annexure-III. 
The detail of Yuva Sahakar Yojana is at Annexure-IV . 
Disbursement details for the last 3 years for women cooperatives in the state of Rajasthan is as 
follows: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(c) The Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several measures to ensure that the 
cooperative sector remains competitive in the digital era. The major measures are as under: 
1. Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project:  The 
Ministry is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of 
functional PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has now been 
increased up to 2925.39 Crore which entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an 
ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national software, linking them 
with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central 
Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). This has been done with a view to improving their 
operational efficiency, transpa rency and accountability through ERP -based National 
Software. The project facilitates standardized accounting, audit, MIS, online service 
delivery and integration with various national digital platforms, thereby enabling 
efficient governance and better ser vice delivery to members. Under the 
Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project, 63,686 
PACS have been onboarded on the ERP -based National Software, 54,707 PACS have 
been declared as e -PACS and more than 51.58 crore digital transactions have been

2. Computerisation of the Office of Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS):  
Centrally sponsored project for computerization of RCS offices in States/Union

aims to enhance the ease of doing business for Cooperative Societies and create a digital

their proposals, and Rs 43.21 crore has been released as the Government of India's share 
to States/UTs. The integrated digital RCS portals of 7 States/UTs have been gone live 
and integrated with National Cooperative Database also. 
3. Computerization of Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs): To 
strengthen the long-term cooperative credit structure, the project of computerization of 
1,867 units of Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs) spread across 13

implementing agency for the project. So far, proposals from 10 States/UTs have been 
received and sanctioned with 1,422 units. Further, GOI share amounting to Rs 16.74 
crore has been released to 10 States/UTs in FY 2023-24, FY 24-25, FY 2025-26 and FY

SUPPLEMENTARY NOTE ON SWAYAMSHAKTI  SAHAKAR YOJNA 
National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) is an apex level statutory institution 
set up by the Government of India under an Act of the Parliament in 1963. NCDC has been 
created for the purpose of planning and promoting programmes for the production, processing, 
marketing, storage, export and import of agricultural produce, foodstuffs, industrial goods, 
livestock, certain other commodities and services on cooperative principles. NCDC extends 
financial assistance to cooperatives at all the three tie rs, Primary, District and Apex / Multi -
State. NCDC is under the administrative control of the Ministry of Cooperation. 
 
I) OBJECTIVE OF THE SCHEME: 
• Access to the affordable cost-effective reliable financial services to the poor. 
• Facilitating women SHGs to access adequate bank credit to undertake the 
common/collective socio-economic activities. 
• Promotion of sustainable livelihood 
II)         CO OPERATIVES ELIGIBLEFOR ASSISTANCE:  
The following types of Agricultural Credit Cooperatives will be eligible for NCDC’s loan 
under this scheme. 
• Primary Agricultural Credit Co operatives (PACS) 
• District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) 
• State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) 
• SHG Federated Cooperatives/ Cooperative federations 
 
III) ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA 
 NCDC loan shall be provided to Credit Cooperatives fulfilling the following criteria of 
direct funding: 
i) Cooperative should have been in operation for not less than 3 years. 
ii) Cooperatives should have positive net worth, not less than 100% paid up share 
capital, i.e there should be no erosion in the paid up share capital. 
iii) Cooperatives should not have incurred any cash loss during last three years and 
there should be net profit in atleast two of the previous three years. 
 
IV) PURPOSE FOR WHICH NCDCASSISTANCEWILLBE EXTENDED: 
 NCDC assistance will be extended to eligible Credit Cooperatives for onward lending of 
working capital loan or term loans to women SHGs. 
 
V) PATTERN OF FUNDING:  
 Loan as per requirement of the Credit Cooperatives and as assessed by NCDC (as per 
credit cooperatives lending business turnover) for onward lending of short /medium term to 
women SHGs. 
VI)       SECURITY:

The loan shall be secured by one, or combination of two or more, of the following to the 
satisfaction of NCDC:  
i. Mortgage of fixed assets of credit cooperatives of value not less than 1.50 times of the 
loan amount. 
ii. Pledge of Fixed Deposit Receipts with face value not less than 1.10 times of   the   loan 
amount 
iii. State Government Guarantee/Bank Guarantee. 
iv. Hypothecation of Loans/Advances of Credit Cooperatives receivable from women 
SHGs, at least to the extent of 1.25 times of the loan amount. 
In addition to the above, Loan agreement and demand Promissory Note will also be 
stipulated. If required, Postdated Cheques shall also form part of the security documents.  
VII)  MODE OF RELEASE OF LOAN: 
          On receipt of the application, loan shall be sanctioned based on the merits of the proposal.  
Release of loan shall be made after completing the formalities and fulfillment of terms & 
conditions stipulated in the sanction letter and shall be in one or more installments, within the 
stipulated period for drawal of loan. 
VIII) PERIOD OF LOAN / MORATORIUM / RATEOF INTEREST: 
          Short term working capital loan will be for upto 3 years with a maximum moratorium of 
6 months in repayment of principal amount. However, there will not be any moratorium in 
payment of interest. Credit Cooperatives may also avail working capital loan for 5 years on 
revolving basis with yearly validation. Loan shall be repaid in half yearly installments 
IX) RATEOF INTEREST:  
 As per NCDC circular for interest rate as amended from time to time.  
X)     PROCESSING FEE & LEGAL FEE: 
           In case of direct funding, the cooperative shall pay processing fee @0.5% of the 
sanctioned amount subject to a maximum of Rs.3.00 lakh plus tax applicable at the time of 
payment. However, No processing fee would be charged for working capital loan upto 1 year. 
The borrower cooperative shall meet the legal expenses incurred for execution of security 
documents.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO– 3811

PARTICIPATION OF SC, ST AND MINORITIES IN PRI 
  
3811. MD. RAKIBUL HUSSAIN: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to promote participation of Scheduled Castes (SC), 
Scheduled Tribes (ST), and minority communities in Panchayati Raj Institutions in Assam; 
(b) whether representation norms are being effectively implemented, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether targeted capacity-building programmes have been undertaken; and 
(d) the outcomes achieved so far? 
 
 ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
  
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) and (b) The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, through Article 243D in Part IX, provides 
for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in every 
Panchayat in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area, and also mandates the 
reservation of the offices of Chairperson in Panchayats at each level for SCs and STs, in such 
manner as the State Legislature may, by law, determine. The provisions for reservation of seats 
and offices of Chairperson for SCs and STs have been incorporated in respective State 
Panchayati Raj Acts of States/Union Territories (UTs). 
  
As informed by the State Government of Assam, 'The Assam Panchayat Act, 1994' 
provides for reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) at all 
three tiers of the Panchayati Raj Institutions, namely the Gaon Panchayat (Section 9), Anchalik 
Panchayat (Section 34) and Zilla Parishad (Section 66). The number of seats reserved shall, as 
nearly as may be, bear the same proportion to the total number of seats to be filled through direct 
election as the population of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes in the respective 
Panchayat area bears to the total population of that area. The reserved seats shall be allotted to 
different territorial constituencies by rotation in the manner prescribed under above said State 
Act. 
  

2 
 
As informed by the State of Assam, the reservation norms are being effectively 
implemented in the State. 
  
(c) and (d) ‘Panchayat’, being a “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of the State List 
of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, targeted capacity building 
programmes for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and their outcomes are the responsibility of 
the concerned States/UTs. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj has implemented the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), 
w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the objective of supporting Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) 
by imparting training to elected representatives, including SCs, STs and minority communities 
and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram Panchayats to 
function effectively across all States/UTs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3812 
  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
FUNDS FOR VB-G RAM G 
 
3812. Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has notified the implementation 
framework, operational guidelines and funding norms for the 
Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rojgar and Aajeevika Mission 
Gramin (VB-G RAM G) Scheme, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the criteria adopted for determining normative allocations under 
the Scheme including the weightage assigned to rural 
population, poverty levels, unemployment, Scheduled Tribe 
population, geographical disadvantage and demand for wage 
employment, State and district-wise; 
(c)  whether any assessment has been made of the gap between the 
demand-driven employment provided under the erstwhile 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) and the normative allocations proposed under VB-G 
RAM G, if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  whether States have been consulted for the allocation formula 
and implementation framework, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  the measures taken to ensure that eligible rural households are 
not denied employment or livelihood support on account of 
exhaustion of normative allocations or budgetary ceilings? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Consequent upon enactment of Viksit Bharat–Guarantee 
for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Act 2025, 
the scheme has been successfully operationalized in rural areas of 
the entire country with effect from 1st July, 2026. All States and 
Union Territories have notified the Scheme and have started works 
under VB-G RAM G by providing employment to the willing 
households as per the provisions of the Act.  The transition from 

Page 2 of 3 
 
Mahatma Gandhi NREGA to VB-G RAM G has been smooth, 
seamless and worker-centric. Over 9.69 Crore person days have 
been generated in approximately within a month of the rollout of 
the scheme in the country. As mandated under section 33 of the 
Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) 
Act, 2025, the Ministry has already framed eight draft rules and 
published  the same in e-gazette inviting 
comments/suggestions/objections from all stakeholders including 
State Governments and general public. This also include the 
“Objective parameters for the Normative Allocation Rules” under 
VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. After examination and consideration of the 
suggestions/ objections received from the Stakeholders, the 
Ministry has already notified the following 4 Rules under the new 
framework of VB-G RAM G as given below:  
  
i.   Transitional Provisions under Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for 
Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB – G RAM G Rules, 
2026. 
ii.   Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin): VB-G RAM G - Administrative Expenses Rules, 2026. 
iii.  Viksit Bharat- Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin): VB-G RAM G, manner of Payment of Wages and 
Unemployment Allowance Rules, 2026. 
iv.  Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin): VB-G RAM G -Manner and procedure of expenditure 
incurred by the State in excess of the Normative Allocation and 
expenses of the scheme for the Union territories without 
legislature Rules, 2026. 
  
Since the Subordinate Legislation prescribing  objective 
parameters for the Normative allocation  is under formulation, the 
Ministry of Rural Development has made interim fund allocations to 
all States/UTs for the financial year 2026-27 as an interim financial 
arrangement to ensure continuity in the implementation of the wage 
employment programme, uninterrupted discharge of the statutory 
entitlements and guarantees under the Act, and seamless availability 
of funds from the commencement of the Act. 
  
(c) to (e): The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides for a statutory 
guarantee of wage employment of one hundred and twenty five days 
to every eligible rural household whose adult members are willing to 
do unskilled manual work subject to the provisions of the Act and the 
Rules made thereunder. The Ministry remains engaged with the 
States/Union Territories through established institutional 
mechanisms for matters relating to implementation of the Scheme.   

Page 3 of 3 
 
VB-G RAM G  is demand-driven programme, and the statutory right of 
every willing rural household to demand employment remains fully 
protected under the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025. The State Government is 
responsible for ensuring availability of employment in accordance 
with the provisions of the Act. To facilitate smooth implementation, 
the Central Government has made an interim allocation of ₹95,692.31 
crore for FY 2026–27(for period between 01.07.2026 to 31.03.2027), 
which is among the highest ever allocation made for any rural 
employment programme at Budget Estimate (BE) stage in the 
country. With the matching state share, the total programme outlay 
is likely to exceeds ₹1.51 lakh crore during FY 2026-27. This interim 
normative allocations will help in ensuring timely availability of funds 
and uninterrupted implementation of the Programme. 
 
The Act further provides that where expenditure incurred for 
providing the statutory employment guarantee exceeds the approved 
normative allocation, the additional requirement shall be met by the 
concerned State Government, thereby ensuring that the entitlement 
of willing rural households is not constrained by the approved 
allocation. In addition, the Act contains enabling provisions for 
natural calamities, pandemics and other extraordinary 
circumstances, under which, on the request of the State Government, 
the Central Government may permit appropriate operational 
relaxations, including temporary expansion of permissible works, 
relaxation of procedural requirements and enhanced employment 
support to affected households, in accordance with the provisions of 
the Act. 
 
Further, where employment is not provided within the 
prescribed period, the household is entitled to unemployment 
allowance in accordance with the provisions of the Act. These 
provisions collectively ensure that the statutory employment 
guarantee under the Act remains fully protected.

(a):  The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has been implementing the Mission

Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and post- harvest management including processing,

Further, the MIDH Operational Guidelines were revised in 2025, with enhanced cost

encourage area expansion, improve productivity and promote the adoption of improved

Research (ICAR–DCR), Puttur is engaged in development of cashew production

Some of the varieties developed by this institute are cocoa Hybrids-(VTLCH 1 to 5) and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3814 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
CLIMATE RESILIENT AGRICULTURE 
  3814. SHRI SAUMITRA KHAN: 
           SHRI MITESHBHAI RAMESHBHAI PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the key initiatives undertaken by the Ministry to promote climate-resilient and climate-
smart agriculture during FY 2026-27, in the country especially in Bishnupur Lok Sabha 
Constituency or in the State of West Bengal; 
(b) whether region-specific crop diversification strategies and climate-resilient seed varieties 
have been promoted, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the details of financial and technical support provided to farmers for adoption of climate-
resilient practices? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government, through the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), is 
implementing a project, namely National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture 
(NICRA), in the country including the State of West Bengal. Under the project, risk and 
vulnerability assessment to climate change has been carried out for 651 agricultural districts 
as per Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). Out of the 310 districts identified 
as vulnerable to climate change, 201 have been categorized as 'High' climate-vulnerable 
and 109 as 'Very High' climate-vulnerable. Of the 201 districts in the 'High' category, 11 
districts fall in the State of West Bengal. Of the 109 district in the ‘Very High' category, 3 
districts fall in West Bengal. None of the districts falling under the Bishnupur Lok Sabha 
Constituency have been identified as climate-vulnerable under either the 'High' or 'Very High' 
category. District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) for these districts have been 
prepared to address weather aberrations and recommending location specific climate 
resilient crops and varieties and management practices. For enhancing the resilience and 
adaptive capacity of farmers to climate variability, location-specific climate resilient 
technologies have been demonstrated under the project through KVKs in 151 districts. Out 
of these 151 climatically vulnerable districts, 7 districts are in West Bengal namely, 
Darjeeling, Cooch Behar, Malda, Murshidabad, 24-Parganas (North), Purulia, and 24-
Parganas (South) . Further, ICAR has released 2,900 crop varieties during the last 10 years 
(2014–2024). Out of these, 2,661 varieties are tolerant to one or more biotic and/or abiotic 
stresses. 
 
In addition, to promote climate resilient and climate smart agriculture, Government is 
implementing number of central and centrally sponsored schemes since long.  Per Drop 
More Crop scheme aims to increase water-use efficiency at the farm level through micro-
irrigation technologies, i.e., drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. Rainfed Area Development 
scheme promotes Integrated Farming System for enhancing productivity and minimizing 
risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health & Fertility scheme assists States in 

promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through judicious use of fertilizers. Organic 
farming is promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) and natural farming 
through the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). Mission for Aatmanirbharta in 
Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds, and National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM) promote crop diversification. Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH), Agroforestry and National Bamboo Mission (NBM) also promote 
climate resilience in agriculture. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) along with the 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) provides comprehensive 
insurance cover against crop failure, thereby helping compensate farmers for losses caused 
by natural calamities and climate-related risks.  Financial support under these schemes is 
provided as per scheme guidelines. 
 
As reported by the Government of West Bengal, to encourage farmers to adopt 
climate resilient agricultural practices, during 2026–27 in the Bishnupur Lok Sabha 
Constituency, demonstration of indigenous varieties of aromatic paddy has been 
undertaken. Organic-based farming is being promoted through Khet Bachao Abhijan along 
with awareness programmes on Soil Health and Fertility. Crop diversification is being 
promoted through cultivation of maize and arhar, while nutri-cereals (ragi) are being 
promoted in upland areas. Prakritik Krishi Karmashala is being implemented to promote 
natural farming practices. Financial assistance of ₹154.91 lakh has been provided for 
Aromatic Paddy Demonstration, ₹112.50 lakh for the Diversified Cropping Programme, 
₹21.50 lakh for Prakritik Krishi Karmashala, ₹15.00 lakh for promotion of nutri-cereals (ragi), 
and ₹4.73 lakh for Khet Bachao Abhijan. Technical support is being provided through 
demonstrations, farmer awareness programmes and training to facilitate adoption of 
climate-resilient agricultural practices.

वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, 
is a transformative “Whole of Government” approach to bring together various 
Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs to ensure integrated planning 
and coordinated execution of infrastructure  projects. PMGS NMP aims to  
facilitate Ministries/States in data driven decision making by utilizing geospatial 
data, satellite imagery and API integration to monitor, plan, and optimize 
infrastructure development. The PMGS NMP is facilitating Ministries/S tates in 
planning of their respective infrastructure projects, including social 
infrastructure projects, in integrated, synchronized and coordinated manner to 

provide seamless and efficient connectivity for the movement of people, goods, 
and services acros s various modes of transport, thereby enhancing last -mile 
connectivity and reducing travel time. 
PM GatiShakti provides an integrated planning framework; the approval and 
implementation of the projects are undertaken by the respective central 
Ministries/Departments and States/UTs under their plans, schemes, 
procedures and budgetary/funding provisions. Hence, no quantified targets or 
expenditure requirements have been set under PM GatiShakti initiative. 
(b): The Network Planning Group (NPG), constituted under the PM GatiShakti 
framework, evaluates the critical infrastructure projects of the central 
Government to ensure integrated planning, multimodality, inter -modality, 
synchronization of eﬀorts, last mile con nectivity, comprehensive development 
in and around the project location, data driven decision makings, etc at the 
planning stage. As on date, 396 infrastructure projects with total estimated cost 
of about ₹ 18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the NPG 
mechanism. Out of these 396 projects, 256 projects have been sanctioned - out 
of which, 198 projects are under implementation. Ministry-wise details are given 
at Annexure-A. 
 
(c) to (e): Government carries out assessment of its initiatives/schemes from time to time 
through various studies, surveys, etc. Apart from these, there are several 
studies by universities and research scholars in this respect. As per these 
assessments, the integrated planning initiatives like, PM GatiShakti, National 
Logistics Po licy, PRAGATI, Sagarmala, development of connectivity 
infrastructure (expressways/ national highways/ dedicated rail freight corridors 
and rail tracks, industrial  corridors/hubs), etc. have shaped the vision of 
connected and competitive India and have impr oved logistics efficiency, turn -
around time, ease of doing business,  industrial growth and reduced logistics 
cost in country. An assessment of logistic cost has been carried out by DPIIT 
in the year 2025 in collaboration with National Council of Applied Ec onomic 
Research (NCAER). As per the assessment, the logistics cost in India is 
estimated at 7.9% of the GDP, which is at par with the advanced economies in 
the world. The Economic Survey 2023 -24 highlighted that these  measures  
have  improved  domestic  manufacturing  and  export competitiveness. 
A study by Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore on impact of 
development of National Highway projects underlines that every -one rupee 
expenditure in National Highways development leads to a ₹3.2 increase in 
Gross Domestic Product (GDP). 
(f):  So far 58 Central Ministries/Departments and all 36 States/UTs have been 
onboarded on the PMGS NMP, covering all infrastructure sectors like road, rail, 
ports & waterways, power, petroleum & natural gas, civil aviation, 
telecommunications, industrial corridors, etc. Further, PM GatiShakti public 
platform (url: ugi.pmgatishakti.gov.in) has been launched in September 2025, 
which provided access of PM GatiShakti data analytics to private entities and 

general public. Through this Query based mechanism, public and private 
entities are able to plan their projects by obtaining data analytic reports from 
the PMGS-NMP Portal through a simple query -based mechanism. The States 
have been encouraged to expand the use of PM GatiShakti f or district level 
planning. About 1800 data layers have been integrated and over 65 software 
modules/tools and more than 100 mobile/web applications have been 
developed and integrated on the platform for the use of stakeholders. Further 
expansion of the PM  GatiShakti initiative is a continuous process - 
mapping/integration of more data layers, development and integration of 
additional features, software modules/tools for planning and analysis 
modules/tools, mobile/ web applications, etc. to be continue furt her as per the 
requirements of the Ministries/Departments, States/UTs and other 
stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
 LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
MUTHALAPPOZHY FISHING HARBOUR 
 
3816. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of the implementation of the project of Rs.177 crore approved by the Union 
Government in November, 2024 for ensuring safety and smooth operation of Muthalappozhy Fishing 
Harbour in Kerala;  
(b) the details of fund released, utilized and the progress of works till date; 
(c) the details of measures taken by the Government to complete the development works without further 
delay; and 
(d) the timeline by which sanctioned projects are likely to be completed?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying, 
Government of India has accorded administrative approval on 01st November, 2024 for Expansion of 
Muthalapozhy Fishing Harbour at Thiruvananthapuram District in Kerala at an estimated cost of Rs.177 
Crore with central share of Rs 106.20 Crore under the Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY). The project has been implemented by the State Government of Kerala.  
 
During the financial year 2025 -2026 and 2026 -27, the central funds of Rs 100 Crore and Rs 30 Crore 
respectively has been allocated to Government of Kerala under PMMSY in SNA SPARSH towards 
implementation of various components/activities approved to Kerala under PMMSY including 
Muthalappozhy Fishing Harbour project. The State Government of Kerala has reported that Rs 45.41 
Crore has been utilised under this project . The physical progress of works as reported by the State is  
30%. 
 
The Department of Fisheries,  Government of India, regularly  reviews the implementation of projects 
approved under the Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) including the Muthalappozhy 
Fishing Harbour project . Further, the State Government of Kerala has stated that the concerne d state 
government officials are reviewing the work twice in a month to avoid delay in the progress of work. 
The State Government of Kerala has stated that the due date of completion of work is 31.12.2027.

RELIEF TO FARMERS AFFECTED BY FLOODS 
 
3817. SHRI GAURAV GOGOI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the damage caused to crops due to the 
recent floods in Assam and if so, the details thereof, district-wise; 
(b) the total area of agricultural land damaged, inundated or rendered uncultivable and 
estimated value of crops damaged due to floods in Assam during the last five years, 
year-wise;  
(c) the total number of farmers affected and the estimated financial loss suffered by 
them during the said period;  
(d) whether the Government has provided or proposes to provide compensation or 
financial assistance to farmers for crop losses caused by the recent floods in Assam 
and if so, the details thereof, including the proposed amount and the mechanism and 
timeline for disbursement, including through the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY), wherever applicable; 
(e) the steps taken to ensure timely assessment of crop damage and disbursement of 
compensation and insurance claims to affected farmers; and  
(f) the steps taken to restore and protect agricultural land from recurring flood 
damage?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

not maintained centrally. However, as informed by the Government of Assam, the 
State has undertaken assessment of damage caused to standing crops due to the 
recent floods in Assam. Submergence of crops is reported and monitored through the 
Disaster Reporting and Information Management Portal (DRIMS) by the State

(d) & (e): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on 
ground level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake 
relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of 
the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of 
India approved items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above 
SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid 
down procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment 
based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum 
submitted by the State Government for financial assistance from NDRF.   The financial 
assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief and not for 
compensation of losses suffered/ claimed.   
  

    The details of funds allocated and released to Assam under SDRF and NDRF 
during 2021-22 to 2025-26 (during 15th Finance Commission period) is available at 
ndmindia.mha.in.  As reported by MHA, the balance available with the State in SDRF 
is 1851.06 crore.  An allocation of Rs.4660 crore is provided for Assam for the period 
from 2026-27 to 2030-31 (under 16th Finance Commission).    
     Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) is being 
implemented by the State of Assam (since inception, i.e. Kharif 2016). The details of 
Claims paid, Farmer applications insured and Farmer applications paid claims in the 
State of Assam in last five years is as under:

 Following steps have been taken by the Government of India to ensure timely 
settlement of claims under the scheme: 
 Government has undertaken development of National Crop Insurance Portal 
(NCIP) as a single source of data for subsidy payment, dissemination of 
information, delivery of services including online enrolment of farmers, 
uploading/obtaining individual insured famer’s details and transfer of claim 
amount electronically to the individual farmer’s Bank Account.   
  

 In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module 
namely ‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims 
from Kharif 2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance 
Portal (NCIP) with Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and 
accounting system of Insurance Companies to provide timely & transparent 
processing of all claims. 
 W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance Company, 
penalty of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP.    
 Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State 
Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate 
claims relating to the Central Government share.  
 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in 
release of State share of subsidy. 
 Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for deposit 
of their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme has been 
made mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial discipline.   
 Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various 
steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data 
through CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance 
companies to witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records 
with NCIP and usage of remote sensing based yield estimation through YES-
TECH have already been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to 
farmers.   
 Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application 
to streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for localised 
calamities/post-harvest losses for individual farms and land parcels under 
PMFBY.  The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the States/UTs 
under the scheme. 
 
(f):  Flood management and anti-erosion schemes are formulated and implemented 
by concerned State Governments.  The Union Government supplements the efforts of 
the States by providing technical guidance and also promotional financial assistance 
for management of floods in critical areas. 
  

 
Integrated flood approach aims at adopting judicious mix of structural and non-
structural measures to provide a reasonable degree of protection against floods 
damages at economic cost.  Short-term and long-term food mitigation measures 
include watershed and catchment management, wetland restoration, strengthening of 
early warning systems and floodplain zoning.  Union Government is implementing a 
centrally sponsored “Flood Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP)” for 
providing central assistance to States for works related to flood control, anti-erosion, 
drainage development, anti-sera erosion etc. during 2021-26.  Total central assistance 
amounting to Rs.9139.75 crore has been released under FMBAP Scheme to various 
States upto March 2026. 
Central assistance of Rs. 1629.02 Crore has been released to the State 
Government of Assam since the XI Plan for 142 projects. 142 flood management 
projects of Assam have been included under the FMBAP Scheme, out of which 111 
projects have been completed, benefitting 7.364 Lakh ha of land and a population of 
174.52 Lakh. 30 projects have been foreclosed.   
The following measures are being taken by the Department of Agriculture, Assam, 
for restoration of flood-affected agricultural land and for protection of cropping from 
recurring flood damage. 
i) District Flood Contingency Plans have been prepared for all the 35 districts 
of the State, providing for crop-wise and situation-wise contingency 
measures.  
ii) Distribution of flood-tolerant and short-duration seed varieties, including 
submergence-tolerant paddy varieties, for re-sowing and late transplanting 
in flood-affected areas. 
iii) Establishment of Community Nurseries for raising of seedlings and their 
supply to farmers whose seedbeds have been damaged due to floods. 
iv) A buffer stock of certified seed is maintained through the Assam Seeds 
Corporation Ltd. (ASCL) for immediate deployment in the affected districts.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) and (b) A list of proposed, under negotiation and currently in force Free Trade 
Agreements (FTAs) with India is placed at Annexure. The details and salient features 
of India’s FTAs entered into force may be sourced at 
https://www.commerce.gov.in/#/international-trade/trade-agreements. Brief features of 
recent FTAs are listed below: 
• India–Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA): India 
has secured 100% d uty-free market access for its exports, covering 98.08% of 
Oman’s tariff lines, representing 99.38% of India’s export value.  
• India - UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) provides 
duty-free access to almost 99 % of India’s exports to the UK , covering nearly 
100% of the trade value.  All zero-duty concessions come into effect with entry 
into force. India’s major exports—from labor-intensive sectors like textiles, gems 
& jewellery, leather and footwear, organic chemical, artisanal products, an d 
ceramics to high-value goods like auto parts, machinery, pharmaceuticals, and 
processed foods have secured zero-duty access to the UK.  

2 
 
• India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA): India has 
secured a binding commitment from EFTA covering 92.2% of tariff lines (99.6% 
of India’s exports), including 100% of non -agricultural products and tariff 
concessions on Processed Agricultural Products  
• India–Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement:  In the FTA all 
exports of India including fo od, agricultural and marine products are eligible for 
zero-duty market access from 1 January 2026.  
• India and United Arab Emirates (UAE) Comprehensive Economic Partnership 
Agreement (CEPA): India has secured duty-free and preferential market access 
on 97% of UAE tariff lines covering 99% of India’s exports, with immediate duty 
elimination on over 80% of tariff lines. 
  
Apart from the above, the India -New Zealand FTA has been signed, and the 
India-EU FTA has concluded negotiations. Brief features are as follows :  
  
• India–New Zealand FTA: New Zealand will provide 100% duty -free market 
access on all tariff lines, including agri -processed products, marine products, 
dairy products and other rural livelihood-based products from the entry into force 
of the agreement. This agreement has been signed and presently under 
ratification.  
• India-European Union (EU) FTA:  Preferential Market Access on 96.8% of tariff 
lines which covers 99.5% of India’s exports. 90.7% of exports (by trade value) to 
the EU to become duty-free on entry into force of the Agreement. The Agreement 
will come into force after signing and ratification by both the Parties. The process 
of signing and ratification will be carried forward by both the Parties in mutual 
consultation. 
  
FTAs are negotiated with the endeavour to deliver comprehensive, balanced, fair 
and mutually beneficial outcomes. It also enables a preferential, stable and predictable 
trade ecosystem for Indian exporters in the trading partner countries. In addition to this 
structured approach, post -implementation, the Government is continuously engaged 
with all stakeholders to ensure effective FTA utilization  through trade promotion, trade 
facilitation and addressing challenges if any. Indicatively, among the recently signed 
FTAs, the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) signed with the 
European Free Trade Association (EFTA) in March 2024 and implem ented in October 
2025 includes commitment to invest USD 100 billion in India over 15 years. Similarly, 
the India – New Zealand FTA signed in April, 2026 is committed to facilitate investments 
of USD 20 billion into India over the next 15 years. 
Despite persistent global challenges, including geopolitical tensions and supply 
chain disruptions, India's exports increased from US$ 677 billion in FY 2021-22 to US$ 
863 billion in FY 2025 -26. Merchandise exports to major FTA partner countries and 
trade blocs have been substantial at US$ 179.1 billion in FY 2025 -26, accounting for 
40.5% of India's total merchandise exports. Merchandise export to recent FTA partner 
also indicated significant export growth. For example, exports to the UAE increased 
from US$ 16.7 billion in FY 2021-22 (prior to CEPA implementation) to US$ 37.4 billion 
in FY 2025 -26, while exports to Australia rose from US$ 4.0 billion in FY 2021 -22 to 
US$ 7.3 billion in FY 2025-26 following the implementation of ECTA. Similarly, exports 

3 
 
to EFTA countries increased from US$ 1.64 billion in FY 2019-20 to US$ 1.76 billion in 
FY 2025-26. 
(c)        Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 establishes a strong data privacy 
framework. It places corresponding obligations on Data Fiduciaries to ensure lawful 
processing and protection of personal data. The Act empowers citizens by giving them 
rights enforceable against the Data Fiduciaries. The Digital Personal Data Protection 
(DPDP) Rules 2025 notified to provide a comprehensive framework for the processing 
of personal data, including cross-border transfers. The framework enables the Central 
Government to prescribe additional conditions, including restrictions on the transfer of 
certain categories of personal data, where necessary. 
  Government is committed to fostering and expanding digital trade partnerships with 
potential nations across the world. For instance, Free Trade Agreements with United 
Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, and the European Union, include a dedicated chapter 
on Digital Trade with an aim to enhance and facilitate digital trade.

  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
INCREASE IN WORKING DAYS UNDER VB-G RAM G 
 
3819. Smt. Delkar Kalaben Mohanbhai: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to increase the number of 
working days under Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and 
Ajeevika Mission-Gramin (VB-G RAM G), if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to launch new programmes 
for generating sustainable employment in the rural areas of 
Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to provide additional 
financial assistance to women Self-Help Groups under National 
Rural Livelihood Mission in Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Consequent upon commencement of the Viksit Bharat–
Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) 
Act, 2025, the scheme has successfully been implemented in rural 
areas of the entire country w.e.f.  01.07.2026. The VB-G RAM G 
provides for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five 
days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household 
whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work 
against one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment available 
under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The new scheme has been 
successfully implemented in rural areas of Union Territory of Dadra 
and Nagar Haveli also w.e.f. 0.1.07.2026 and an interim allocation Rs. 
9.02 crore has been made for the UT.   
  

Page 2 of 2 
 
Further, under Section 5(4) of the Act, the State/UT 
Governments may make provision for providing additional days of 
employment beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from their 
own resources. 
 
The Act also aims to strengthen sustainable rural livelihoods 
through the creation of durable assets and implementation of the 
permissible works specified in Schedule I of the Act, namely Water-
related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related 
Infrastructure and Special Works to Mitigate Extreme Weather 
Events. These provisions are intended to enhance livelihood security, 
strengthen rural infrastructure and promote sustainable rural 
development. 
 
(c): Funds are allocated by the Central Government under the 
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission 
(DAY-NRLM) for extending livelihood assistance to Self Help Groups 
in the form of capitalisation support (Revolving Funds/RF, Community 
Investment Fund/CIF) as well as for other mission activities. Further, 
based on the utilisation of funds and the assessed needs of the 
States/UTs, additional allocations are provided to them within the 
mission's annual overall budgetary provision. 
 
The detail of capitalization support provided to Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli and Daman and Diu since inception is Rs.980.71 lakhs as on 
31st July 2026. Funds released under DAY-NRLM to Dadra and Nagar

BENEFICIARIES OF NSAP 
 
3820. Shri Asaduddin Owaisi: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that disbursement of 
pensions under the National Social Assistance Programme 
(NSAP) has reportedly been delayed or stopped for a large 
number of beneficiaries since January 2026 due to technical 
issues, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the total number of beneficiaries affected due to delay, rejection 
or non-disbursement of NSAP pension since January 2026 along 
with the reasons identified for the same, States and UT-wise; 
(c)  whether such disruptions were caused due to Aadhaar-related 
issues, DBT/PFMS failures, banking errors, beneficiary data 
mismatches, or any other technical reasons, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d)  the steps taken by the government, including directions issued 
to States and UTs for alternative modes of pension 
disbursement, to ensure that no eligible elderly persons, widows 
and persons with disabilities are denied their pension 
entitlement? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): During the last quarter of FY 2025–26, funds amounting to 
Rs. 3,299.93 crore were released to States/UTs under National Social 
Assistance Programme (NSAP). With effect from 2026–27, funds 
under NSAP are being released through SNA-SPARSH mechanism. 
Under this mechanism, States/UTs with legislature, after onboarding 
on SNA-SPARSH, utilize funds against the Mother Sanction issued by 
the Ministry. The Ministry has issued Mother Sanction amounting to 
Rs. 5572.33 Crore for the first installment of 2026-27 to all the 
States/UTs. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
  
Temporary difficulties in release of payments owing to 
migration of NSAP into SNA-SPARSH were resolved after detailed 
consultation and technical support and release was restored in the 
fourth quarter of 2025-26 with release of Rs. 3,299.93 crore during 
this period.  
  
(c) & (d): At the time of initiation of payment, prescribed system-
based validation checks are carried out to ensure that benefits are 
credited to the intended beneficiaries and to prevent leakages. 
Payment failures, wherever reported, are addressed promptly through 
necessary corrective action by the concerned authorities. States/UTs 
are expected to ensure that no beneficiary is denied his or her 
pension for the reasons that she/he has inactive or frozen bank 
account and/or Aadhaar number or other technical reasons. The 
Ministry extends necessary support to the States/UTs for resolution 
of technical issues. 
  
As per the guidelines of NSAP, the responsibility for 
identification/selection of beneficiaries, verification of applications, 
sanctioning, maintenance/deletion of beneficiary data and last mile 
disbursal of pension to the beneficiaries vests with the respective 
States/UTs. The States/UTs are expected to develop an effective and 
proactive strategy sensitive to the special needs of the beneficiaries 
to ensure that no beneficiary is denied his or her pension.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3821 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES 
  3821. THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the need recognised by the Government to promote sustainable agricultural practices in 
view of increasing concerns regarding soil health, groundwater depletion, climate change 
impacts and long-term sustainability of agricultural production systems; 
(b) the details of schemes and incentives provided by the Government for encouraging 
adoption of organic farming, agroforestry and other environmentally sustainable agricultural 
practices among farmers; 
(c) the programmes proposed by the Government for scaling up sustainable agriculture 
while ensuring productivity enhancement, resource conservation and income security for 
farmers; 
(d) the findings of evaluations conducted by the Government regarding adoption levels of 
such practices and the challenges encountered by farmers in implementing them across 
different regions; and 
(e) the future policy directions envisaged by the Government for integrating sustainability 
with economic viability and strengthening the resilience, competitiveness and long-term 
growth of the agricultural sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): Agriculture is a State subject. The Government is supplementing the efforts of 
State/UT Government for promoting sustainable agriculture through various schemes and 
programs. Under these schemes emphasis is being placed on balanced nutrient 
management, efficient water use, conservation agriculture, integrated farming systems, 
agroforestry, natural and organic farming, and promotion of climate-resilient agricultural 
technologies.  
Under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, assistance is provided to States for 
promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through the judicious use of fertilizers. This 
improves fertilizer use efficiency and promotes balanced nutrient application. 26.18 crore 
Soil Health Cards have been generated so far. To increase water use efficiency at farm level 
through micro irrigation, Government is implementing Per Drop More Crop Scheme.  Under 
the scheme, fertigation is also promoted. This enables application of water-soluble fertilizers 
directly to root zone ensuring precise nutrient delivery. 114.60 lakh hectares has been 
brought under micro-irrigation, benefitting about 100 lakh farmers.  Organic farming is being 
promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) and Mission Organic Value 
Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States. 
Assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer under 
PKVY and MOVCDNER. PKVY has covered 18.93 lakh hectares, benefiting 33.63 lakh 
farmers. MOVCDNER has brought 2.36 lakh hectares under organic farming, benefiting 

2.74 lakh farmers. Agroforestry Scheme is being implemented to encourage integration of 
trees with agricultural crops. To ensure availability of quality planting material, financial 
assistance is provided for setting up of new nurseries and raising of saplings in existing 
nurseries under Agroforestry Scheme. Financial assistance includes ₹16 lakh for setting up 
big nurseries (1 ha), ₹10 lakh for small nurseries (0.5 ha), and up to ₹5 lakh per existing 
nursery for raising saplings is provided under the programme. 826 nurseries have been 
established and about 1062.18 lakh saplings raised in last 3 years. The National Mission on 
Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25.11.24 to promote 
Natural Farming. The Mission strengthens agriculture practices with scientific agro 
ecological approaches for sustainability, climate resilience and safe food. Under NMNF, 
11.81 lakh hectares have been covered in 24,031 clusters, benefiting 24.69 lakh farmers. 
Incentive support on Rs. 4000/ acre for 2 years is given for farmers to practice Natural 
Farming, preparation of natural farming inputs or purchase of inputs from Bio-input 
Resource Centers (BRCs) etc. Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on 
Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) and National Food Security Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) & 
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) promote crop diversification. 
Financial assistance/incentives under the Schemes are provided in accordance with the 
respective operational guidelines of the Schemes.  
The Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 
(PMKSY) to enhance physical access to water on farms, expand cultivable area under 
assured irrigation, improve on-farm water-use efficiency and promote sustainable water 
conservation practices. Under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) component, the schemes of 
Surface Minor Irrigation (SMI) and Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of Water 
Bodies are being implemented by the Department of Water Resources, River Development 
and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. As reported by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, 
Central Assistance is provided to States/UTs for creation and restoration of irrigation 
potential under these schemes. Besides, under Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and 
Ajeevika Mission – Gramin (VB-G RAM-G), being implemented by the Ministry of Rural 
Development, water conservation activities are prioritised through Natural Resource 
Management (NRM) works. These constitute 110 works out of 318 permissible works under 
the programme, improving water security and conservation. 
NITI Aayog has undertaken the evaluation of various schemes being implemented. 
As per the evaluation reports, under Per Drop More Crop Scheme, 62.46% of farmers 
reported a substantial increase in water use efficiency or crop yield. Under the Rainfed Area 
Development Scheme, 70.28% of farmers reported a substantial improvement in farm 
productivity. The study also reported that 63.78% of farmers adopting soil Health Card 
recommendations experienced improved fertilizer use efficiency or crop yield, while 68.5% 
reported improvement in soil health through the use of natural inputs. Under the Organic 
Farming, 75.85% of farmers reported significant improvements in soil fertility, reduced 
chemical input costs, or enhanced produce quality. Under the National Mission on Natural 
Farming, 90.1% of farmers reported reduced input costs compared to the use of chemical 
fertilizers. The report also highlights the positive contribution of MIDH to farm profitability, 
livelihood diversification, and long-term capacity building in the horticulture sector. As per 
the evaluation report, strategic interventions could increase domestic edible oil availability 
to 16 MT by 2030 and 26.7 MT by 2047, strengthening self-sufficiency in oilseeds. 
As reported by Central Ground Water Board, as per the pre-monsoon 2026 
assessment, the groundwater situation remains largely stable across the country. Out of 
9,085 monitoring wells, 87.8% (7,977 wells) fall under the normal category. These findings 
indicate that the interventions are contributing to efficient water management, strengthening 
resource conservation, improving climate resilience and supporting the long-term 
sustainability of agricultural production systems. 

The adoption of sustainable agricultural practices varies across regions depending 
on agro-climatic conditions, availability of irrigation infrastructure, and local resource 
endowments. The Government continues to strengthen sustainable agricultural practices 
through improved irrigation, water conservation, efficient resource management and 
climate-resilient interventions to integrate sustainability with economic viability and enhance 
the resilience, competitiveness and long-term growth of the agricultural sector. Despite the 
challenges posed by biotic and abiotic stresses, the agriculture sector has recorded 
sustained growth in crop productivity and overall agricultural production over the last 
decade. Food grain production has increased from 252.03 million tonnes in 2014–15 to a 
record 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25, while horticulture production has increased from 
280.98 million tonnes in 2014–15 to 370.73 million tonnes in 2024–25, reflecting the 
resilience and steady growth of agricultural production across the country.

REVIEW OF SOIL HEALTH CARD ISSUANCE 
 
3822. DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the total number of Soil Health Cards (SHCs) issued to farmers under the Soil 
Health Card Scheme, State-wise, including Tamil Nadu; 
(b)  the frequency and coverage of soil testing conducted in the last three years, and 
number of farmers receiving recommendations based on soil test results; 
(c)  whether the Government has observed gaps in issuance, renewal, or accuracy of 
SHCs, particularly for small and marginal farmers; 
(d)  the measures being taken to increase awareness among farmers about the use of 
SHCs for optimal fertilizer application and soil nutrient management; 
(e)  whether any follow-up support, training or financial incentives are provided to 
farmers adopting recommendations from SHCs; and 
(f)  the steps being taken to improve digital tracking, laboratory infrastructure, and 
timely delivery of SHCs across all States? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (c): 26.26 crore Soil Health Cards (SHCs) have been generated/issued to farmers 
in the country under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme since inception of the scheme i.e. 
2014-15 till date. State-wise details of issue of SHCs, including Tamil Nadu are at 
Annexure-I. Total 8313 Soil Testing Labs (1267 Static Soil Testing Labs, 168 Mobile Soil 
Testing Labs, 6197 Mini Soil Testing Labs and 681 Village Level Soil Testing Labs) have 
been established under the scheme. During the last three years from 2023-24 to 2025-26, 

2.42 crore soil testing have been conducted and 2.42 crore SHCs have been 
generated/issued to farmers including small & marginal farmers in the country. 
 
(d) & (e): Under the  Scheme, around 7.17 Lakh demonstrations, 130627 farmer’s 
training programmes and 7,425 farmer’s mela have been organized to enable farmers to 
follow recommendations in the SHC. In addition, 70,002 Krishi Sakhis have been trained 
to support farmers in using SHCs among other issues. School soil health programme 
was started in 2023-24, wherein students participates in soil sample collections, testing, 
SHC generation and providing advisory to farmers. Under the programme 2015 soil labs 
have been established in schools to spread awareness of SHC in children & thereby their 
families. SHC also provides recommendations specific for natural farming and organic 
farming. 19.37 lakh soil samples of natural farmers have been collected since, 2025-26 
till date and 14.57 lakh SHCs have been generated thereof. Beneficiary linked schemes 
of agriculture including National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds and Mission for 
Aatmanirbharta in Pulses also encourage farmers to generate SHC and follow the 
recommendations.  
Rural Agriculture Work Experience (RAWE) Programme, a component of the Student 
READY (Rural Entrepreneurship Awareness Development Yojana) provides undergraduate 
agriculture students with practical exposure to village and farming. These students 
disseminate improved agricultural technologies through extension. From 2021–22 to 2025–
26, the programme covered 1,05,329 undergraduate students from 62 agricultural 
universities. Low-cost technologies such as yellow sticky traps, pheromone traps, seed 
treatment, vermicomposting, integrated farming systems etc All these extension activities 
seek to address the gaps in issuance, renewals & use of SHCs by farmers, including small 
& marginal farmers. Soil health & Fertility Scheme covers the cost of SHC, and same is 
provided to the farmers free. Government bears Rs. 300 for generation of each SHC and 
same is provided to farmers free of cost. No financial incentives are provided to farmers 
adopting recommendations from SHCs.  
 
(f): Farmer can digitally track generation of SHC once sample is collected by entering 
mobile number through soil health card portal https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in/soilhealthcard . 
After generation of SHC, it can be also downloaded from the portal. Under the scheme 
financial assistance is provided to states for setting up of soil testing laboratories. Rs. 75 
lakh per laboratory is provided for setting up of static/mobile soil testing laboratory whereas 
Rs. 1.5 lakh is provided for setting up of Village Level Soil Testing Laboratory. Total 8313 
Soil Testing Labs (1267 Static Soil Testing Labs, 168 Mobile Soil Testing Labs, 6197 Mini 
Soil Testing Labs and 681 Village Level Soil Testing Labs) have been established under the 
scheme. Citizen charter has been prepared and issued on 25.10.2023 for timely delivery of 
SHCs to the farmers. As per citizen charter, entire activity of soil sample collection, testing, 
generation of SHC and issue of recommendations to farmers should be completed within 
25 days (30 days in case of hilly & north eastern states) of sample collection.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3823 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST, 2026  
 
AGRICULTURAL INITIATIVES IN TAMIL NADU 
 
3823. SHRI NAVASKANI K: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the progress of area coverage under 
summer crops and the extent of acreage brought under cultivation in Tamil Nadu during 
current summer season and if so, details thereof; 
(b)  the details of area covered under paddy, pulses, oilseeds and maize in Tamil Nadu 
during current summer season as compared to the corresponding period of previous year, 
crop-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has implemented any district-specific initiatives in 
Ramanathapuram district to promote summer crop cultivation through efficient water 
management, climate-resilient agricultural practices and improved extension services and, 
if so, the details thereof; 
 (d)  the measures taken to ensure the timely availability of quality seeds, fertilizers, 
irrigation support and other agricultural inputs to farmers in Ramanathapuram district; and 
(e)  whether any special assistance has been provided to enhance summer crop 
productivity, improve water-use efficiency and increase farmers' income in 
Ramanathapuram district and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE   
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) regularly reviews 
the progress of area coverage under various crops, including summer crops, based on the 
information furnished by the States. The details of area covered during summer season for 
the years 2024-25 and 2025-26 under rice, maize, pulses and oilseeds in Tamil Nadu are 
as under: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
    *As per 3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW 
 
 
 
Crops 
Area in Thousand Ha 
2024-25 2025-26* 
Rice 272.56 227.95 
Maize 3.00 22.71 
Total Pulses 166.59 134.73 
Total Oil Seeds 107.98 87.64 

(c) to (e): The Prime Minister Dhan- Dhanya Krishi Yojana (DDKY) was approved by the 
Union Cabinet on 16th July, 2025 to cover 100 districts, including Ramanathapuram, and 
was formally launched on 11th October 2025. The Scheme aims to enhance agricultural 
productivity, increase adoption of crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices, 
augment post-harvest storage at the panchayat and block levels, improve irrigation 
facilities, and facilitate availability of long-term and short-term credit. The scheme is being 
implemented through convergence of 36 existing schemes across 11 Departments, other 
State schemes and local partnerships with the private sector.  
 
 Ramanathapuram is one of the districts covered under DDKY in Tamil Nadu. District 
Action Plans (DAPs) have been formulated and approved by the District Dhan-Dhaanya 
Krishi Yojana Samiti in consultation with relevant stakeholders. The DAPs are envisaged 
to address district specific agriculture development plan and address the local challenges 
keeping scheme objectives through convergence of the schemes. Ramanathapuram 
District has also formulated the DAPs and initiated activities as per their plans. 
 
 In addition, the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is implementing various 
other Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) in the state of Tamil Nadu. Some of these are: 
 
 The National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) is being implemented in 28 
States including Tamil Nadu and 2 Union Territories (UTs) with the objective of increasing 
the production and productivity of Shree Anna, Rice, Wheat, Coarse Cereals, and 
Commercial Crops (Jute and Sugarcane). Newly released high-yielding, climate-resilient, 
bio-fortified, varieties of crops resistant to insect, pests and diseases are being promoted 
under NFSNM. Flexibility has been given to States / UTs to identify districts with low 
productivity and high production potential. Demonstrations of newly released varieties and 
latest agricultural technologies are also promoted under NFSNM. District specific 
implementation data is maintained by the states.  
 
 The Government ensures timely availability of quality seeds and fertilizers by 
periodically assessing requirement and availability with States/UTs and concerned 
agencies through Zonal Conferences for Agricultural Inputs. To make seeds available at 
affordable prices, financial assistance is provided for seed-related activities including 
distribution of quality seeds, creation of National Seed Reserve, strengthening seed 
infrastructure, farmer trainings, demonstrations and free distribution of minikits of new High 
Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of pulses and Nutri-cereals under schemes such as National 
Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM), National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds 
and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). These interventions enhance productivity and 
help reduce cost of cultivation. Production of seed in public sector is also encouraged to 
ensure availability of quality seeds at affordable prices to farmers. The requirement of 
fertilizers assessed by DA&FW is intimated to the Department of Fertilizers to ensure 
seamless availability of fertilizers before the cropping season starts. Further, DA&FW in 
collaboration with DOF regularly monitors the availability status of the fertilizer across the 
country, including Tamil Nadu, through video conference on weekly basis. 
  

             In Ramanathapuram district, as reported by the State Government, seed farms of 
paddy, millets, pulses, and oilseeds were raised during 2025-26 for production of certified 
seeds from which 770 MT of paddy, 35 MT of millets, 30.26 MT of pulses, and 3.93 MT of 
oilseeds were procured for distribution during 2026-27. So far, 2 MT of paddy, 2 MT of 
millets, 2.26 MT of pulses, and 2.5 MT of oilseeds were distributed to farmers.  Certified 
seed stock of 768 MT of paddy, 33 MT of millets, 28 MT of pulses, and 1.43 MT of oilseeds 
were stocked in Agricultural Extension Centres for distribution to farmers. Green manure 
has been grown in an area of 760 acre, to improve soil health, which is one of the important 
soil health improving practices.  
 
As reported by the State Government, during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season (April 
2026 to September 2026), against the estimated requirement of 6,200 MT of Urea, 1,540 
MT of DAP, 300 MT of MOP and 3,300 MT of Complex fertilisers, the Ramanathapuram 
district has, up to 06.08.2026, received 4,356 MT of Urea, 111 MT of DAP, 105 MT of MOP 
and 172 MT of Complex fertilisers. As on 07.08.2026, the district had an available stock of 
5,484 MT of Urea, 700 MT of DAP, 208 MT of MOP and 2,433 MT of Complex fertilisers, 
against the estimated requirement for August 2026 of 1,140 MT of Urea, 380 MT of DAP, 
30 MT of MOP and 1,700 MT of Complex fertilisers. The available stocks were sufficient to 
meet the district’s requirement, and through continuous monitoring, timely replenishment 
and need-based redistribution, uninterrupted availability of fertilisers has been ensured. 
Consequently, no shortage of fertilisers has been reported by farmers in Ramanathapuram 
district during the current Kharif season. 
 
To ensure that only quality fertilisers are supplied to farmers, annual targets are fixed 
for drawing fertiliser samples from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers. The samples 
are analysed in state-notified Fertiliser Quality Control Laboratories, and department and 
legal action is initiated under the provisions of the Fertiliser (Control) Order, 1985, wherever 
violations are detected. The Department also conducts regular inspections and surprise 
enforcement drives to prevent the sale of non-standard fertilisers, hoarding, black marketing 
and diversion of subsidised fertilisers. Further, fertiliser sales are monitored in real time 
through the DBT-enabled Point of Sale (PoS) system, ensuring transparent distribution and 
uninterrupted availability of quality fertilisers to farmers. 
  
 The Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme is being implemented in the Country, 
including Tamil Nadu, from the year 2015-16, which focuses on enhancing water use 
efficiency at farm level through Micro Irrigation technologies namely Drip and Sprinkler 
irrigation systems. Micro Irrigation helps in water saving as well as reduced fertilizer usage, 
labour expenses, other input costs and overall income enhancement of farmers. Under the 
PDMC Scheme, financial assistance is provided to farmers for installation of micro 
irrigation systems @ 55% and 45% of the unit cost to small & marginal farmers and other 
farmers respectively. From 2015-16 to so far, Central Assistance of Rs. 3229.29 crore has 
been provided to the State of Tamil Nadu for implementation of PDMC Scheme. During 
this period, an area of 13.74 lakh hectare has been covered under Micro Irrigation through 
PDMC in the State of Tamil Nadu which includes 0.13 lakh hectare in Ramanathapuram 
district of the State. As reported by the State Government, an area of 48 ha is covered by 
micro irrigation systems (Sprinkler and Rain gun) to utilize the available water in efficient

3825. SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण  मंũी

(a) the details of pending crop loss compensation owed to chilli and other farmers in

State Government's matching funds;  
(b) the total crop damage assessed in Andhra Pradesh during Kharif 2024 and Rabi 2024-
25, the NDRF or SDRF funds released by the Central Government against this damage, 
and whether the amount released is adequate to compensate affected farmers; and  
(c) the status of coverage for economically critical horticultural crops like banana, chilli, 
under PMFBY, and any proposals by the Ministry for a specialized national horticultural 
crop insurance scheme with affordable premiums for small farmers?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground 
level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures 
in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved items and 
norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the 
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of disaster 
of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial 
Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum for assistance under NDRF submitted by the 
State Government. The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way 
of relief and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed.   
During the financial year 2024-25, the State Government of Andhra Pradesh was 
allocated an amount of Rs.1380.80 crore (Rs.1036.00 crore Central share + Rs.344.80 
crore State share) under SDRF.  Further, an amount of Rs.56.895 crore was released from 
NDRF during 2024-25. Balance available under SDRF with the State is Rs.2085.85 crore.  
An allocation of Rs.6533 crore is provided for Andhra Pradesh under SDRF for the period 
from 2026-27 to 2030-31 (under 16th Finance Commission).    
As informed by the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, crop damage was 
assessed during Kharif 2024 & Rabi 2024-25 to an extent of 15,860.83 Ha. of this, Input 
Subsidy was released to farmers covering 14,460.86 Ha. The details are furnished in the 
Annexure. 

Government has introduced yield based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to farmers suffering crop 
loss/damage arising out of natural calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize 
the income of farmers etc.   
This scheme is voluntary for State/UTs as well as farmers. Further, it is State 
Government’s prerogative to notify districts and crops for implementation, as per the 
provisions of PMFBY. The scheme is being implemented in 25 States/UTs including 
Andhra Pradesh. All willing farmers are eligible to enrol under the scheme. 
      Under this Scheme, majority of the claims are settled within the stipulated timelines 
under the Operational Guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) i.e. 
within 21 days of the receipt requisite yield data from the concerned State Government, 
by the insurance companies. However, during the implementation of PMFBY, some claims 
remained pending, primarily on account of: 
 
a. delay in providing State Government share of claims  
b. incorrect/delayed submission of insurance proposals by banks and unverified bank 
account details of enrolled farmers 
c. discrepancy in yield data & consequent disputes between State Government and 
insurance companies, etc.  
 
  The pending claims on account of these issues are settled after their resolution as per
