GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH & EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3826 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
PRECISION AGRICULTURE 
 
3826.  SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृषि और ककसान कल्याण 
मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any study of international best practices in  
precision agriculture and efficient land -use technologies to enhance productivity and  
sustainability in smallholder farming systems; 
 
(b) the steps being taken to promote the use of technologies such as AI, drones, sensors, 
satellite-based monitoring and precision irrigation among farmers;  
 
(c) whether the Government is considering the adoption of a comprehensive precision 
farming ecosystem to improve productivity on limited land holdings, reduce input costs and 
optimize water and fertilizer use; and  
 
(d) the expected impact of such technologies on farm incomes, climate resilience and  
sustainable agricultural growth in the country? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a): Yes, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has taken up a program of National 
Importance namely, Network Program on Precision Agriculture (ICAR - NePPA) having 16 ICAR 
Research Institutes of different domains. Under this program, technologies are developed using 
sensors, remote sensing at different platforms (ground, airborne -Drone and satellite platforms), 
AI and ICTs in line with international best practices in precision agriculture related to  
• Spatio-temporal monitoring and management of crop and soil health. 
• Sensor based post -harvest quality monitoring and management (of mango, banana, 
pulse and rice, etc). 
• IoT based precision vertical farming for  high valued vegetables under controlled 
environment. 
 

2 
 
 
 
 
• Developed sensor -based monitoring and management of aquatic environment for 
precision aquaculture. 
• Monitoring of livestock health using different IoT enabled sensing for precision livestock. 
 
 ICAR continuously studies, adapts and develops advanced precision agriculture and 
efficient land-use technologies suited to Indian conditions. ICAR Institutes have developed and 
validated technologies such as sensor -based irrigation, IoT-enabled environmental monitoring, 
drone-based spraying, AI-enabled precision planters, remote sensing and GIS applications, drip 
fertigation, poly-mulching, raised-bed cultivation, modified raised and sunken conservation beds, 
agro-aqua land configuration, automated livestock management systems, low -cost protected 
cultivation, hydroponics, aeroponics, agrivoltaic farming, precision subsurface drip irrigation and 
other water-efficient irrigation technologies to improve productivity, resource-use efficiency and 
sustainability in smallholder farming systems. ICAR has developed and demonstrated a tank -
based super -intensive precision shrimp farming system. The technology yields 120 –150 
tonnes/ha/year over three annual cycles and the system integrate smart automation, strict 
biosecurity, and eco-efficient management for all farm sizes. 
 
(b): ICAR is promoting precision agriculture through: 
• Development and validation of AI-, IoT- and ICT-enabled decision support systems for 
crop and natural resource management; 
• Use of drones for crop monitoring, precision input application and crop health 
assessment; 
• Remote sensing, GIS and satellite-based monitoring for crop assessment and resource 
mapping; 
• Sensor and IoT-based irrigation and fertigation systems for efficient water and nutrient 
management; 
• Precision nutrient management using enhanced -efficiency fertilizers, nano -fertilizers 
and biofertilizers; 
• Development of digital tools such as the Dweep Microclimate Monitor and AI -based 
models for water stress assessment and livestock management; 
• Establishment of a Remote Pilot Training Organisation (RPTO) at Dehradun for 
UAV/drone training;  
• Technology demonstrations, farmer training, capacity building and digital advisory 
services through ICAR Institutes, AICRPs and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). 
• AI, sensor and IoT based technologies/equipment/ systems developed for production 
and post production agriculture such as; smart micro -irrigation system utilizing 
automation and sensor networks to optimize water use efficiency,  Variable rate 
fertilizers a pplicator,  AI & IoT enable jute grading system,  SPAD meter 2.0 for 
measuring leaf chlorophyll concentration, IoT System for Monitoring and Control of 
Cold Room, Instrument for Rapid detection of Aflatoxin -B1 in maize, Smart Banana 
Supply Chain: Sensor ba sed monitoring and Bloc -chain enabled Traceability, Digital 
twin-based fruit quality monitoring, AI based Grain Analyzer Software, Artificial 
Intelligence Based Quality Assessment of Rice Seeds, Contamination Measurement 
Techniques using Image Processing i n Seed Cotton,  portable device for non -
destructive and quick ginning percentage measurement based on computer vision and  

3 
 
 
 
 
machine learning etc. and conducted drone demonstrations in an area of 230 ha, 
benefitting 2487 farmers. 
• ICAR institutes use drones and mobile apps to demonstrate AI -driven fertilizer and 
pesticide spraying in some crops to farmers. 
 
 In addition, some of the areas in which ICAR applies artificial intelligence (AI) are: 
  
• Use of drone for collecting water samples for analysis from open -water bodies & 
difficult terrains; distribution of feed & medicines to the culture systems; transportation 
of fish & goods; biomass estimation; health monitoring, etc.   
• Developed IoT-based dissolved oxygen management system. 
• Fisheries resource assessment and predictions in inland open-water under AI and Big 
Data platform. 
• Establishing smart production system and hatchery using automated devices and 
gadgets for enhancing production. 
• Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, drones, and satellite 
imagery—to strengthen early disease warning systems, biosecurity, and overall 
livestock management. The specific initiatives and technical applications deployed for 
livestock protection. 
• Satellite & AI -Based Early Warning Systems: ICAR -National Institute of Veterinary 
Epidemiology and Disease Informatics (NIVEDI) utilizes Geographic Information 
Systems (GIS), satellite spatial datasets, and predictive machine learning models to 
forecast 15 economically important livestock diseases outbreaks up to two months in 
advance, enabling state authorities and farmers to take preventive action. 
• Sensor-Based Health & Reproduction Monitoring: Wearable IoT sensors (such as 
smart neck collars, rumination tags, and leg pedometers) are integrated into herd 
management systems to measure real -time body temperature, rumination activity, 
and estrus cycles, allowing early diagnosis of illness before clinical symptoms surface. 
• Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) scheme to promote adoption of new technologies in 
agriculture and allied sectors including agri -drones through technology assessment, 
demonstration and capacity development among the farmers. The KVKs/ICAR 
Institutes/Agricultural Universities conducted 38,402 Agri -drone demonstrations on 
nutrients, fertilizers, chemicals (insect & pest) applications  in 41,280 ha area. Total 
4,54,083 farmers participated in the Agri -Drone demonstrations and field 
interventions.      
      
(c): Yes. ICAR promotes an integrated  precision farming ecosystem by developing location -
specific technologies for  precision irrigation, nutrient management, protected cultivation, 
mechanization, digital decision support and climate -smart agriculture. These tec hnologies are 
being disseminated through field demonstrations, farmer training, capacity building programmes 
and collaboration with State Departments, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other stakeholders 
to facilitate their adoption by farmers. 
 
 

4 
 
 
 
(d): Precision agriculture technologies have demonstrated significant improvements in 
productivity, profitability, resource -use efficiency and climate resilience. Precision irrigation 
technologies, including solar -powered Jhola Kundi systems, farm ponds and micro -irrigation, 
increased cropping intensity from 137% to 272%, doubled the crop diversification index (0.40 to 
0.80), increased average monthly farmer income from ₹4,644 to ₹19,676, and reduced 
dependence on diesel and ele ctricity while mitigating about 40.5 tonnes of CO ₂ emissions 
annually. At Goa, precision agriculture technologies increased rice and cowpea yields by 4.69% 
and 6.58%, respectively, while reducing irrigation water use by 92.9% and labour  requirement 
by about 95%.  Farm pond -based rainwater harvesting systems increased crop yields by 20 –
55%, while polyhouse cultivation integrated with automated drip irrigation and fertigation 
generated net returns of ₹2.72 lakh per 15 gunta with a B:C ratio of 4.57. In Bihar, integration of 
raised beds, drip fertigation and poly -mulching improved nutrient -use efficiency by 30 –85%. 
Adoption of drip irrigation and protected cultivation reduced irrigation water requirement by 70 –
80%, while hydroponics reduced water use by up to 90%. Drone-based foliar nutrient application 
improved crop yields by 4–5%, reduced spraying costs by about 15%, enabled spraying of one 
acre in about 6 minutes using only 9.5 litres of water and 0.5 litre  of nano -fertilizer, while 
minimizing crop damage and ensuring uniform application. These technologies collectively 
enhance farm income, optimize water and fertilizer use, reduce production costs and support 
sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural growth.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
 The integration of AI, IoT, drones, and satellite imagery enhances livestock management 
by creating proactive early disease warning systems, strengthening biosecurity, and optimizing 
overall farm efficiency include: 
 Predictive Disease Control and Reduced Mortality: AI models and IoT-enabled biometric 
sensors can detect physiological stress and predict potential disease outbreaks 5 –12 days 
before clinical symptoms appear, enabling timely intervention. This can reduce v eterinary 
expenses by 20–40% while preventing large-scale livestock losses. 
 Optimized Productivity and Reproductive Performance: Real -time wearable sensors 
automate estrus detection, improving the success rate of artificial insemination by 15 –30%. In 
addition, smart microclimate control and precision feed management can enhance mi lk yields 
by up to 18%, leading to improved overall livestock productivity.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3827 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Status of Agriculture Infrastructure Projects 
3827.  SHRI CHHATRAPAL SINGH GANGWAR  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  the present status of agriculture infrastructure, warehouse, cold storage and value 
addition projects in Uttar Pradesh and Bareilly district particularly under Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund and other Central Schemes; 
(b)  the details of the benefits accrued to the farmers and improvement in agricultural  
marketing facilities as a result of these Schemes; and 
(c)  whether any additional initiative is proposed by the Government to promote agro- 
processing and agricultural exports in Bareilly district ? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 (a) to (c) : Agriculture is a State subject. However, the Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the State Governments including Uttar Pradesh for development of agriculture 
infrastructure, warehouses, cold storage and other value addition projects through policy 
support, budgetary assistance and various schemes/programmes. The Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund (AIF) of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, facilitates 
medium and long-term financing for the creation of post-harvest infrastructure at the farm-gate 
and viable farming assets such as warehouses, cold storages, processing units, godowns and 
logistics facilities through eligible lending institutions. The scheme provides loans at an interest 
rate capped at 9% with 3% interest subvention and credit guarantee coverage up to ₹2 crore. 
Under AIF, total 16,994 projects have been sanctioned in Uttar Pradesh, with a 
cumulative loan amount of ₹9,799.04 crore and investment mobilisation of ₹16,736.74 crore. 
The approved projects include 1,295 Warehouses, 905 Cold Storage and Cold Chain projects, 
4,588 primary processing centers, 2,449 Custom Hiring Centers and 5,039 farm/harvest 
automation projects. In Bareilly District, 786 agriculture infrastructure projects have been 
approved under  AIF with a cumulative loan amount of ₹565.73 crore and total project cost of 
₹993.08 crore. The approved projects include 367 Farm/Harvest Automation projects, 169 

  
 
 
Primary Processing Centers, 32 Warehouses, 17 Cold Storage and Cold Chain projects, and 
37 Custom Hiring Centers. 
As per Impact Assessment Study of Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) conducted by 
Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmadabad in 2025, the scheme has improved access to 
finance for agricultural enterprises, including small and marginal farmers, entrepreneurs and 
established agri-businesses. It has resulted in improved price realization and an upward shift of 
the beneficiaries in the agri-value chain. According to the study, each AIF unit on an average 
supports a minimum of 12-13 direct jobs during peak season, 6 during lean months and 19 
indirect jobs through backward and forward linkage such as logistics, marketing, repairs, 
packaging and ancillary input services. Interventions under the AIF have resulted in an average 
reduction of 5-15% in post-harvest losses driven by improved storage, processing and 
mechanization systems that enhance efficiency and reduce spoilage across commodities. The 
beneficiaries surveyed reported income gains ranging from 11-15 %.  Further as per the study, 
the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) has strengthened farm-gate infrastructure and 
improved mechanisation. It has addressed gaps in storage, processing, logistics, and market 
linkages by supporting a wide range of infrastructure projects for different types of beneficiaries.  
In addition to AIF, the Integrated Scheme for Agriculture Marketing (ISAM) of the 
Department supports state governments through creation and improvement of market 
structures, capacity building and generating access to market information through sub 
schemes namely Agriculture Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) and e-NAM (National Agriculture 
Market).  
Under the Agriculture Marketing Infrastructure (AMI), creation of post-harvest 
marketing infrastructure including storage/ modern warehouses infrastructure is promoted 
across the country including Uttar Pradesh.  Under the scheme, subsidy @ 33.33% for NER, 
hilly area, Women/SC/ST promoters, PACS & FPOs etc. and @25% for others is provided for 
eligible projects.   In Uttar Pradesh, total 1,343 storage projects with a cumulative storage 
capacity of 63,08,971 MT have been supported with subsidy of ₹204.17 crore  under the 
scheme .This includes  36 storage projects with a cumulative storage capacity of 3,18,907.319 
MT and subsidy of ₹6.78 crore in Bareilly District.    
Under e-NAM, the all-India electronic trading (e-trading) portal links existing physical 
agricultural marketing committees (APMCs) through a virtual platform to create a unified 
national market for agricultural commodities. The portal serves as a single window for all 
information and services related to APMCs, including arrivals of commodities, quality and 
price, provisions for responding to buy-sell proposals, trade proposals, and other services 
such as direct electronic payment settlement into farmers' accounts. Under this scheme, in 
Uttar Pradesh 162 mandis have been connected through the e-NAM platform out of these 3 
are in Bareilly District.   

  
 
 
Further, the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) which 
promotes holistic growth of the horticulture sector, also provides support for creation of post-
harvest management (PHM) and marketing infrastructure for better price realization of 
horticulture produce. In Uttar Pradesh, since the inception of the scheme, 2788 units including 
pack houses, cold storage units, refrigerated vans, primary processing units, ripening 
chambers, pre-cooling units attached to cold storages and mobile pre-cooling units have been 
established in Uttar Pradesh under the scheme. 
The National Horticulture Board (NHB) is also implementing the credit-linked back-
ended subsidy scheme to promote creation of modern infrastructure across the horticulture 
value chain, including production, post-harvest management, and scientific storage of 
horticultural produce. Financial assistance ranging from 35% to 50% of the eligible project cost 
is provided for establishing commercial horticulture projects such as protected cultivation, 
pack houses, grading and packing units, primary processing units, ripening chambers, and 
reefer vehicles. Assistance is also provided for the establishment and modernization of Cold 
Storages, Controlled Atmosphere (CA) Storages, and Onion Storages with a capacity 
exceeding 5,000 metric tonnes at the rate of 35% of the eligible project cost, which is enhanced 
to 50% for North Eastern, Hilly and Scheduled Areas. These interventions strengthen post-
harvest infrastructure, reduce post-harvest losses, improve storage and marketing facilities, 
and enable better price realization for horticultural produce. 
The National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oil Seeds also supports post-harvest 
management, processing and value addition. The Mission promotes investment in oil 
extraction by providing financial assistance for the establishment of oil mills and extraction 
units at 33% of the project cost, subject to a maximum assistance of ₹9.90 lakh per unit, 
thereby fostering the growth of agro-based industries. During 2025–26, financial assistance 
was provided for the establishment of 400 oil mills under the Mission.  Under NMEO-Oilseeds, 
5 seed hubs and 3 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned in Uttar Pradesh.  
Further, 2 oil mills have also been established in the State. 
The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) incentivizes setting up/expansion 
of food processing infrastructure through its Central Sector Umbrella Scheme - Pradhan Mantri 
Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY); Central Sector Scheme - Production Linked Incentive 
Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) and Centrally Sponsored Scheme - PM 
Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME). These schemes are demand 
driven and are implemented across the country including Uttar Pradesh. Under Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), financial assistance is provided to entrepreneurs 
for setting up of food processing industries. In Uttar Pradesh, under the scheme, a total of 103 
projects have been approved with the project cost of ₹ 2007.98 crore including 9 projects with 
the project cost of ₹ 82.28 crore in Bareilly District. The Production Linked Incentive Scheme 

  
 
 
for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) is, inter alia, intended to support creation of global 
food manufacturing champions and support Indian brands of food products in international 
market. In Uttar Pradesh, under the scheme, 26 proposals under different categories are 
operational having a committed investment of ₹ 1052.1 crore.Under Pradhan Mantri 
Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, financial, technical

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3829 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11th August, 2026 
 
AGRICULTURAL INPUT COSTS AND MSP 
 
3829. DR. M K VISHNU PRASAD: 
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the increase in MSP has kept pace with the rising cost of cultivation;  
(b) whether the Government has assessed the sharp increase in the prices of 
fertilizers, pesticides, seeds, diesel, electricity, and labour over the last five years;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide direct input subsidies to small and 
marginal farmers; and  
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी      (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the 
recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after 
considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments 
concerned. 
While recommending MSP every season in a year, CACP considers important 
factors like cost of production, overall demand-supply situation of various crops in 
domestic and world markets, domestic and international prices, inter-crop price 
parity, terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural sector, likely effect of 
price policy on rest of the economy and a minimum of 50 percent as the margin over 
cost of production. 
  

Within the cost of production, CACP considers all costs in a comprehensive 
manner which include all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired 
human labour, bullock labour/ machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses 
incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, diesel, electricity, 
manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest 
on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous 
expenses and imputed value of family labour.  
 
(c) & (d): The Government is implementing several schemes and programmes to 
provide income support to farmersand toincrease agricultural productivity, reduce the 
cost of cultivation, promote crop diversification, ensure remunerative returns. These 
various schemes / programmes cover the entire spectrum of agriculture including 
credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, seeds, 
mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, 
extension activities, procurement of crops, digital agriculture etc.

AMRITSAR TEXTILE CLUSTER 
 
3830.  SHRI GURMEET SINGH MEET HAYER: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details of specific schemes being implemented to preserve, modernize, and promote the 
traditional textile industry, including the woollen and shawl -weaving segments in Amritsar, 
Punjab;  
(b) the details of the funds allocated and spent for the Amri tsar textile cluster during the last ten 
years scheme and year-wise; and  
(c) the details of future action plan and infrastructure development strategies formulated by the 
Government to enhance the global competitiveness of this border-district textile hub? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (c):    The Government of India has implemented various schemes for modernization 
and promotion of the traditional textile industry including the woollen and shawl -weaving 
segments across the country including Amritsar, Punjab. The major schemes include Scheme 
for Integrated Textile Park (SITP) for setting up textile parks with state of the art 
infrastructure in textile hubs; Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme focusing on Man -
Made Fibre (MMF) Fabric, MMF Apparel and Technical Textiles to boost large scale 
manufacturing and enhancing competitiveness; National Technical Textiles Mission 
(NTTM) focusing on Research & Innovation in the field of specialty fibres and technical 
textile, indigenous development of machinery and creating human resources with requisit e 
skills; SAMARTH -Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector with the objective of 
providing demand driven, placement oriented, skilling program; Amended Technology 
Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS); Integrated Wool Development Programme (IWDP) for 
the d evelopment of Wool Sector, National Handloom Development Programme; Raw 
Material Supply Schemes; and National Handicraft Development Programme. 
  
In order to protect and promote traditional textiles and handicrafts, the Textiles Committee 
under Ministry of Textiles is facilitating registration of unique textiles and handicrafts of the 
country under Geographical Indications Act, 1999. As a part of this, an initiative is 
undertaken for the protection and promotion of the traditional Amritsar Shawl of Punjab b y 
filing an application for registration under the Geographical Indications of Goods 

(Registration and Protection) Act, 1999. The initiative is aimed at preserving the traditional 
craftsmanship, strengthening the identity of Amritsar Shawls, and enhancing their 
marketability and value.  
  
The Ministry through Central Wool Development Board has been implementing "Integrated 
Wool Development Programme" (IWDP) during the period of 15th Finance Commission with 
total allocation of Rs 125.99 crore for the develop ment of Wool Sector in all major wool 
producing States/Union Territories(UTs) with the help of States/UTs Govts.  
  
In order to promote ease of doing business in the country to achieve the vision of generating 
employment and promoting exports through "Make  in India", Amended Technology 
Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS) is implemented across the country including the state of 
Punjab to provide credit linked Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS) to units for purchase of 
benchmarked machinery in different segments of  Textile Sectors. The scheme aims at 
augmenting of investment, productivity, quality, employment, exports along with import 
substitution in the textile industry. Under ATUFS scheme, 70 cases have been settled and 12.9 
Cr. Capital investment subsidy has bee n released to units located in Amritsar, Punjab during 
the year 2018 to 2024. The details of year -wise subsidy released under  ATUFS scheme is as 
under: 
                 (Rs. in Cr) 
Year Subsidy Released 
2018 0.11 Cr 
2019 0.03 Cr 
2020 2.83 Cr 
2021 2.19 Cr 
2022 4.70 Cr 
2023 1.21 Cr 
2024 1.83 Cr 
Total 12.9 Cr 
  
With a view to increasing investments, generating employment opportunities and boosting 
exports in textile sector, the Ministry is implementing Scheme for Integrated Textile Park 
(SITP) to provide subsidy for setting up textile parks with world -class, state -of-the-art 
infrastructure in textile hubs across the country. Under SITP Scheme, 3 Textile parks have 
been taken up in Punjab with details as below- 
  
S. 
No Name of the park District Funds Released 
(₹ in crore) 
1 Lotus Integrated Tex Park Barnala 40.00 
2 Rhythm Textile & Apparel Park Ltd Nawanshehar 36.00 
3 Ludhiana Integrated Textile Park Ltd Ludhiana 36.00 

  
Samarth (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textiles Sector) of Ministry of Textiles provides 
demand driven, placement oriented skilling programmes to supplement the efforts of the 
Indian textile industries in creating jobs in the organized textile and related sectors, covering 
the entire value chain of textiles, excluding Spinning and Weaving in organized sector, on pan 
India basis. A total of 4,737 beneficiaries have been trained (passed) in the State of Punjab. 
  
Under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and Raw Material Supply 
Schemes (RMSS) in Handloom sector, finan cial assistance is provided to eligible handloom 
agencies/workers for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms & accessories, solar 
lighting units, construction of workshed, skilling, product diversification & design innovation, 
technical and common in frastructure, publicity and brand development through India 
Handloom Brand (IHB), Handloom Mark (HLM) and GI tag , e -commerce facilities, 
marketing of handloom products in domestic/overseas markets, concessional loans under 
weavers’ MUDRA scheme and social security etc.  
  
The Government is implementing various schemes and initiatives to boost the Indian textile 
and apparel sector and enhance its competitiveness. The major schemes/initiatives include 
Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) Sche me; Remission of Duties and 
Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme; Export Promotion Mission (EPM), 
comprising Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha; and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Exporters 
(CGSE). 
  
The Government has also adopted a focused export -promotion and market -diversification 
strategy covering 40 priority countries. The Sixteen Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) which are 
in force, including the India –United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade 
Agreement (CETA); and the concluded FTAs with the Euro pean Union (EU) and New 
Zealand provide an opportunity for Indian textiles and apparel sector to enhance their exports 
and undertake market diversification. 
The Government of India launched RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export 
Facilitation) on 19 March 2026 under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) to support 
exporters affected by disruptions arising from the West Asia/Middle East conflict and 
maritime challenges in the Gulf region.  
  
Customs duty on imports of cotton falling under Chapter 5201 has been temporarily exempted 
from 1 June to 31 October 2026 to augment domestic availability. Further, the Government 
has approved the Mission for Cotton Productivity for the period 2026 –27 to 2030 –31 to 
address key bottlenecks, improve productivity growth, and resolve quality-related concerns in 
India’s cotton sector.

(b) to (d)  The Spices Board, under the “Sustainability in Spice Sector through

board provide support for infrastructure development for processing and value addition, 
setting up/upgradation of in-house laboratories, common processing and warehousing

During 2021-22 to 2025-26, 2,95,600 samples from export consignments of chilli were

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3832 
ANSWERED ON 11th AUGUST, 2026 
Functioning of Service Cooperative Societies 
3832. Shri Vijay Baghel: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it has come to the notice of the Government that in the Service Cooperative 
Societies functioning under the District Cooperative Bank, Durg, the records relating 
disbursement of agricultural loans, distribution of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs are 
being maintained both online and offline, thereby causing difficulties to society employees as 
well as farmers; 
(b) if so, the reasons for such dual record -keeping (online and offline) and the steps taken by 
the Government to eliminate this practice; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to make all operations in the Service Cooperative 
Societies fully online, in line with the existing banking system, and to dispense with the 
mandatory maintenance of offline records; and 
(d) if so, the proposed timeline in this regard and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
  
(a) to (d)          As per the information provided by Registrar of Cooperative Societies, 
Government of Chhattisgarh, across 311 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in the 
Durg, Balod, and Bemetara districts under the jurisdiction of the District Cooperative Central 
Bank Ltd., Durg, operations related to agricultural loans, fertilizers, seed distribution, and 
auditing are conducted via an online system. However, due to certain administrative and 
statutory requirements, as well as server network issues, the manual maintenance of some 
records and registers remains necessary.  
  
  To address the challenges associated with the physical maintenance of loan disbursement 
and agricultural input -related registers, the Ministry of Cooperation launched the PACS 
Computerization Project in 2022. One of the key objectives of the project is to enable PACS 
to carry out their business operations through an ERP -based Common National Software, 
thereby eliminating the need for manual maintenance of records. 
  

Page 2 of 2 
 
  The implementation of the PACS Computerization Project encompasses online 
maintenance of records, transparent accounting, seamless reconciliation with District Central 
Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), expeditious loan 
processing, reduced transaction costs, and enhanced service delivery to members. 
  
The sun-set date of the project is 31 March 2027.

 3834. SHRI KULDEEP INDORA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed that the climate, temperature and 
agricultural conditions of Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh closely resemble those areas 
of Madhya Pradesh where large-scale successful cultivation of dragon fruit is being 
carried out; 
(b) whether it has come to the notice of the Government that dragon fruit is a high-
value crop grown with minimal water requirement, which could be suitable for this 
region, if so, the details thereof 
(c) whether the Government is considering to encourage cultivation of dragon fruit in 
Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh by providing scientific studios, pilot projects, 
demonstration plots, quality planting material training, subsidy and marketing support, 
and 
(d) if so, the details and time-frame thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (d):  Agriculture is a State subject. The assessment of location-specific climatic 
suitability for the cultivation of crops is undertaken by the concerned State 
Government. As reported by the Government of Rajasthan, climatic conditions of Sri 
Ganganagar-Hanumangarh does not closely resembles with Madhya Pradesh. As in 
Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh area the soil is sandy, high warm wind velocity in 
summers, temperature shoots up to 48 degree Celsius for long duration in summers 
and temperature dips below 0 degree Celsius in winters. Dragon fruit performs well in 
warm conditions specially when the average temperature remains between 20-30 
degree Celsius. The temperature above 38-40 degree Celsius for prolonged period 
can cause sunburn, stem damage, poor flowering and reduced fruit development. The 
crop is also frost sensitive. Therefore, Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh area may not 
suitable for dragon fruit cultivation. 

 
       Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is implementing the Mission for 
Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) for holistic development of the 
horticulture sector, including promotion of high-value fruit crops such as dragon fruit, 
based on agro-climatic suitability and the Annual Action Plan approved by the State 
Government. Under MIDH, assistance is available to the States including State of 
Rajasthan for promotion of dragon fruit through need-based interventions. These 
interventions include area expansion under fruit crops, including dragon fruit, and the 
production and distribution of quality planting material through accredited nurseries. 
Crop-specific Centres of Excellence are established for the production of quality 
planting material. Demonstrations of improved technologies, improved cultivation 
practices and protected cultivation technologies are undertaken. Capacity building, 
training, exposure visits and skill development programmes are organised for farmers. 
Assistance is also provided for the establishment of post-harvest management 
infrastructure. The Post-Harvest Management and Centre of Excellence components 
under MIDH are demand/entrepreneur-driven and Government assistance in the form 
of credit-linked back-ended subsidy is available through the State Horticulture 
Missions. However, no separate proposal specifically for promotion of dragon fruit 
cultivation in Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh districts has been received from the 
Government of Rajasthan under MIDH.

MODERNISATION AND CAPACITY EXPANSION OF BHILAI STEEL PLANT 
  
 
3836.  SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
  
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to modernise and expand the production 
capacity of the Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP) under the National Steel Policy; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the estimated investment, implementation 
timeline and expected increase in production capacity; 
 
(c) the steps taken to enhance the production of value-added steel and improve 
operational efficiency at BSP; and 
 
(d) the impact of the proposed expansion on employment generation and industrial 
development in Chhattisgarh? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(d):     Steel is a deregulated sector. Decisions regarding modernization and 
expansion of production capacity are taken by the concerned steel company based on 
techno-commercial considerations, commercial viability, market demand, and the 
availability of resources.  
Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) has approved the expansion of the Bhilai 
Steel Plant (BSP) from 6.8 MTPA to 10.2 MTPA crude steel capacity.  
To enhance the production of value-added steel and improve operational 
efficiency, Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP) has undertaken various steps which includes 
technology upgradation, modernization of production facilities, digitalization, process 
optimization, energy efficiency measures and increased focus on the production of 
value-added steel for strategic sectors.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3837 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11TH AUGUST 2026 
 
ADVANCES IN AGRICULTURE TECHNOLOGY 
 
3837. SHRI V K SREEKANDAN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether advances in agriculture technology have made tremendous inroads into the 
agricultural sector; 
(b) whether it is true that this has helped in enhancing production manifold and creating 
innovative solutions to modern farming challenges; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that mechanisation of harvesting of horticulture crops 
continued to pose a challenge; 
(d) whether agriculture now stands as a multidisciplinary field with mechanical, 
automation and computing engineers all playing a big role in the mechanisation 
process; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी        (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Advancements in agricultural technology have significantly transformed the 
agriculture sector by enhancing productivity, improving resource-use efficiency, reducing 
the cost of cultivation, minimizing labour drudgery and promoting climate-resilient farming 
practices.  Modern technologies such as improved farm machinery, precision agriculture, 
drones, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, sensors, remote 
sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), satellite-based applications, automation 
and digital technologies are increasingly integrated into agricultural operations. 
 
  The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is promoting agricultural 
mechanization through the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), which is 
being implemented as a component of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme "Rashtriya Krishi 
Vikas Yojana (RKVY)". Financial assistance is provided to farmers for the purchase of 
agricultural machinery and equipment, establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), 
High-Tech Hubs, Farm Machinery Banks (FMBs) and for demonstration, training, testing 
and capacity building relating to agricultural mechanization. These interventions enable 
small and marginal farmers to access modern farm machinery at affordable rates. 
 
  The Department is also promoting the use of agricultural drones by providing 
financial assistance for drone procurement and demonstrations under the SMAM. Drone 
technology is being utilized for pesticide and nutrient application and generation of digital 
agricultural data thereby improving efficiency and reducing input costs. 
 

  To promote precision agriculture and digital technologies, the Department is 
implementing the Digital Agriculture Mission under which digital public infrastructure, 
technology-based farmer-centric services and data-driven decision support systems are 
being deployed for improving agricultural planning and delivery of services. The Farmer 
Registry created under AgriStack is designed to serve as a foundational database for the 
efficient, transparent and targeted delivery of agricultural services and benefits. It is 
envisaged to facilitate integration with various farmer-centric schemes and digital 
platforms, including PM-KISAN, the Jan Samarth platform for Kisan Credit Card (KCC) 
loans, and MSP-based crop procurement systems. As on 06.08.2026, a total of more than 
10.33 crore farmers IDs have been generated. Further, the Digital Crop Survey, i.e., 
survey to digitally capture crops being grown on every farmland in the country with photos 
and geo-tags, has enabled plot-level visibility of crops and better estimation of areas sown 
across seasons, which in turn supports evidence-based planning for production 
estimation, procurement, input supply and logistics management. In Kharif 2025, the 
Digital Crop Survey (DCS) has been conducted in 604 Districts covering more than 28.5 
crores plots. BharatVistaar (Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources) 
is a multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for 
Agriculture. The platform provides farmers with AI-enabled, real-time and location-specific 
agricultural advisories and access to Government schemes and agricultural support 
services. To date, the platform has served over 5.9 lakh farmers and addressed more than 
93 lakh farmer queries. 
 
  Research, design, development, testing and refinement of agricultural machinery 
are undertaken through the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), State 
Agricultural Universities (SAUs) and other research organizations. These institutions have 
developed location-specific and crop-specific machinery suitable for diverse agro-climatic 
conditions and varying farm sizes. 
 
(c): Mechanization of harvesting in horticultural crops is being promoted through the 
development and dissemination of crop-specific harvesting technologies suitable for 
diverse horticultural crops, taking into account variations in crop characteristics, plant 
architecture, fruit maturity, farm sizes and the need to minimize mechanical damage while 
maintaining produce quality. Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture 
(MIDH), financial assistance is provided to States/UTs for the adoption of improved 
horticultural tools, implements and machinery including equipment required for 
horticultural operations. In addition, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) 
and its institutes undertake research and development to develop, refine and evaluate 
appropriate mechanization technologies for horticultural crops, which are disseminated to 
farmers through demonstrations, training and extension programmes. 
 
(d) & (e): Agriculture has increasingly evolved into a multidisciplinary field involving 
agricultural, mechanical, electrical, electronics, automation, instrumentation, computer 
and data science engineers. Integration of engineering, computing, robotics, Machine 
Learning, AI, IoT, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), GIS, remote sensing and 
data analytics has accelerated the development of intelligent farm machinery, 
autonomous equipment, precision farming systems, protected cultivation technologies 
and smart farm management solutions. 
 
  The Government continues to promote innovation, research, technology 
development, skill development, entrepreneurship and adoption of modern agricultural 
technologies through its various schemes and programmes so as to enhance productivity, 
improve resource-use efficiency, strengthen sustainability, and make Indian agriculture 
more resilient and competitive.

ABSENCE OF ELECTED LEGISLATIVE BODY 
 
†3838.     SHRI PATEL UMESHBHAI BABUBHAI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that due to the absence of an elected 
legislative body in  Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, the 
participation of local public representatives in  administrative and 
development decision-making processes is limited; 
 
(b) whether the Government is considering to constitute 
Development/Advisory Territorial  Council with adequate representation of 
Members of Parliament, Zila Panchayats, Municipalities  and other elected 
representatives to strengthen democratic participation; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to empower the said Council with 
mandatory consultation rights regarding prioritization of development 
schemes, review of major projects and key administrative decisions; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has studied the administrative models of other 
Union Territories and formulated any policy regarding providing Rajya Sabha 
representation and greater democratic self-governance to Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli and Daman and Diu, if so, the details  thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) The Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu has 
geographical area of 603 square km and population of 5,86,956 as per Census 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3838 FOR 11.08.2026  
2011. The Union Territory has adequate democratic mechanism to ensure 
participatory governance. The  Union Territory is represented in the Lok 
Sabha through 02 elected Members of Parliament. In accordance with the 
provisions of 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment, the Union Territory has 
two-tier panchayat system in ru ral areas and municipal councils in urban 
areas.  
 
 The elected local bodies, constituted under the “ The Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012” play a significant 
role in local governance, development planning and implementation of 
welfare and developmental programmes. The Sarpanches of Gram 
Panchayats have been vested with adequate finan cial powers under " The 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayats (Application of Funds 
and Maintenance of Accounts) Rules - 2024".  
 
(b) to (d) No such proposal is under consideration of the Ministry at 
present.

MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3839 
  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
ROAD PROJECTS UNDER PMGSY 
 
3839. Smt. June Maliah: 
 Shri Shafi Parambil: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of roads sanctioned, completed and under construction 
under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) during the 
last five years, State and district-wise including Kerala; 
(b)  the total funds allocated, released and utilised for the Scheme 
during the said period, State and district-wise including Kerala; 
(c)  whether any projects have been delayed and the reasons for that, if 
so, the reasons therefor and the action taken against defaulting 
contractors, State-wise; and 
(d)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely completion of 
all pending rural road projects, State-wise including Kerala? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
  
(a): Since the Financial Year 2021-22 till 06.08.2026, a total of 18,807 
road works covering 98,505 km length and 3661 number of bridges have 
been sanctioned across the States/UTs, including the state of Kerala 
under the various verticals of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana 
(PMGSY). During this period, a total of 23,247 road works covering 1, 
34,751 km length (including the road length sanctioned in previous years) 
and 5,287 number of bridges have been completed by the States/UTs 
including the state of Kerala. As on 06.08.2026, a total of 12,447 road 
works of 41,368 km length and 1775 number of bridge works are at 
various stages of construction in the States/UTs including the state of 
Kerala. Further, the State wise, District-wise and Parliamentary 
Constituency-wise details of PMGSY projects may be accessed at the 
programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb on a real-time 
basis. 
 

(b): The fund for implementation of PMGSY is released by the Ministry 
to the States/UTs as a whole and not district-wise. Further, the funds are 
released on the basis of works in hand, the progress achieved in the 
project and after due submission of necessary documents. The fund 
release under PMGSY is through the SNA SPARSH system. Accordingly, 
the details of funds released and expenditure incurred by the States/UTs 
including the state of Kerala during the last five years and the current 
year are given in the Annexure.  
 
(c): In the state of Kerala, 134 road works of 699 km length has been 
sanctioned under PMGSY-III during the last five years. The Government 
has extended the timeline for completion of PMGSY-III works up to March 
2028. Accordingly, the state has been advised to expedite the ongoing 
works and ensure their completion within the stipulated timeline. In 
cases where delay is attributable to the contractor, action is taken by 
the concerned State/UT in accordance with the provisions of the 
Standard Bidding Document (SBD)/contract agreement, which, inter alia, 
provides for issuance of notices, levy of liquidated damages and 
termination of contract in cases of fundamental breach. 
To ensure completion of the balance works within the revised time 
frame, regular review meetings are conducted at the State/UT, regional 
and national levels and progress of implementation is closely monitored. 
Issues affecting project execution are reviewed on a case-to-case basis 
and necessary interventions are undertaken in coordination with all 
concerned stakeholders to facilitate their timely resolution.  
  
(d): The implementation of PMGSY is monitored through a multi-tier 
mechanism to ensure the timely completion of works, quality 
maintenance and improved accessibility of rural roads including in the 
state of Kerala. The major measures taken by the Ministry include: 
 Fixing annual physical and financial targets for achievements and 
reviewing progress regularly with States/UTs. The achievements of 
States/UTs are regularly monitored by way of Regional Review 
Meetings (RRMs), Performance Review Committee (PRC) meetings, 
monthly review meetings and Pre-Empowered/Empowered 
Committee meetings with the States/UTs. The State/UT 
Governments are also advised to convene meetings with the 
concerned authorities to expedite matters relating to land issues, 
forest and wildlife clearances in order to expedite completion of 
works.  
 Monitoring is undertaken through the Online Management, 
Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS), supported by geo-
tagged photographs and GIS-based inspections. 
 To ensure timely implementation of works, the States/UTs are also 
prescribed to adhere to the timelines for tendering and award of 
works from the date of sanction of the works by the Ministry. 

 Adopting a three-tier quality management mechanism comprising 
Programme Implementation Units (PIUs), State Quality Monitors 
(SQMs), and National Quality Monitors (NQMs) to ensure adherence 
to prescribed technical specifications. 
 Electronic Maintenance of PMGSY roads (e-MARG), an online 
platform, has been implemented in all the States/UTs to monitor 
maintenance of PMGSY works for five years from the date of 
completion (i.e. under Defect Liability Period- DLP). Consequent 
upon the introduction of e-MARG, a software module for monitoring 
maintenance and payments to the contractor during the defect 
liability period, such payments to contractors have been made 
commensurate with the quality of roads through a performance-
based contract management system. 
These measures are being implemented uniformly across all States/UTs, 
including the state of Kerala, to improve rural connectivity and ensure 
the creation and maintenance of durable all-weather rural roads.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3840 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
 
PROMOTION OF TEXTILE INDUSTRY IN MADHYA PRADESH 
 
3840#.  Smt. Anita Nagarsingh Chouhan: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the projects approved for promotion of the textile industry in Madhya Pradesh under 
the PM MITRA Mega Textile Parks Scheme are being implemented;  
(b) if so, the details and current status thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has any special proposal to promote the textile and apparel industry, 
textile clusters, garment manufacturing units, and handloom and tribal textile crafts in Ratlam -
Jhabua and Alirajpur Lok Sabha Constituencies;  
(d) whether any special initiative is being taken under the PM MITRA Sc heme for skill 
development of youth, women and tribal artisans, attracting investment and generating 
employment; and  
(e) if so, the details thereof and the proposed investment, expected employment generation and 
future action plan for Madhya Pradesh, particularly in Ratlam, Jhabua and Alirajpur? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) & (b):  To develop integrated large scale and modern industrial infrastructure facility for 
entire value-chain of the textile industry, the Government has approved setting up of 7 (Seven) 
PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks in Greenfiel d/Brownfield 
sites with scheme outlay of Rs. 4,445 Crore for the period 2021 -22 to 2027-28. The Government 
has finalised 7 sites including one in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh for setting up PM MITRA Parks. 
So far, investment interests of ₹ 20,126 crore have been r eceived and GoI share of ₹ 50 
crore has been released to the park during FY 2025-26. 
Current Status of the project is as under; 
 Foundation stone laid on 17th September, 2025 by Hon’ble Prime Minister. 
 100% land acquired, Environmental Clearance (EC) received. 
 Joint Venture agreement signed between central and state government. SPV incorporated. 
 Land has been transferred in name of SPV. 
 A DPR worth Rs. 2,063 Crore for PM MITRA Park Madhya Pradesh has been approved. 

 EPC Contract for core infrastructure has been awarded and work has started on the site. 
So far, expenditure of ₹61.62 crore has been made. 
(c): The Ministry of Textiles is administering following schemes to promote handloom sector 
and welfare of handloom workers across the country including Madhya Pradesh: 
  
1. National Handloom Development Programme(NHDP); 
2. Raw Material Supply Scheme(RMSS); 
  
Under the above schemes, financial assistance is provided to eligible handloom 
agencies/workers for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms & accessories, solar lighting 
units, construction of workshed, skilling, product diversification & design innovation, technical 
and common infrastructure, publicity and brand development through India Handloom Brand 
(IHB), Handloom Mark (HLM) and GI tag, e -commerce facilities, marketing of handloom 
products in domestic/overseas markets, concessional loans under weavers’ MUDRA scheme and 
social security etc. 
(d) & (e):  There is a provision for dedicated Skill Development Centre under PM MITRA 
Scheme. Ministry  of Textiles through SAMARTH (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textiles 
Sector) provides demand driven, placement -oriented skilling programmes to supplement the 
efforts of the Indian textile industries in creating jobs in the organized textile and related s ectors, 
covering the entire value chain of textiles, excluding Spinning and Weaving in organized sector, 
on pan India basis. As on 05.08.2026, a total of 24,959 beneficiaries trained (pass) in the State of 
Madhya Pradesh. Ministry of Textiles along with ot her concerned central Ministries and 
respective State Government are in process of taking various initiative of skill development for 
the youth and women of districts including Dhar and nearby districts.  
PM MITRA Park, in Dhar  Madhya Pradesh is expected to generate employment for 
approx. 3 lakh people (1 lakh direct and 2 lakh indirect) upon completion including for persons 
from Dhar and nearby districts in Madhya Pradesh.

PROMOTING ENTREPRENEURSHIP AMONG RURAL YOUTH 
 
3842. Smt. Malvika Devi: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken any special initiatives to 
promote entrepreneurship among rural youth in Kalahandi Lok 
Sabha constituency and Nuapada district of Odisha, through 
programmes such as the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National 
Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) and other schemes of the 
Ministry, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the number of rural enterprises established and the employment 
generated therefrom in Kalahandi and Nuapada districts during 
the last three years, scheme and year-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to establish dedicated Rural 
Business Incubation Centres, entrepreneurship facilitation 
centres or mentoring and handholding support mechanisms for 
aspiring entrepreneurs in Kalahandi and Nuapada, particularly 
for women and tribal youth; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, including the financial assistance 
proposed, implementation timeline and the measures taken to 
promote value addition in agriculture, millets, forest produce, 
handicrafts and other local livelihood activities in Kalahandi Lok 
Sabha Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Rural Development, under the Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), 
implements Rural Self Employment Training Institute (RSETI) 
programme for rural youth in the age group of 18–50 years to promote 
entrepreneurship in the entire country including in Kalahandi Lok 
Sabha Constituency and Nuapada district of Odisha.  The objective of 
the programme is self-employment and micro-enterprise 

Page 2 of 6 
 
development, with a mandate of minimum 70% settlement (including 
a maximum of 10% wage employment), along with credit linkage 
facilitation and handholding support to trainees for up to two years 
after completion of training.  
 
Further Odisha Livelihoods Mission (OLM), under the Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), 
has been taking various initiatives to promote entrepreneurship 
among rural youth in Kalahandi Lok Sabha Constituency and Nuapada 
district of Odisha. Skill development, entrepreneurship orientation 
and capacity building are provided through Rural Self Employment 
Training Institutes (RSETIs), which offer free skill-based residential 
training, entrepreneurship development, counselling and post-
training handholding support to rural youth for establishing self-
employment ventures and micro-enterprises. Institutional credit is 
facilitated through SHG Bank Linkage and interest subvention. 
 
The details of the number of rural enterprises established and 
the employment generated there from in Kalahandi and Nuapada 
districts during the last three years are at Annexure-I  
 
(c) & (d): At present, there is no proposal under the Rural Self-
Employment Training Institutes (RSETI) Scheme to establish 
dedicated Rural Business Incubation Centres, Entrepreneurship 
Facilitation Centres. However, the existing RSETIs in Kalahandi and 
Nuapada provide Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs), 
skill training, mentoring, and post-training hand-holding support to 
aspiring entrepreneurs, including women and Scheduled Tribe (ST) 
youth, to facilitate self-employment and the establishment of 
sustainable micro-enterprises. The performance of women and 
Scheduled Tribe (ST) candidates under the RSETIs during the last 
three years are at Annexure-II(a) and Annexure- II (b). 
 
Further, RSETI is a demand-driven scheme; hence, funds are not 
allocated State-wise. However, funds are released to the State for all 
categories altogether, including women, directly to the respective 
States/UTs. The details of funds released under the RSETI programme 
to the State of Odisha during the last three years are as follows: 
₹1,250.76 lakh in 2023–24, ₹1,464.00 lakh in 2024–25, and ₹2,119.86 
lakh in 2025–26. Thus, a total of ₹4,834.62 lakh has been released to 
the State during the said period. 
 
Also Under the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme 
(SVEP) umbrella, entrepreneurship facilitation support is being 
expanded in the concerned districts. In 2026-27, Kesinga Block of 

Page 3 of 6 
 
Kalahandi district has been selected under SVEP. The programme 
will support approximately 2,400 micro enterprises over a period of 
four years, with a provision of about ₹6.50 crore for implementation. 
Further, Dharmagarh Block in Kalahandi district and Boden Block in 
Nuapada district have been selected under the Micro Enterprise 
Development (MED) Programme under the SVEP umbrella. These 
blocks will be supported for a period of eighteen months, during 
which around 200 micro and nano enterprises will be supported in 
each block. An amount of ₹20 lakh per block has been provisioned 
towards capacity building, handholding and administrative support. 
Working capital support will be provided through the Community 
Investment Fund (CIF) available with the Gram Panchayat Level 
Federations (GPLFs), supplemented through bank linkage. 
Enterprises in sectors such as agriculture, millets, forest produce, 
handicrafts and other local livelihood activities will be promoted 
under these interventions.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(b) SEZs set up under the SEZ Act, 2005 and SEZ Rules, 2006 are primarily private 
investment-driven initiatives. An SEZ may be set up either jointly or severally by the 
Central Government, State Government or any person for manufacture of goods or 
rendering services, or for both, or as a free trade warehousing zone. The Central 
Government has not set up any SEZ after the enactment of the SEZ Act, 2005. Th e 
Board of Approval, constituted under SEZ Act, 2005, only considers those proposals 
which have been duly recommended by respective State Government. The feasibility 
study, wherever required, is carried out by the respective entrepreneur or the concerned 
State Government prior to submitting the proposal for consideration of this 
Department. There is no proposal or feasibility study under consideration in this 
Department to set up an Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) Park or 
a Common Facility Center for processing rare earth permanent magnets in any of the 
above two SEZs. 
  
(c) The SEZ Developers and units are granted fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to attract 
investment and to facilitate trade and export. The fiscal concessions and duty bene fits 
allowed to SEZs are laid down in the SEZ Act, 2005. Particularly, under Section 26(1)(a) 
of the SEZ Act, goods imported into, or services provided in an SEZ or a Unit to carry 
on the authorised operations by the Developer or entrepreneur are exempt from paying 
any duty of customs, under the Customs Act, 1962 or the Customs Tariff Act, 1975. In 
addition, as per the IGST Act, 2017 imports by SEZ Developer or units for authorised 
operations are exempt from payment of Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGS T). 
Some of the non -fiscal incentives allowed to SEZ units and Developers for export 
facilitation include single window clearance for Central and State level approvals and 
dedicated customs wing for faster clearance.

Strengthening of Cooperative Institutions in Vellore 
3845. Thiru D M Kathir Anand: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has examined the functioning of cooperative institutions in Vellore 
district of Tamil Nadu, including Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Societies, Urban 
Cooperative Banks, Cooperative Marketing Societies, Cooperative Housin g Societies, 
Cooperative Milk Producers' Societies and other cooperative institutions operating in the district 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the programmes introduced by the Government to strengthen governance, professional 
management, digitalisation and member services in cooperative institutions of the district; 
(c) whether financial, technical or capacity-building support has been provided or is proposed for 
improving the operational efficiency and long-term sustainability of these cooperative institutions, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the initiatives taken to expand credit access, marketing support and business opportunities for 
cooperative members, particularly farmers, artisans and small entrepreneurs; and 
(e) the details of the reforms and developmental measures undertaken by the Government to 
enhance the overall performance and outreach of the cooperative sector in the district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) To examine the functioning of cooperative institutions across the country, including those in 
Vellore district of Tamil Nadu, the Ministry of Cooperation (MoC) has adopted a multi -layered 
institutional mechanism for monitoring cooperative sector initiatives at the State and district levels, 
with a view to ensuring effective coordination, implementation and monitoring. For this purpose, 

Page 2 of 5 
 
committees have been constituted at various levels, from the national level to the district level. 
These include: 
i. Inter -Ministerial Committee (IMC) – Chaired by the Hon’ble Minister of Home Affairs & 
Cooperation; 
ii. National Level Coordination Committee (NLCC) – Chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of 
Cooperation; 
iii. State Cooperative Development Committee (SCDC) – Chaired by the Chief Secretary of the 
respective State/UT; and 
iv. District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC) – Chaired by the District Collector of 
the respective district.  
As per information received from the State of Tamil Nadu, two SCDC meetings and two 
DCDC meetings have been convened so far.  
Further, Ministry has launched the ‘Cooperative Ranking Framework’ which provides 
standardized parameters —including audit compliance, financial performance, and operational 
activities—that enable the State Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) to conduct independent 
assessments and take necessary steps to strengthen societies at the State, district, and block levels.  
The sector -wise details of the total number and the number of functional cooperative 
societies in Vellore district are attached at Annexure-A. 
 
(b) to (e) The Government has undertaken a series of digital, financial and capacity -building 
measures to strengthen governance, professional management, service delivery, operational 
efficiency and outreach of cooperative institutions, including those functioning in Vellore district: 
• Under the National Plan for formation of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and Fishery 
Cooperative Societies to achieve cooperative coverage in every uncovered Panchayat/village 
over a period of five years, as on 15.07.2026, a 27 PACS, 940 DCS and  36 FCS have been 
registered in the State of Tamil Nadu including 11 DCS in the Vellore district. 
• Under the Central Sector Project for Computerization of PACS, 4,561 PACS have been 
sanctioned and Rs 55.73 Cr have been disbursed to the State of Tamil Nadu. As on 15.07.2026, 
hardware has been delivered to 4,532 PACS and 4,481 PACS have been onboarded onto the 
common ERP-based national software including 64 PACS in Vellore District. The initiative is 
aimed at improving transparency, accounting, audit, monitoring, digital service delivery and 
integration with the cooperative banking structure. 
• The Model Bye -laws circulated by the Ministry of Cooperation and adopted by the State 
enable PACS to undertake more than 25 diversified business activities.  

Page 3 of 5 
 
• As per information provided by the State of Tamil Nadu, in Vellore district, 55 PACS are 
functioning as Common Service Centres and Fair Price Shops; 43 PACS are providing micro-
ATM facilities, 55 PACS are working as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras. 
• Further, 28 PACS are providing agricultural machinery services, 9 are operating 
Pharmacy/Medical Store , one is operating a Cooperative Medical Shop, 43 PACS  have 
godowns. 
• For improving professional management and long -term institutional sustainability, capacity-
building programmes are conducted through the National Council for Cooperative Training. 
In Tamil Nadu, such programmes are implemented through the Natesan Institute  of 
Cooperative Management, Chennai, and the Institute of Cooperative Management, Madurai. 
During the last five years, these institutions have trained 1,31,499 participants in the State, 
including 2,688 participants from Vellore district, in areas such as cooperative governance, 
financial management, digital literacy, computerization and business diversification.  
• In addition, 4,097 PACS Secretaries in Tamil Nadu have been trained in the effective use of 
Common Service Centre services; 4 programmes conducted for capacity building of 105 BoDs 
/ Secretaries of M -PACS with emphasis on good governance, professional management, 
business diversification and effective functioning of societies.  
• Village-level awareness programmes are being conducted to disseminate information 
regarding Government schemes, institutional credit, market linkages and business 
diversification. In Tamil Nadu, 560 such programmes have benefited 72,885 members, 
including 2,234 members from Vellore district. 
• NABARD has conducted various cooperative training programmes covering key areas such 
as women empowerment for PACS staff, preparation of Business Development Plans, the 
impact of NPAs on the financial health of PACS, and corporate governance in PACS. During 
FY 2023 -24 to FY 2025 -26, a total of 578 such cooperative training programmes were 
conducted in Tamil Nadu, including Vellore, training 15,635 officials.  
• Financial and technical assistance is also available through the National Cooperative 
Development Corporation for eligible cooperative projects in agriculture, dairy, fisheries, 
handloom, marketing, processing, storage and allied sectors, subject to prescri bed eligibility 
conditions and project appraisal. The details of financial assistance in the State of Tamil Nadu 
during last five years by NCDC is provided at Annexure-B

3846. Shri K Radhakrishnan: 
Shri Benny Behanan: 
 Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the total number of posts reserved for Divyangjan in Central Government 
Ministries Departments and other Autonomous bodies Ministry/Institution-wise; 
(b) the details of the number of recruitment drives conducted and the number of persons 
recruited from these drives between 2017 and 2026 disaggregated by gender and the type of 
disability, year-wise; 
(c) the number of posts reserved for Divyangjan lying vacant as of June 2026; and 
(d) whether the Government has considered developing an incentive-based framework to 
encourage the employment of Divyangjans in the public and private sector, if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment  
(SHRI B L VERMA) 
  
(a)- (c): Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 mandates that 
every appropriate Government shall provide not less than 4% reservation in the cadre strength of 
each group of posts in Government establishments for persons with benchmark disabilities 
(PwBDs). Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) has issued instructions from time to time 
to all the Ministries/Departments in this regard.  As per the data reported to this department by 
DoPT, Department of Financial Services (DFS) and the survey report of Public Sector 
Enterprises 2024-25, the total number of Divyangjan working across all the Central Ministries as 
on 01.01.2026 is 31261 and the total number of Divyangjan working in Public Sector Banks, 

Public financial institutions and Public Sector Insurance Companies is 23156. The total number 
of Divyangjan working in Public Sector Enterprises is 12105. 
  
(d): Section 35 of the RPwD Act 2016 mandates that the appropriate Government and the local 
authorities shall, within the limit of their economic capacity and development, provide incentives 
to employer in private sector to ensure that at least five per cent. of their work force is composed 
of persons with benchmark disability.

Cooperative Societies in Odisha 
3847. Dr. Sambit Patra: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of registered cooperative societies in Odisha; 
(b) whether special incentives are provided by the Government to women -led and tribal -led 
cooperative societies in the State of Odisha and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of financial assistance provided for the development of the cooperative sector in 
the country during the last five years, State-wise; and 
(d) the measures taken by the Union Government to promote cooperative banking in rural areas 
across the country including Odisha along with the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 8,667 
cooperative societies in Odisha, out of which 8,063 cooperative societies are functional. 
 
(b) The National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) , a statutory corporation 
under the Ministry  of Cooperation , provides financial assistance to the cooperative sector , 
including Women and Tribal cooperatives , across the country , including Odisha . NCDC 
encourages women cooperatives to avail financial assistance under its schemes, namely, 
‘Swayam Shakti Sahakar Yojana’, ‘Nandini Sahakar’, and ‘Yuva Sahakar’. The activity-wise 
financial assistance disbursed by NCDC in Odisha during the last five years are attached at 
Annexure-1. 
 
(c) The Government launched the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS 
in 2022 to bring all functional PACS onto a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based 
national software. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the Project with a financial outlay 

Page 2 of 5 
 
of ₹2,516 crore. The project has since been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay 
of ₹2,925.39 crore. The State-wise and year-wise details of funds released under the project are 
attached as Annexure-2. 
 
Additionally, the State -wise details of financial assistance provided by NCDC for the 
development of the cooperative sector during last five years are attached at Annexure-3. 
 
(d) The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several 
initiatives to promote cooperative banking in rural areas across the country, including Odisha, 
under the vision of "Sahakar-se-Samriddhi."  Key initiatives include: 
• Removal of the monetary ceiling on Gold Loans for Cooperative Banks. 
• Permission for One-Time Settlement (OTS) of outstanding loans. 
• Enhancement of individual housing loan limit for Rural Cooperative Banks to ₹75 lakh. 
• Promotion of Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS) for doorstep banking services. 
• Notification of StCBs and DCCBs as Member Lending Institutions under the CGTMSE 
Scheme. 
• Enhancement of Priority Sector Lending limit for Dairy Cooperative Societies from ₹5 
crore to ₹10 crore. 
• Establishment of Sahakar Sarathi to provide technology services to Rural Cooperative 
Banks. 
• Inclusion of Rural Cooperative Banks under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme. 
• Permission for eligible StCBs and DCCBs to open new branches through the automatic 
route. 
• Relaxation of financial and business authorisation norms for Cooperative Banks. 
• Removal of the requirement  of ₹50 crore net worth for Rural Cooperative Banks to 
become Corporate Agents for insurance distribution.
