GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRYAND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3873 
 ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
ALLOCATION FOR FISHERIES SECTOR 
 
3873.  SMT. PRATIMA MONDAL: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total allocation for the fisheries sector under the Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) and the measurable improvements the Ministry has recorded in fishers' 
incomes, value addition and post-harvest infrastructure, rather than expansion of scheme coverage; 
(b)  the aims to raise seafood exports substantially despite rising tariff bar riers and shifting 
global trade patterns; 
(c)  the strategy adopted by the Ministry to diversify export markets and strengthen the  
competitiveness of Indian seafood in the face of increasing international protectionism; 
(d)  the recurring outbreaks of live stock diseases continue to affect dairy farmers and reduce 
productivity; and 
(e)  the progress made by the Ministry towards achieving nationwide control of major animal 
diseases and the extent to which it is measuring the economic impact of these intervent ions on 
farmers' incomes? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRYAND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c) :  The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore, with effect from the financial year 2020-
21 for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in all States/UnionTerritories. 
PMMSY inter-alia provides financial assistance for development of fisheries infrastructure 
including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, fish markets, cold storages, ice plants, wholesale 
fish markets, hatcheries, brood banks amongst others.  
 

In addition, the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) implemented 
with effect from the financial year 2018-19 by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India 
provides concessional finance to various Eligible Entities including State Governments/Union 
Territories for development of fisheries and aqu aculture infrastructure. The key infrastructure 
activities approved under these schemes (PMMSY and FIDF) includes; 184 fishing harbours and 
fish landing centres, 775 cold storages and ice plants,1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish  
kiosks, 117 retail  fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets, 28,489 units of fish transportation 
facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto 
rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks.  
 
Despite rising tariff barriers and shifting global trade patterns, India's marine product exports 
reached 19.72 lakh metric tonnes, valued at Rs. 73,890 crore (USD 8.46 billion) during 2025-26. 
The share of value -added products in seafood exports increase from 2% in 2013 -14 to 11% in 
2024-25. The marine exports were made to over 128 countries. The United States remained India's 
largest export market, followed by China, the European Union (EU), Southeast Asia (SEA), Japan, 
the Middle East, and other countries. 
For the sustainable growth of seafood exports, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, 
in collaboration with the Department of Commerce and the Marine Products Export Development 
Authority (MPEDA) and Export Inspection Council has undertaken various initiatives to diversify 
export markets. These initiatives includes, sensitization and awareness programmes on the India-
UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), conducting stakeholder 
consultations, organizing Chintan Shivirs on value addition, identifying new export markets and 
deepening India's presence in existing markets to enhance trade facilitation, promoting exports 
through trade delegations and international trade fairs, organizing Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs) and 
Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), National Workshop on Seafood Exports and collaborating 
with Indian Missions abroad to facilitate market access. The Department of Fisheries has also held 
a series of Round Table meetings with the Embassies and High Commissions of potential partner 
countries to explore avenues for collaboration, strengthen bilateral trade cooperatio n in the 
fisheries sector.  
Further, the Department of Fisheries , Government of India is promoting diversified aquaculture 
under the PMMSY by encourag ing the culture of high -value species such as seabass, cobia, 
pompano, mud crab, GIFT tilapia, grouper, Penaeus monodon, scampi, and seaweed, with a focus 
on identifying new export markets and deepening existing ones  for global competitiveness of 
Indian seafood.  
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is also promoting value addition, enhancing 
biosecurity and quality compliance, encouraging automation and Research and Development 
(R&D) collaboration, and sustainable fisheries development. In addi tion, the Government 
continues to engage with importing countries to address sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) issues, 
export certification requirements, and market access barriers, while strengthening laboratory 
infrastructure, residue monitoring, and qual ity control systems to ensure compliance with 
international standards. 
(d) and (e): The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying has reported that,100% financial 
assistance is provided  to States/UTs for prevention of economically important livestock diseases 
namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and 
Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is also provided to 

States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritized activities such as vaccination against other 
livestock diseases, control of emergent and exotic diseases, strengthening of laboratory, disease 
surveillance, training and awareness. It is reported that 147.05 crore, 3.19 cr ore, 6.74 cr ore and 
0.26 crore doses of Vaccine for FMD, brucella and PPR and classical swine fever are administered 
respectively. The total   34.62 crore, doses of Vaccine have been administered for lumpy skin 
disease. Financial assista nce is provided to the 29 States/Union Territories on sharing basis for 
operation of 4019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU) to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s 
doorstep. The livestock disease outbreak has been reduced from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025.

3874. SHRI RAM SHIROMANI VERMA: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite crop damage due to floods and 
natural disasters, many farmers in Shravasti and Balrampur are not receiving insurance 
claims on time and if so, the reasons therefor; 
(b) the details of claims received, claims sanctioned and payments made under the 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) in the said districts during the last five years, 
district-wise; and 
(c) whether the Government is considering to implement any new system for speedy 
disposal of crop insurance claims and to connect maximum number of farmers with this 
scheme and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी                 (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Details of claims reported, claims paid and claims pending in Shravasti and 
Balrampur districts of Uttar Pradesh during last five years ii.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26 under 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)  are given below : 
(Rs. in crores) 
District Reported Claims Paid Claims Pending Claims 
Shravasti 34.19 33.86 0.32 
Balrampur 17.89 17.68 0.22 
 
Majority of the claims are settled within the stipulated timelines under the Operational 
Guidelines of the PMFBY i.e within 21 days of the receipt requisite yield data from the 
concerned State Government by the insurance companies. However, some claims 
remained pending, primarily on account of unverified bank account details of enrolled 
farmers.  

(c) :  Government has taken following steps to improve claims settlement timelines and to 
improve the insurance coverage under the scheme : 
(i): For timely settlement of claims under the scheme: 
- The National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) is the single source of data for 
subsidy payment, dissemination of information, delivery of services including 
online enrollment of farmers, uploading/obtaining individual insured famer’s 
details and transfer of claim amount electronically to the individual farmer’s Bank 
Account.   
 
- In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module 
namely ‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims from 
Kharif 2022 onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance Portal 
(NCIP) with Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and accounting system 
of Insurance Companies to provide timely & transparent processing of all claims. 
 
- W.e.f. Kharif 2024, in case payment is not made timely by Insurance Company, 
penalty.of 12% is auto-calculated and levied through NCIP.    
 
- Delinking of Central Government share of premium subsidy from that of State 
Governments has been implemented so that farmers can get proportionate 
claims relating to the Central Government share.  
 
- 12% penalty is also levied from Kharif 2025 on State Government for delay in 
release of State share of subsidy. 
 
- Opening of ESCROW Account by the State Government concerned for deposit of 
their premium share in advance as per provisions of the scheme has been made 
mandatory w.e.f. Kharif 2025 season for bringing financial discipline.   
 
- Also, towards leveraging technology in implementation of the scheme, various 
steps like capturing of yield data/Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) data through 
CCE-Agri App & uploading it on the NCIP, allowing insurance companies to 
witness the conduct of CCEs, integration of State land records with NCIP and 
usage of remote sensing based yield estimation through YES-TECH have 
already been taken to improve timely settlement of the claims to farmers.   
 
- Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP), developed as a digital mobile application 
to streamline and improve the efficiency of crop loss assessments for loacalised 
calamities/post harvest losses for individual farms and  land parcels under 
PMFBY. The use of CLAP has been made mandatory for all the States/UTs 
under the scheme. 

(ii): With a view to improve insurance coverage: 
- AIDE (App for Intermediary Enrolment): A smart-phone App has been 
designed and rolled out in Kharif 2023 for enrolment of farmers at their door-
steps through a large network of Insurance Intermediaries. It offers a completely 
paper-less and cash-less experience to a farmer. 
 
- The Government has actively supported the awareness activities being carried 
out by the States, implementing Insurance Companies, financial institutions, and 
Common Service Centres (CSCs) network to disseminate key features of 
PMFBY amongst farmers and members of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). 
 
- Further, a structured awareness campaign ‘Crop Insurance Week/Fasal Bima 
Saptah’ has been initiated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
since Kharif 2021 season onwards to increase the awareness about benefits of 
the scheme, sensitize the stakeholders and to increase overall enrolment of 
farmers, with special focus on identified aspirational/tribal districts. Along with 
this, ‘Fasal Bima Pathshalas’ are also being organized at village/GP level for 
knowledge building of farmers on various aspects of scheme implementation.  
 
- Government had also organized a nationwide Doorstep Crop Insurance 
Policy/receipt Distribution mega drive – ‘Meri Policy Mere Haath’. Hard copies of 
crop insurance policy receipts are distributed to farmers enrolled under PMFBY 
through special camps at gram Panchayat/village level. 
 
- Apart from this, other activities for awareness generation involve the publicity of 
key features and benefits of the scheme through advertisements in leading 
National and local newspapers, airing of audio-visual spots on regional / local 
channels, distribution of IEC material in local languages, dissemination of SMS 
through Kisan/ National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) portal and organisation of 
online workshops of all stakeholders including farmers, Panchayat Members, and 
other key stakeholders.

3875. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there will be increase in assistance under area expansion programme of Oil 
Palm taken up under National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm as the assistance provided is 
low; 
(b) whether the Government will consider more plantation of palm tree in Dhenkanal and 
Angul district of Odisha as these areas are thunder prone and are being affected by 
elephant menace; and 
(c) whether the Government will consider to plant more palm-tree in common remote 
and dense forest area to save the life of common villager and farmer from elephant 
menace? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a):  Under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), financial 
assistance for area expansion is provided to farmers as per the approved norms of the 
scheme. The assistance covers planting material, maintenance during gestation period and 
intercropping inputs. There is no proposal to increase assistance under the mission.  
(b):  Under NMEO-OP, identification of suitable areas for oil palm cultivation is 
undertaken by the State Governments based on agro-climatic suitability, availability of 
irrigation, land suitability and other technical parameters. For 2026-27, the Government of 
Odisha has allocated target of 200 ha. for Dhenkanal and 100 ha. for Angul for Oil Palm 
plantation. 
(c):  Under NMEO-OP, Oil palm cultivation is recommended on non-forest lands and 
agricultural lands. In initial years intercropping with other crops is undertaken. In mature 
plantations shade loving crops are being grown in some areas. The Government is not 
promoting oil palm cultivation in forest areas.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3876 
  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY 
 
3876. Shri Hasmukhbhai Somabhai Patel: 
 Shri Bharat Singh Kushwah: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the current status of implementation of skill development 
programmes under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya 
Yojana (DDU-GKY) to align them with changing industrial 
requirements and emerging employment opportunities along 
with the number of rural youth benefited therefrom; 
(b)  the sectors in which training has been imparted under the 
scheme and the arrangements made for placement of trained 
youth and for establishing coordination with industries; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure retention of 
candidates who have secured employment and the outcomes 
achieved in this regard so far; 
(d)  the total financial outlay earmarked for effective 
implementation of the scheme along with the amount 
sanctioned and spent thereunder so far; and 
(e)  the details of training, employment, financial allocation and the 
future action plan under the scheme in Madhya Pradesh 
particularly in Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 (SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 
is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana 
- National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood 
diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural 
youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through 
placement-linked skilling programs. To align with evolving industry 
requirements and emerging employment opportunities, revised 
guidelines under DDU-GKY 2.0 have been rolled out from FY 2025-26 

Page 2 of 3 
 
with focus on industry-led training, sustainable employment, 
enhanced post-placement support, upskilling and reskilling 
opportunities and greater flexibility in training delivery. Emerging 
sectors such as Electric Vehicle (EV) maintenance, renewable 
energy, logistics, healthcare, care economy, retail, hospitality and 
media & entertainment are also being prioritised. Since inception, 
around 18.45 lakh rural youth have been trained and about 12.35 lakh 
candidates have been placed under the scheme. 
  
(b): Training under DDU-GKY has been imparted across diverse 
sectors including Apparel, Automotive, Beauty & Wellness, 
Construction, Electronics, Healthcare, Hospitality, IT-ITES, Logistics, 
Retail, Telecom, Agriculture and allied sectors, among others. 
Placement of trained candidates is facilitated through mandatory 
industry partnerships, employer tie-ups, job fairs, campus placement 
drives, industry consultations, and engagement with Sector Skill 
Councils and employers. The scheme mandates placement-linked 
outcomes and continuous industry participation in curriculum design 
and training delivery. Further, the features like 20% allocation of 
targets to captive employers in each State/UT and the batch mode 
payments to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) linked to 
successful mandatory placement period of 6 months, have been 
incorporated to ensure coordination with industries. 
  
(c): To improve retention and sustainability of employment, DDU-
GKY 2.0 emphasizes long-term employment outcomes (minimum 70% 
placement including maximum 20% self or gig employment for 
minimum of 6 months) through one year post-placement tracking and 
support, counselling, migration support, alumni engagement, 
grievance redressal mechanisms, and opportunities for 
upskilling/reskilling. Under the revised framework, candidates are 
required to be tracked and supported for a longer duration to 
facilitate sustained employment and career progression. Since 
inception, about 12.35 lakh candidates have been placed under the 
Scheme. 
  
(d): For FY 2026-27, Budget Estimates (BE) of ₹750 crore has been 
kept for training around 1.37 lakh rural youth. Further, Mother 
Sanction amounting ₹361.96 crore has been issued to the States/UTs 
and an expenditure of ₹50.89 crore has been made by the States/UTs 
till date. 
  
(e): In the State of Madhya Pradesh, DDU-GKY is being implemented 
through the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihoods Mission 
(MPSRLM). Since inception, around 93 thousand candidates have 

Page 3 of 3 
 
been trained and around 56 thousand candidates have been placed in 
the State of Madhya Pradesh under the scheme. Further, for FY 2026-
27, mother sanction amounting to ₹10.00 crore has been issued to 
the State of Madhya Pradesh.

severely drought-affected and its 'Aanewari' being less than 50%, the farmers of the district 
have not yet received the benefits of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) for 
the Kharif year 2025-26; 
 
(b) whether with regards to the crop insurance disbursed in the State of Maharashtra, 
the affected farmers of Yavatmal district alone have been deprived of the benefits of the 
said scheme and if so, the reasons behind the said discriminatory action; 
 
(c) whether the Union Government is considering the serious condition of the farmers of 
Yavatmal district and will issue directions for an immediate inquiry against the crop 
insurance companies; and

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): As informed by the State Government of Maharashtra, out of the total claims 
of Rs. 506.75 lakh for Kharif 2025 season in Yavatmal district under Pradhan Mantri Fasal 
Bima Yojana (PMFBY), claims of Rs. 491.97 lakh have been paid to the eligible farmers. 
 As per PMFBY Operational Guidelines, claims are determined as per provisions 
contained in the operational guidelines of the scheme.  Government of Maharashtra has 
issued resolution dated 24.06.2025 clarifying that the data declared by any Government 
Department or Agency regarding ‘Paisaewari’/’Annewari’, drought, scarcity or flood damage

DIGITAL AGRICULTURE MISSION 
 
3879. SHRI NILESH DNYANDEV LANKE: 
DR. SHIVAJI BANDAPPA KALGE: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of Digital Agriculture Mission (DAM) and the number of farmers 
benefited through its digital tools, technologies and market linkages across the country, 
State-wise, particularly in Maharashtra; 
(b) the specific steps being taken for the effective implementation of Digital Agriculture 
Mission in Maharashtra, particularly in rural areas and for small and marginal farmers, to 
improve access to technology, agriculture-related data and weather forecasts; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to expand digital infrastructure in Maharashtra; and 
(d) the measures being implemented under Digital Agriculture Mission to effectively address 
the region-specific challenges in Maharashtra? 
                                                 
ANSWER 
 
 MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): Under the Digital Agriculture Mission, AgriStack is a digital foundation established to 
leverage data and digital services in the agriculture sector so that various government schemes 
can reach eligible farmers more quickly and effectively.  It consists of three foundational 
registries associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Referenced Village 
Maps and Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the State Governments/ Union 
Territories.  
AgriStack supports a wide range of digital services, and scheme delivery including 
accurate targeting of beneficiaries for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under PM-KISAN, 
Minimum Support Price (MSP)-based procurement through the Food Corporation of India 
(FCI), and booking of Fertilizer. It also enables faster delivery of services, such as disaster 
relief disbursement, sanctioning of Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans within half an hour, and 
improved farmer outreach for participation in procurement schemes. Furthermore, the Farmer 
ID is being used for enrolment under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), 
procurement under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) of PM-ASHA, and linking with Soil Health 
Cards to support crop and input planning. In addition, Digital Crop Survey data is being utilized 
to generate near real-time crop production estimates. 
As of 6th August, 2026, more than 10.33 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across 
the country, including more than 1.36 Crore Farmer IDs in Maharashtra. The State-wise details 
of Farmer IDs are given in Annexure – I.  

Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 
Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country, including 34,99,974 plots in 
Maharashtra. The State-wise details of DCS plots are given in Annexure – II. 
(b): Farmers can register for a Farmer ID themselves using their mobile phones. However, 
in Maharashtra, a campaign was undertaken through Common Service Centres (CSCs) to 
facilitate the creation of Farmer IDs, to ensure that the maximum number of farmers obtain 
their Farmer IDs at the earliest. 
Maharashtra has developed AI-based application, MahaVistar, through which farmers 
are provided with timely information in their local language on their mobile phones, including 
weather forecasts, crop management practices, pest and disease management, market 
information for the sale of agricultural produce, and other agriculture-related advisory services. 
 
(c): As reported by the Government of Maharashtra, the State is expanding and 
strengthening the digital agriculture infrastructure through the implementation of the AgriStack 
initiative. It is being utilized for multiple use cases, including implementation of loan waiver 
schemes, delivery of benefits under agriculture-related schemes through the MahaDBT and 
PoCRA DBT platforms, disaster relief and rehabilitation, fertilizer distribution, and other 
Government service delivery mechanisms. These initiatives are aimed at creating an 
integrated, farmer-centric digital ecosystem for efficient and transparent governance in the 
agriculture sector. 
 
(d): Under the Digital Agriculture Mission, special measures are being implemented in 
Maharashtra to ensure the inclusion of farmers from all regions, including those facing region-
specific challenges. In this regard, for farmers covered under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 
(FRA), the process of generating Farmer IDs has been initiated and as of 4 August 2026, a 
total of 22,597 Forest Rights holder farmers have successfully registered for obtaining their 
Farmer ID. This initiative will enable these farmers to access the benefits of the Digital 
Agriculture Mission and various farmer-centric digital services in a seamless manner.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3880 
  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
DELAY IN WAGE PAYMENT UNDER MGNREGS 
 
3880. Shri Narayandas Ahirwar: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it has come to the notice of the Government that there 
is a delay in the payment of wages to workers under the 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) at several places, State and district-wise including 
Bundelkhand; 
(b)  if so, the reasons therefor along with the steps taken by the 
Government to ensure timely payment of wages; 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to further strengthen the 
monitoring mechanism to enhance transparency, prevent 
corruption and ensure that the full benefits of development 
schemes reach the eligible beneficiaries in rural areas, State 
and district-wise including Bundelkhand, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to introduce any new scheme 
or policy to provide sustainable employment at the local level to 
the youth trained under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen 
Kaushalya Yojana especially the youth from Bundelkhand, upon 
the completion of their training, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS the wage payments are 
directly credited by the Central Government to the accounts of the 
beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer protocol.  At the 
beginning of each financial year, admissible pending liabilities of the 
previous years, if any, are duly reimbursed by the Government of 
India. Accordingly, all due and admissible pending wage liabilities 
upto FY 2025-26 have already been cleared.  

Page 2 of 3 
 
  
Release of funds to States/UTs is a continuous process, subject 
to submission of proposal and compliance with extant guidelines. 
Financial sanctions are issued periodically based on States’ demand 
for funds, utilisation of previously sanctioned amounts, and receipt of 
complete proposals with requisite documents, in accordance with 
the Scheme’s prescribed procedure. During the current financial year 
(2026–27), ₹912.43 crore has been released to the State of Uttar 
Pradesh under the wage component of the Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. 
  
(c) & (d): As the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025   has come into force with 
effect from 1st July, 2026, a comprehensive institutional, community-
based and technology-enabled framework has been implemented 
under the Programme to ensure transparency, accountability, 
effective monitoring, timely utilisation of funds and achievement of 
the intended outcomes. Multi-tier monitoring at the Gram Panchayat, 
Intermediate Panchayat, District, State and National levels, 
mandatory Social Audit through independent Social Audit Units, 
public disclosure of records and information, grievance redressal 
mechanisms, regular inspections and concurrent monitoring are 
being undertaken as part of the implementation framework. 
  
The implementation is further supported through technology-
enabled systems. Attendance is being recorded through the National 
Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) to enhance transparency and 
authenticity, Area Officer monitoring visits are being conducted for 
independent field verification and assessment of the quality of 
implementation, assets are being geo-tagged, electronic 
Measurement Books (e-MB) are being used for recording 
measurements of works, and real-time monitoring of physical and 
financial progress is being carried out through the Management 
Information System (MIS). These measures are applicable across all 
States and Union Territories, including the Bundelkhand region, to 
ensure that the benefits of the Scheme reach eligible beneficiaries in 
a transparent and accountable manner. 
  
  
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 
is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana 
- National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood 
diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural 
youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through 
placement-linked skilling programs. DDU-GKY guideline provides 
social inclusion of SC/ST (50%), Women (33%), and PwDs (5%). 

Page 3 of 3 
 
  
The Ministry has introduced Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen 
Kaushalya Yojana 2.0 (DDU-GKY 2.0) in 2025-26, which focuses on 
demand-based skilling, industry partnerships, placement-linked 
training, and emerging job roles to enhance employability and 
livelihood opportunities for rural youth. DDU-GKY 2.0 emphasizes 
long-term employment outcomes (minimum 70% placement including 
maximum 20% self or gig employment for minimum of 6 months) 
through one year post-placement tracking and support, counselling, 
migration support, alumni engagement, grievance redressal 
mechanisms, and opportunities for upskilling/reskilling. Under the 
revised framework, candidates are required to be tracked and 
supported for a longer duration to facilitate sustained employment 
and career progression. 
  
Regular review and time-to-time monitoring are being done for 
training quality, assessment, placement outcomes thereby 
contributing to the effective implementation of the scheme, 
livelihood promotion and timely implementation. 
   
In the Bundelkhand region, 36036 candidates have been trained 
and 23275 candidates have been placed under the scheme since 
inception till date.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE 
 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3883 
ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
  
LAC INDUSTRY IN DISTRICT PURULIA IN WEST BENGAL 
  
3883. SHRI JYOTIRMAY SINGH MAHATO: 
  
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री) be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the potential of Purulia district, West 
 Bengal for the development of the lac industry, considering its significant lac 
 production, tribal population and scope for value addition and exports, if so, the 
 details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has any proposals to establish a Lac Processing and  
 Value Addition Centre, Testing Laboratory, Common Facility Centre or Export 
 Facilitation Centre in Purulia to strengthen the lac value chain, if so, the details 
 thereof; 
(c) whether any financial assistance, technology support, skill development, 
 branding and market linkage initiatives have been extended to lac growers, Self -
 Help Groups, Farmer Producer Organisations and entrepreneurs in the district 
 during the last five years, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has prepared any roadmap t o promote exports of lac 
 and lac-based products from Purulia under the Districts as Export Hubs initiative 
 or any other Central scheme, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the measures proposed to be taken by the Government to develop Purulia as a 
 national hub for lac production, processing and exports? 
 
ANSWER 
वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA)  
(a)  India produced about 21,272 tonnes of lac during 2025 -26 and exported about USD 
174 million worth of lac and its value -added products during the same period. (Previous 
three years production and exports are given at Annexure).  
The Shellac and Forest Products Export Promotion Council (SHEFEXIL), which is the nodal 
Export Promotion Council under the Department of Commerce for promotion of exports of 
Non-Timber Forest Produce, including lac and its value-added products, has assessed the 
potential of Purulia district, West Bengal, for the development of the lac industry. As per 
the assessment, Purulia is one of the important lac-producing districts in the country and a 
substantial tribal population in the district are engaged in lac cultivation. As per the records 
of the District Industries Centre, Purulia, lac cultivation is undertaken over about 700 
hectares across 12 of the 20 blocks of the district.  
(b) to (e)  Key initiatives undertaken for the welfare of lac growers in the distr icts include 
financial assistance for establishment of a lac -based Van Dhan Vikas Kendra at 
Balarampur block of Purulia district under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (through TRIFED), 

2 
 
aimed at promoting value addition and livelihood generation in the lac sector; and formation 
of 23 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) in Purulia district under the Central Sector 
Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs. 
Further, key initiatives undertaken by the Government for development of the lac sector 
and promotion of exports of lac and its value-added products, including from Purulia district, 
are as under: 
(i) The Export Promotion Mission (EPM) being implemented by the Department of 
Commerce, aims to strengthen India’s export competitiveness through targeted financial 
and trade facilitation interventions. The Mission operates through two integrated sub -
schemes: (1) Niryat Protsahan, which focuses on improving access to affordable trade 
finance for MSMEs through instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, credit 
guarantee and credit enhancement support for diversification into new markets; and (2) 
Niryat Disha, which focuses on non-financial enablers that enhance market readiness and 
competitiveness, including export quality and compliance support , assistance for 
international branding, packaging and participation in trade fairs, export warehousing and 
logistics, inland transport reimbursements, and trade intelligence and capacity -building 
initiatives. The benefits under the Mission are available t o exporters across sectors, 
including exporters of lac and lac-based products from Purulia district. 
(ii) Under the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative of the Directorate General of Foreign 
Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, the export potential o f districts is identified and 
promoted through District Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs) and District Export 
Action Plans (DEAPs). Purulia district has been identified under the DEH initiative, and the 
DEAPs are prepared in coordination with Central Min istries/Departments, State 
Governments and district -level stakeholders, and are aligned with the One District One 
Product (ODOP) initiative. 
(iii) A number of export promotion initiatives have been undertaken, inter alia including the 
organisation of Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs) and Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), as 
well as participation of exporters in national and international exhibitions and trade fairs. 
Key events over the last three years include the Bharat Nutraverse Expo (New Delhi), 
Vitafoods Eur ope (Geneva/Barcelona), Food Ingredients Europe (Frankfurt), and 
SupplySide West (Las Vegas, USA). These initiatives aim to connect Indian exporters of 
non-timber forest produce, including lac and its value-added products, with global buyers. 
(iv) The Mini stry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) has established 65 
Export Facilitation Centres (EFCs) across the country, including four in West Bengal, 
namely, Central Tool Room & Training Centre (CTTC), Kolkata; MSME Testing Centre, 
Kolkata; Branch MS ME-Development and Facilitation Office, Siliguri; and MSME -
Development and Facilitation Office, Kolkata. These Centres provide mentoring, 
handholding and export -related support to MSMEs across the State to facilitate their 
participation in international trade.

 Shri Jai Parkash: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of complaints regarding 
delays in wage payments to workers under the Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) in 
Sonipat and Hisar Lok Sabha Constituencies of Haryana; 
(b)  if so, the details regarding the number of registered MGNREGS 
workers, man-days generated, sanctioned, time-line for wage 
payments, disbursed wages and delayed payments within the 
above Constituencies during the last three years, year-wise; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely payment of 
pending wages through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and to 
resolve technical and administrative bottlenecks; 
(d)  whether any special initiatives have been undertaken to 
enhance the efficiency of the digital payment system, Aadhaar-
based Payment System (ABPS) and grievance redressal 
mechanism; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and the outcomes achieved in the 
Sonipat and Hisar Lok Sabha Constituencies? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): Consequent upon the commencement of the Viksit Bharat 
– Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G 
Act, 2025, the scheme has been successfully implemented across the 
rural areas of the country with effect from 1st July, 2026 including 
Haryana. With regard to VB- G RAM G Scheme it is stated that an 
Interim Allocation of Rs. 590.19 crore has been made as Central 
Share for financial year 2026-27 for the period between 01.07.2026 to 

Page 2 of 5 
 
31.03.2027 to the State of Haryana. Subsequently, Mother Sanctions 
amounting to Rs. 194.93 crore have been issued as first instalment 
for various components based on the proposal received from the 
State.  
  
Payment of wages under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS), which 
stands repealed with effect from 01.07.2026 on commencement of 
implementation of VB-G RAM G it is stated that fund release to 
States/UTs, including  State of  Haryana is a continuous 
process.  Under the Scheme, the Wage payments are directly credited 
by the Central Government to the accounts of the beneficiaries 
through Direct Benefit Transfer protocol. Sanctions for Wage 
payments are issued daily by the Ministry through the Public Finance 
Management System (PFMS) based on fund transfer orders received 
from the States/ UTs after following due procedures. At the beginning 
of each financial year, admissible pending liabilities of the previous 
years, if any, are duly reimbursed by the Government of India. 
Accordingly, all due and admissible pending wage liabilities upto FY 
2025-26 have already been cleared. 
  
Details of % of Fund Transfer Orders (FTOs) generated within 15 
days from the closure of muster rolls Sonipat and Hisar district of

(c):     Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, the wage payments are directly 
credited by the Central Government to the accounts of the 
beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer protocol based on Fund 
Transfer Orders (FTOs) generated by concerned State/UT 
Government. As per the provisions of the Act, beneficiaries are 
entitled to receive wage payments within 15 days of closure of 
muster rolls. The Government continuously monitors the 
implementation of Mahatma Gandhi NREGS through the Management 
Information System (MIS), regular review meetings and other 
appropriate mechanisms and whenever any specific implementation 
issue comes into the notice of the Ministry efforts are made to resolve 
the same at the earliest.   
   
     Further, in order to ensure timely payment, the Government of 
India has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure 
(SOP) to all States/UTs, which defines fixed timelines for each stage 
of the wage payment process from muster roll uploading to FTO 
approval. The Ministry along with the States/UTs has been making 
concerted efforts for improving the timely payment of wages. 
States/UTs have been advised to generate pay orders in time.  
  
  In addition, the Ministry has taken various steps to ensure timely 
payment of wages to workers under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. These 
include: 
 Improvement of National Electronic Fund Management System 
(Ne-FMS) 
 Intensive consultation with State Governments and other 
stakeholders for ensuring timely payment of wages, verification 
of pending and delay compensation claims etc. 
 Formulation of Standard Operating Procedure for monitoring of 
timely payment and payment of delay compensation. 

Page 4 of 5 
 
 Reviewing the status of timely payment and payment of delay 
compensation with the States/ UTs during periodic meetings, 
 Performance Review Committee meetings, Mid-term Reviews 
etc.  
   
Further, continued efforts have been undertaken by the Ministry 
through various technological interventions for ensuring timely 
payments of wages. Some of the key interventions include:  
 Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): Wages are transferred directly 
from the central account to workers’ bank accounts, minimizing 
the role of intermediaries. This has proven to be effective in 
enhancing transparency and preventing leakages. Almost 100% 
of the funds are managed electronically with the wage payment 
made entirely through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) protocol. 
 Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS): APBS conversion is a 
major reform process where benefits are credited directly into 
the bank accounts based on the Aadhaar of the workers under 
Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, preferably Aadhaar Based Payments, 
cutting several layers in the delivery process. APBS helps in 
better targeting, increasing the efficiency of the system and 
reducing the delays in payments, ensuring greater inclusion by 
curbing leakages thereby promoting greater accountability and 
transparency. 
 National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS): Real-time 
attendance capture through geo-tagged photographs at the 
worksite ensures accurate and timely recording of attendance, 
which helps in timely payment of wages. 
        
  Further as per the provisions mentioned in Schedule-II of the 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGA), wage seekers shall be entitled to receive 
payment of compensation for the delay, at the rate of 0.05% of the 
unpaid wages per day of delay beyond the sixteenth day of closure of 
muster roll. Delay compensation rules are notified by the State 
Government concerned. The amount due for compensation is duly 
verified and approved, and then paid by the concerned State 
Government.  
  
(d) & (e): To ensure timely payment of wages to the beneficiaries 
under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS and to address the issues arising due 
to frequent changes in bank account numbers of the beneficiaries 
and subsequent non-updation, it was decided to implement Aadhar 
Payment Bridge System (APBS). This has been made mandatory with 
effect from 1st January 2024.  
  

Page 5 of 5 
 
  APBS helps in improving the transparency and accountability of 
wage distribution under the scheme and ensure faster crediting of 
wages in the account of beneficiaries. Aadhar Authentication also 
reduces leakage and corruption and ensures that only legitimate 
beneficiaries with verified identities receive wages.  In case of failure 
in payment through APBS, an alternative route to make payment is 
available through account-based payment that is National Automated 
Clearing House.  
  
  Here, it is also stated that, the Government has undertaken 
several initiatives to enhance the efficiency of the digital payment 
system and grievance redressal mechanism under the erstwhile 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) and these provisions have been further strengthened 
under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. These include Direct Benefit 
Transfer (DBT) of wages through the Aadhaar-based Payment System 
(ABPS), electronic Fund Management System (e-FMS), Aadhaar 
seeding, digital generation of Fund Transfer Orders (FTOs), real-time 
monitoring through the Management Information System (MIS), and a 
technology-enabled grievance redressal mechanism with provision 
for registration, tracking and timely disposal of grievances.

IMPACT OF FODDER SHORTAGE 
 
3885: SMT. PRIYANKA GANDHI VADRA 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन , पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
 be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the adverse impact of fodder shortage on dairy 
farmers’ incomes, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the details of dry fodder, green fodder and concentrate feed deficit since 2019 and schemes to 
increase production and supply, State-wise;  
(c) the details of projects supported under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund 
(AHIDF) to establish animal feed plants, State -wise including in Lok Sabha Constituency Wayanad 
in Kerala; and  
(d) whether the Government has taken initiatives to promote alternative green fodder, if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d)    As per the assessment made in 2019 by Indian Council of Agricultural Research  (ICAR) 
- Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi, the country faces estimated deficits 
of 11.24% in green fodder, 23.4% in dry fodder, and 28.9% in concentrate feed ingredients.   
 
To supplement the efforts of State Governments towards self -sufficiency in fodder, the Department 
of Animal Husbandry and Dairying provides support through the following interventions: 
 
i. Under National Livestock Mission (NLM), financial assistance is provided for quality fodder 
seeds production including breeder, foundation, and certified seeds. During last five years, an 
amount of Rs.1,152.40 Crores has  been released and 1.6 lakh tonnes of quality fodder seed 
produced. Central Agencies like National Seed Corporation Limited(NSCL), National Dairy 
Development Board(NDDB) , Krishi Vikas S ahakari Samiti L imited(KVSSL), Sadbhav 
Consumers Multi State Cooperative Society L imited(SADBHA V), National Cooperative 
Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF), National Agricultural Cooperative 
Marketing Federation of India Limited (NAFED) and Hindustan Insecticides Limited  (HIL) 
empanelled under National Livestock Mission(NLM) for quality fodder seed production are 
working in different States across the Country. Further, under NLM -Entrepreneurship 
Development Programme (N LM-EDP), 50% subsidy (up to Rs. 50 lakhs) is offered for 

establishing infrastructure like hay/s ilage/Total Mixed Ration (TMR) blocks and setting up  
seed processing/grading units. Under this, 204 projects have been approved with a project cost 
of Rs.201.02 Crores and approved subsidy of Rs.86.65 Crores. List of projects supported 
under NLM-EDP for hay/silage/Total Mixed Ration (TMR) blocks is given in annexure-I.   
 
 
ii. Under Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), 3% interest subvention 
is provided to individual entrepreneurs, private companies, Micro, Small, and Medium 
Enterprises ( MSME), Farmers Producers Organizations (FPOs), Section 8 companies and 
Dairy Cooperatives to establish various infrastructure activities including animal feed plants.  
 
iii. 100 dedicated Fodder-Plus Farmer Producer Organisations have been established by National 
Dairy Development Board (NDDB) across the country to bo ost local production and supply 
of fodder.  
 
iv. Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying(DAHD) has instructed all the States and 
Union Territories to establish a State Fodder Task Force to monitor availability, increase 
fodder cultivation area and ensure convergence with other schemes such as Viksit Bharat – 
Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). 
 
v. ICAR-IGFRI, in collaboration with All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on 
Forage Crops, is strengthening national fodder production by establishing over 70 year-round 
forage gardens across State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), 
and Non-Governmental Organisations ( NGOs) that have trained over 10 lakh farmers and 
stakeholders, developing 112 high-yielding varieties across 19 crops over the last decade, and 
formulating area-specific fodder strategies for 29 St ates. ICAR-IGFRI has developed State-
specific fodder development plans for 28 States and one Union Territory.  
 
The State -wise details of projects approved under  the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure 
Development Fund (AHIDF) for establishing animal feed plants is given in annexure-II. No project 
for Animal Feed Plant has been approved in Wayanad Lok Sabha Constituency.  
 
The Central Government has already taken multiple proactive initiatives to promote alternative 
green fodder such as spineless cactus, hydroponic fodder,  fodder sugarcane, azolla, moringa 
cultivation under its various schemes viz., Watershed Development Component - Pradhan Mantri 
Krishi Sinchayee Yojana(WDC-PMKSY 2.0), Pradhan Mantri -Rastriya Krishi Vikas Yojana( PM -
RKVY), various Silvi pasture and Horti pasture integration programmes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3886 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11th August, 2026 
 
DISTRICT AGRICULTURE CONTINGENCY PLANS 
3886. SHRI VISHALDADA PRAKASHBAPU PATIL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान 
कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether, in view of the projected El Nino conditions and weak monsoon, the 
Government has prepared any estimate of the value of agricultural output and farm 
income that may be lost during the current Kharif season, especially in Maharashtra, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the list of the 315 districts identified by the Government as potentially 
affected by weak monsoon conditions, along with their categorisation as high‑priority, 
medium‑priority & low‑priority; 
(c) whether the Government has compiled data on the coverage of Pradhan Mantri 
Fasal Bima Yojana, PM‑KISAN & other such schemes in these 315 vulnerable 
districts, particularly in Maharashtra, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government would share the DACPs (District Agriculture Contingency 
Plans) for these 315 districts in the public domain, including their budgetary allocations 
& timelines for each measure? 
 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a):  The sowing operations for the Kharif 2026-27 season are still underway, and the 
First Advance Estimates of production for major Kharif crops for the agricultural year 
2026-27 (July–June) have not yet been released. 
(b): District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) have been updated for 15 States 
including Maharashtra covering 342 Districts which are likely to receive below normal 
rainfall by the ICAR Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) 
in consultation with the States for implementation. Based on the probability of rainfall, 
irrigation coverage and cropped area, 262 districts have been identified as vulnerable 
districts, for focused monitoring and review of the preparedness. The list of 262 
vulnerable districts is given at Annexure I. 
  

 
Further, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have also been issued by 
ICAR for Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) for mitigation of El Niño-related risks.  
(c) & (d):  The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is continuously monitoring 
the evolving monsoon situation and the possible impact of El Niño conditions on 
agriculture in close coordination with the India Meteorological Department (IMD), 
various Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) institutions, ICAR- Central 
Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Central Water Commission 
(CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast 
Centre (MNCFC), the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), the 
Department of Fertilisers (DoF) and State Governments. Further, the Government has 
undertaken the following measures: 
i. Weekly meeting of the Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG) is being held with 
the representatives of India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water 
Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis 
National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), Indian Council of Agriculture 
Research - Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA), 
Department of Fertilizers, Department of Food & Public Distribution and the 
State Governments to review rainfall situation, reservoir storage, groundwater 
levels, crop sowing, input availability, market situation and pest/ disease 
incidence for timely intervention. Meeting with State Agriculture Secretaries and 
Relief Commissioners held under the chairmanship of Secretary (DA&FW) on 
27.04.2026 to review availability of inputs like seeds, fodder, drinking & 
irrigation water, fertilizers and general preparedness. Further, a meeting of the 
Crisis Management Group had been conducted on 17.06.2026 to assess and 
strengthen preparedness for the monsoon. In addition, the National Disaster 
Management Authority has also reviewed the preparedness of below-normal 
rainfall conditions emanating from the likely impact of the El Nino conditions on 
19th June 2026. Review of the situation has been undertaken by the Agriculture 
Minister, Government of India with the State Agriculture Ministers for Kharif 
preparedness amid El Nino conditions on 23.06.2026. 
ii. Adequate availability of seeds has been ensured, against the demand of 172.80 
lakh quintals from the States, there was availability of 192.25 lakh quintals of 
Kharif crop seeds. States have maintained 1% seeds i.e. 1.74 Lakh quintals as 
National Seed Reserve.  
  

iii. Special emphasis has been laid on promoting crop diversification, promotion of 
short-duration and drought-tolerant crop varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, 
water conservation practices, micro-irrigation, mulching, inter-cropping and 
practices of other climate-resilient technologies. Due to the delay as well as the 
likelihood on adverse impact of El Nino conditions, sowing is likely to be 
affected in respect of Tur, Soybean and Cotton and accordingly, the advisories 
to the farmers have been given to sow Maize, Bajra and Moong, and other short 
duration crops.  
iv. A nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyaan was organised during 1-30 June, 2026 in 
which 80,67,300 farmers participated in 1,14,567 programmes which were 
organised to promote water conservation, introduce efficient irrigation and 
climate-resilient farming practices. Simultaneously, an intensive Kisan Credit 
Card (KCC) saturation drive is being implemented in the vulnerable districts.  
v. Government has been implementing the yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal 
Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and the weather index-based Restructured Weather 
Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) since Kharif 2016 to provide 
financial support to farmers against crop losses arising from natural calamities 
and adverse weather events, thereby stabilizing farm income. PMFBY provides 
comprehensive insurance coverage from pre-sowing to post-harvest against 
widespread and localized risks. The schemes are voluntary for States/UTs and 
farmers, with implementation based on districts and crops notified by the 
concerned State Governments. In the identified vulnerable districts, awareness 
and enrolment drives are also being undertaken to enhance insurance 
coverage. 
vi. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a Central Sector Scheme 
launched in February 2019 to provide income support of ₹6,000 per year to 
eligible farmer families in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 through Direct 
Benefit Transfer (DBT). Since its inception, over ₹4.46 lakh crore has been 
transferred directly to farmers' bank accounts, ensuring transparency and 
eliminating intermediaries. Identification and verification of beneficiaries are 
carried out by the respective State/UT Governments, with validation through 
Aadhaar, Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and Income Tax 
databases before release of benefits. As per the 23rd Instalment of release of 
funds under PM-KISAN, the district-wise number of beneficiaries and funds 
released as well as the total funds released till date for the Districts in the State 
of Maharashtra is given at Annexure II. 
  

 
vii. As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures at 
the ground level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments 
undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available 
in the form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with 
the approved guidelines. Additional financial assistance, over and above 
SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as 
per laid down procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes 
an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). 
The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief 
and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed. 
The details of fund allocation under SDRF State-wise during 2026-27 to 
2030-31 (under the XVIth Finance Commission) as provided by the Ministry of 
Home Affairs is given at Annexure III. 
viii. The Central Water Commission and State Governments have been advised to 
undertake advance planning for optimum utilization of reservoir water and 
promote efficient irrigation practices. Assistance to farmers is available through 
ongoing schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana: Per Drop 
More Crop (PDMC) with a focus on enhancing water-use efficiency at the farm 
level through installation of Micro-Irrigation systems. Department of Rural 
Development is utilising Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) (VB G Ram G) funds for rejuvenating water structures – such 
as farm ponds, check dams, canal desilting, and bori bandhans – to trap every 
drop of early or residual rainfall. Further, as part of the climate resilient 
agricultural practices, the Department is also implementing various Schemes 
viz. the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), Kisan Credit Card (KCC), 
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), National Food 
Security Mission (NFSM), Integrated Scheme on Oilseeds Mission, Mission for 
Aatmanirbharta in Pulses and other existing programmes across the country.  
ix. The District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) are prepared at the District 
level in consultation with the State authorities and Indian Council of Agriculture 
Research - Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA). 
These are available at the District-level and not maintained centrally. 
Suggested measures are implemented at the District level as per their 
requirement.

INCREASE IN FISH PRODUCTION 
 
3888.  SHRI SUKANTA KUMAR PANIGRAHI: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the details of total funds allocated and expenditure incurred under the Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and the National Animal Disease Control Programme 
(NADCP) in Odisha durin g the last three financial years (2023 -24 to 2025 -26), district-wise 
including Kandhamal, Boudh, Ganjam and Nayagarh districts; 
 
(b) the achievements made by the Government in these districts, including increase in fish 
production, establishment of Bio -floc units, artificial insemination coverage and other 
measures taken by the Government to improve the livelihoods of fishers, dairy and livestock 
farmers; and  
 
(c) the steps taken by the Government under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure 
Development Fund (FIDF) to strengthen cold chain facilities, fodder banks, fishery 
infrastructure and veterinary services, particularly in the tribal and interior areas of these 
districts? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying 
(MoFAH&D), Government of India, has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) across all States and U nion Territories, including Odisha, since 
2020–21. During this period, the Department has approved fisheries development proposals 
submitted by the Government of Odisha amounting to ₹1,301.18 crore, including a Central 
share of ₹484.64 crore, covering a br oad range of interventions across the State, including in 
Kandhamal, Boudh, Ganjam, and Nayagarh districts to strengthen the fisheries and aquaculture 
value chain. Under PMMSY, during the last three years, the Government of India has released 
₹161.03 crore to the Government of Odisha for implementation of the approved activities. The 
district‑wise details of funds released, as reported by the Government of Odisha, are furnished 
at Annexure‑I. 
 

 
 
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, is implementing 
the National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) with the objective of improving 
animal health, enhancing livestock productivity, reducing economic losses, and incre asing 
farmers’ income. The programme emphasises universal livestock identification and creation of 
a digital livestock database to strengthen disease surveillance and facilitate efficient 
implementation of animal health interventions. Under NADCP, an amount of ₹12.78 crore has 
been allocated to the State of Odisha for the last three financial years (2023–24 to 2025–26).  
(b) Under PMMSY and other initiatives, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, is 
extending financial support to all States and Union Territories, including Odisha, for enhancing 
fish production through a range of interventions including establishment of cage and pen 
culture units, biofloc systems, Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), new ponds, 
hatcheries, brood banks, and stocking of fingerlings in reservoirs and wetlands. As reported by 
the Government of Odisha, 15 biofloc units have been set up in Kandhamal, Boudh, Ganjam, 
and Nayagarh districts. The district‑wise increase in fish production in these districts over the 
last three years, as reported by the State Government, is furnished at Annexure‑II.  
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, under the Rashtriya 
Gokul Mission (RGM), is implementing the Artificial Insemination (AI) Programme across all 
States and Union Territories, including Odisha, to accelerate genetic improvement of bovine 
livestock and enhance milk productivity. The year-wise number of animals inseminated under 
the AI Programme in Kandhamal, Boudh, Ganjam, and Nayagarh districts  during 2023–24 to 
2025–26, as reported by the Government of Odisha, is furnished at Annexure-III. 
 
(c) Under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), the 
Department of Fisheries, MoFAH&D, has sanctioned 13 projects in Odisha w ith a total 
investment of ₹784.32 crore, including interest subvention support of ₹286.39 crore. Of these, 
11 projects amounting to ₹740.92 crore have been approved for the Government of Odisha, 
while 2 projects with an outlay of ₹43.40 crore have been sanctioned for private entrepreneurs 
in the State The approved projects strengthen diverse areas of fisheries infrastructure across the 
State.

IMPACT OF EL NINO ON AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION 
3891. DR. D RAVI KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी  
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the likely impact of El Niño on agricultural 
production in Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the measures taken to promote drought-resilient crops and micro-irrigation; 
(c) whether additional crop insurance and compensation measures are proposed; and 
(d) the details of awareness programmes conducted for farmers? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a):  Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is continuously monitoring the evolving 
monsoon situation and the possible impact of El Niño conditions on agriculture in the 
country, including in Tamil Nadu, in close coordination with the India Meteorological 
Department (IMD), various Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) institutions, 
ICAR- Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Central Water 
Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop 
Forecast Centre (MNCFC), the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), the 
Department of Fertilisers (DoF) and State Governments.  
Further, the sowing operations for Kharif 2026-27 are still underway in Tamil Nadu, 
and the first advance estimates for all major Kharif crops in the 2026-27 agricultural year 
(July–June) have not yet been released.  
(b): The Government has laid special emphasis on promoting drought-resilient agriculture 
through crop diversification, cultivation of short-duration and drought-tolerant crop 
varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, water conservation practices, micro-irrigation, 
mulching, inter-cropping and other climate-resilient technologies. In view of the anticipated 
impact of El Niño conditions during Kharif 2026, farmers have been advised to shift from 
crops likely to be affected, to other short-duration crops. Further, assistance is being 
provided under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana – Per Drop More Crop 
(PDMC) for installation of micro-irrigation systems to improve water-use efficiency at the 
farm level. During 2026-27, Rs. 255.64 crores has been allocated to the State of Tamil 
Nadu for implementation of the PDMC Scheme and Rs.127.82 Crores has been released 
by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. A nationwide Khet Bachao 
Abhiyaan was organised during 1-30 June, 2026 in which 80,67,300 farmers participated 
in 1,14,567 programmes which were organised to promote water conservation, introduce 
efficient irrigation and climate-resilient farming practices.  

The Central Water Commission and State Governments have been advised to 
undertake advance planning for optimum utilization of reservoir water and promote 
efficient irrigation practices. Department of Rural Development is utilising Viksit Bharat – 
Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB G Ram G) funds for rejuvenating 
water structures – such as farm ponds, check dams, canal desilting, and bori bandhans – 
to trap every drop of early or residual rainfall. Further, as part of the climate resilient 
agricultural practices, the Department is also implementing various Schemes viz. the 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Mission for 
Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), National Food Security Mission (NFSM), 
Integrated Scheme on Oilseeds Mission, Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses and other 
existing programmes across the country.  
The District Agriculture Contingency Plan (DACP) has been prepared in 
consultation with the State Government of Tamil Nadu wherein suggestion for cultivation 
of short-duration and drought-tolerant crop varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, water 
conservation practices, micro-irrigation, mulching, inter-cropping and other climate-
resilient technologies has been made.  
(c): The Government has strengthened preparedness to safeguard farmers against 
potential crop losses, particularly in view of the anticipated El Niño conditions during Kharif 
2026. Under the existing crop insurance framework, the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(RWBCIS) continue to provide financial protection to farmers against crop losses arising 
from natural calamities and adverse weather events. PMFBY offers comprehensive 
insurance coverage from the pre-sowing stage to the post-harvest period, covering both 
widespread and localized risks. The implementation of these schemes remains voluntary 
for States/UTs and farmers and is carried out for notified crops and districts as identified 
by the respective State Governments. 
As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State Government 
is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground level in the 
wake of notified calamities including cyclones. The State Governments undertake relief 
measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State 
Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved 
items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered 
from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case 
of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-
Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum for assistance under NDRF 
submitted by the State Government. The financial assistance provided under SDRF and 
NDRF is by way of relief and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed. The details 
of fund allocation under SDRF State-wise during 2026-27 to 2030-31 (under the XVIth 
Finance Commission) as provided by the Ministry of Home Affairs is given at Annexure. 
(d): The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India continuously 
undertakes awareness programmes in collaboration with the State Governments and with 
active involvement of Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Indian 
Council of Agricultural Research and Krishi Vigyan Kendras to educate farmers on modern 
agricultural practices and enhance crop productivity, production and farmers’ income.  
The "Khet Bachao Abhiyan” has been undertaken from 1 June to 30 June, 2026 
across the country to create awareness among farmers about balanced and judicious use 
of fertilizers, reduce excessive application of DAP and urea to minimize the cost of 
cultivation. During the Abhiyan, more than 10 thousand programmes were organized in 
the State of Tamil Nadu involving approx. 3 lakhs farmers and other stakeholders. 

A Centrally Sponsored Scheme “Support to State Extension Programs for 
Extension Reforms” (ATMA) is being implemented in 734 districts of 28 states & 5 UTs in 
the country, including all the 37 districts of Tamil Nadu. The Scheme promotes a 
decentralized and farmer-friendly extension system in the country. The objective of the 
Scheme is to support State Government’s efforts and to make available latest agricultural 
technologies and good agricultural practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and 
allied areas to farmers through different extension activities viz; Farmers Training, 
Demonstrations, Exposure Visits, Kisan Mela, Mobilization of Farmers Groups and 
organizing Farm Schools etc.  During 2025-26, Rs. 43.70 Crores had been released under 
ATMA Scheme to Tamil Nadu, against which an expenditure of Rs. 43.55 Crores was 
incurred, benefitting more than 4 lakhs farmers in the State. During 2026-27, an allocation 
of Rs. 44.45 Crores has been made for Tamil Nadu.

3892. Shri Sanjay Uttamrao Deshmukh: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the number of cases of irregularities reported in 
various rural development schemes during the last three years, 
State-wise; 
(b)  whether the Government has conducted any inquiry in this 
regard, if so, the details thereof and  the action taken against 
the guilty officers/employees; 
(c)  the steps taken to prevent such irregularities in future; 
(d)  the present status of social audit in rural development schemes; 
(e)  the number of districts where regular social audit is being 
conducted; and 
(f)  the number of complaints received during the course of social 
audit? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
(a) & (b): The responsibility of implementation of various rural 
development schemes/programmes at ground level lies with the 
State Government and grievances/ complaints received in the 
Ministry are referred to the concerned State/UT authorities to 
undertake necessary verification/inquiry and also for taking 
appropriate action against the officials/persons found responsible, in 
accordance with the applicable rules and procedures.  Further, the 
Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) has put in place effective 
mechanisms to ensure transparency and accountability in the 
implementation of its programmes /schemes by the States/UTs. The 
Ministry also advises the States/UTs to take corrective and remedial 
measures wherever deficiencies are noticed. However, the Ministry 
does not maintain data about such cases. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(c): The implementation framework provided through schematic 
guidelines of the programmes prescribed by MoRD has inbuilt 
measures to prevent irregularities.  Further, end-to-end digital 
solutions have also been operationalized under the programmes to 
ensure ease of implementation, better targeting, effective delivery 
and improved transparency besides enabling concurrent monitoring 
/assessment of progress and effectiveness by the stakeholders 
concerned on real time basis.  Additionally, with a view to strengthen 
the preventive mechanism, grievance redressal has been made as an 
integral part in the implementation of the schemes/programmes and 
is being carried out as per the guidelines of the schemes on priorities. 
There is a procedure of lodging complaints on the Centralized Public 
Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal 
(pgportal.gov.in). The complaints received in the Ministry through 
CPGRAMs or otherwise, are forwarded to the respective State 
Governments for redressal of the grievance and furnishing the ATRs 
to the Ministry under intimation to the complainant within one month 
of receipt of the complaint. Further, the Ministry regularly reviews/ 
monitors proper implementation of the schemes by States/UTs 
through various forums such as Performance Review Committee 
meetings, Mid-term Reviews, Common Review Missions, NLMs, 
Empowered Committee meetings, Monthly Reviews, Area Officers 
visit, Video conferences etc.  
  
(d) to (f): Social audit is an important mechanism for ensuring 
transparency and accountability in the implementation of 
schemes/programmes. States/UTs, being responsible for 
implementation of the programmes at ground level, have been 
advised to undertake regular social audits in accordance with their 
laid down policies/guidelines. Complaints/irregularities noticed 
during the course of social audit are taken up by the State 
Governments/UT authorities concerned for verification and 
appropriate remedial actions. Regular social audits are being 
conducted in several districts across the country under the 
programmes and the Ministry continues to encourage States/UTs to 
strengthen and institutionalize social audit processes.

 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a): To develop integrated large scale and modern industrial infrastructure facility for entire 
value-chain of the textile industry, the Government has approved setting up of 7 (Seven) PM 
Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks in Greenfield /Brownfield sites 
with scheme outlay of Rs. 4,445 Crore for the period 2021 -22 to 2027-28. The Government has 
finalised 7 sites including one in Warangal, Telangana for setting up PM MITRA Parks. 
(b): The site was selected under brownfield category. ₹ 300 Cr. has already been expended 
towards development of trunk infrastructure. The park was formally inaugurated by Hon’ble 
Prime Minister on 10.05.2026. Currently, the park is operational with around 548 acres of land 
already being allotted to investors and c ommercial production has started. Once completed, the 
project is envisaged to generate 1 Lakh direct and 2 Lakh indirect Jobs. With existing 
commitments alone, over 24,400 direct jobs are expected to be generated. A strong majority of 
the workforce in oper ating apparel units comprises women. Structured skilling programs and 
local preference policies ensure gainful employment for youth and vulnerable sections, including 
Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST), fostering inclusive regional 
development.  With regards to handloom sector , budget is not allocated State -wise. Funds are 
released to eligible handloom agencies based on receipt of viable proposals under the extant 
scheme guidelines. Year -wise Budget Estimates and expenditure under the National Handloom 
Development Programme (NHDP) are mentioned in Annexure. 

(c) to (e):  The Ministry of Textiles is administering following schemes to strengthen the 
handloom sector and welfare of handloom workers across the country including Telangana: 
1. National Handloom Development Programme(NHDP); 
2. Raw Material Supply Scheme(RMSS); 
Under the above schemes, financial assistance is provided to eligible handloom agencies/workers 
for raw materials, procurement of upgraded looms & accessories, solar lighting units, 
construction of workshed, skilling, product diversification & design innovation, technical and 
common infrastructure, publicity and brand development through India Handloom Brand (IHB), 
Handloom Mark (HLM) and GI tag, e -commerce facilities, marketing of handloom  products in 
domestic/overseas markets, concessional loans under weavers’ MUDRA scheme and social 
security etc. 
Further, the following support has been provided to handloom sector in Telangana during since 
2014:  
 35 Small Handloom Clusters have been taken up for financial assistance of Rs.21.29 
crore benefitting to 7,962 handloom workers.  
 86 marketing events organized to facilitate and promote sales of Handloom Products. 
 To enhance productivity, marketing capabilities and facilitate better incomes, 36 
Handloom Producer companies have been formed. 
 8,604 beneficiaries provided loans under Weavers’ MUDRA Scheme. 
 52,149 beneficiaries enrolled under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and 
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana. 
 Total 149 lakh kg of yarn supplied under Transport Subsidy & Price Subsidy.
