GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3894 
FOR ANSWER ON 11.08.2026  
 
 
STEEL SCRAP RECYCLING POLICY AND RESOURCE EFFICIENCY 
 
 
3894. SHRI ANURAG SHARMA: 
 
 Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the current status of implementation of the Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in the 
country, including the major initiatives undertaken thereunder, year and State/UT-
wise; 
 
(b) the details of steel scrap recycling capacity created and the quantity of steel scrap 
processed and recycled so far, year and State/UT-wise; 
 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to promote organised scrap collection, 
scientific processing, shredding infrastructure and greater utilisation of domestically 
recycled steel scrap in steel manufacturing for reducing raw material imports and 
carbon emissions, State/UT-wise; 
 
(d) the strategy adopted by the Government to develop a robust and sustainable 
ecosystem for steel scrap recycling through public-private participation, investment 
promotion, regulatory support and technology adoption, State/UT-wise; and 
 
(e) the outcomes achieved in terms of resource efficiency, circular economy, energy 
conservation, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and enhancement of the 
competitiveness of the domestic steel sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a),(c)&(d): The current status of implementation of Steel Scrap Recycling Policy in 
the country including the measures taken by the Government to promote organized 
scrap collection, scientific processing and utilization of domestically recycled steel 
scrap in steel manufacturing as well as measures to develop robust and sustainable 
ecosystem for steel scrap recycling through public-private participation, investment 
promotion, regulatory support and technology adoption across the country are as 
under: -  
(i) The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy, 2019 provides a coordination framework with 
various Ministries to promote recycling of ferrous scrap generated from various 
sources. 
 
Contd…..2/- 
 

 
: 2 : 
(ii) The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has formulated the 
Vehicle Scrapping Policy, 2021 that includes a system of incentives/disincentives 
for creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Under the 
policy, MoRTH has issued rules for Registration and Functions of Vehicle Scrapping 
Facility (RVSF), which provides the procedures and infrastructure facilities required 
for de-pollution and dismantling of End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) for further recovery 
of metal and other materials under environmental regulations. As on 24.07.2026, 
151 Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs) are operational across 23 
States/UTs. 
 
(iii)  The Government of India has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes 
(Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to ensure safe handling, 
storage, recycling, utilisation, treatment and disposal of hazardous and other 
wastes in an environmentally safe manner. 
 
(iv)   Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change has introduced the 
Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025, which establishes a 
framework for managing End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) in an environmentally sound 
manner and mandates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), requiring vehicle 
producers to meet annual scrapping targets based on the type of vehicle and 
materials recovered. 
 
(v)    Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 has been notified by Ministry of Shipping, Ports 
and Waterways with aims to regulate and promote the safe and environmentally 
sound recycling of ships. 
 
(b) During Financial Year 2025-26, total 36 million tonnes ferrous scrap was 
recycled for production of steel, of which approximately 28 million tonnes of scrap was 
generated domestically and 8 million tonnes were imported.  The state/UT-wise details 
of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs) across the country is available on 
the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ parivahan portal at the URL given 
below: - 
 
‘https://vscrap.parivahan.gov.in/vehiclescrap/vahan/rvsfdetails.xhtml’. 
 
(e) Steel is a deregulated sector and the Government acts as a facilitator by 
creating a conducive policy environment for the development of steel sector in the 
country. The initiatives taken by the Government and their outcomes in terms of 
resource efficiency, energy conservation, reduction of greenhouse gas emissions are 
as under:- 
 
 
(i) Ministry of Steel has released the Taxonomy for Green Steel for defining and 
categorizing the low emission steel. During Financial Year 2025-26, 90 steel units 
have been awarded green steel certification under the notified Green Steel 
Taxonomy Framework. 
 
(ii) Four pilot projects have been awarded for implementation of pilot projects for 
use of hydrogen in steel sector under National Green Hydrogen Mission launched 
by Ministry of New & Renewable Energy.  
 
Contd…..3/- 
 

 
: 3 : 
 
(iii) National Solar Mission launched by Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in 
January, 2010 promotes the use of solar energy and also helps to reduce the 
emission of steel industry. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Power has notified Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) on 
28.06.2023 for regulating Indian Carbon Market across various industrial sectors, 
which is also applicable to steel plants.  
For competitiveness of domestic steel sector, the Government has launched 
the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty Steel with a financial 
outlay of ₹ 6322 crore. The Scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of the 
domestic steel industry by promoting investment and the domestic production of value-
added specialty steel, reducing import dependence, and strengthening domestic 
manufacturing capabilities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
LOK SABHA

ASSISTANCE TO COASTAL FISHERMEN 
 
3898.  SHRI GODAM NAGESH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the details of total fish production in the country during the last five years, year-wise; 
(b)  whether the fish production has increased or decreased as compared to previous  years; 
(c)  the details of financial assistance and development programmes implemented for the 
welfare and livelihood of coastal fishermen during the said period; 
(d)  whether the Government has undertaken any measures for the development of fishing  
harbours, fish landing centres and other fisheries infrastructure in coastal areas, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(e)  the details of funds released and beneficiaries covered under such schemes, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) and (b): The annual fish production in the country has registered a steady increase from 
147.25 lakh tonnes in 2020–21 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25. The year-wise fish production 
during the period from 2020–21 to 2024–25 is as follows: 
Sl No Year Fish production (in lakh tonnes) 
1 2020-21 147.25 
2 2021-22 162.48 
3 2022-23 175.45 
4 2023-24 183.93 
5 2024-25 197.75 
 
(c) to (e): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  
has been implementing the following schemes/ programmes for holistic development of fisheries 
including welfare of coastal fishermen in the country.  
(i) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):  The Department has been  
implementing PMMSY from Financial Y ear 2020 -21 with  an estimated investment of 

Rs.20,750 crore for holistic development of fisheries sector including welfare of fishers 
and fish farmers in the country.  
 
(ii) Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF):  In order to 
address the infrastructure requirement for fisheries sector, FIDF was launched in the year 
2018-19 with a total funds size of Rs 7522.48 crore. FIDF provides concessional finance 
to the Eligible Entities (EEs), including State Governments/Union  Territories for 
development of identified fisheries infrastructure facilities. The Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India provides interest subvention up to 3% per annum for the repayment 
period of 12 years inclusive of moratorium of 2 years for pro viding the concessional 
finance by the Nodal Loaning Entities (NLEs) at the interest rate not lower than 5% per 
annum.  
 
(iii) Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY):  To make the 
fisheries sector resilient and incentivize adoption of efficienc ies in fisheries value chain, 
the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has been implementing a Central Sector 
Sub-scheme "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY)" a sub -
scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with an investment 
of Rs. 6000 crore. PMMKSSY aims at formalization of the fisheries sector, incentivizing 
the aquaculture insurance, fisheries micro and small enterprises value chain efficiency, 
adoption of safety and quality system for safe fish production etc. 
 
(iv)  Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish farmers:  Additionally, t he 
Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018 -19 has extended the Kisan

The development of fishing harbours, fish landing centres and fisheries infrastructure facilities 
is one of the important areas envisaged and are supported under the PMMSY and FIDF. Under

Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years has approved another 
94 fishing harbours and fish landing centres at a total of cost of Rs.4916.46 crore and its projects 
cost restricted for interest subvention at Rs.3651.19 crore. The Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India under PMMSY and FIDF has also approved proposals amounting to Rs 
2,797 crore for development of cold chain and marketing facil ities in the country  including 
coastal areas. The key activities approved includes; 775 cold storages and ice plants, 28,489 units 

of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with

TEXTILE RECYCLING AND CIRCULAR ECONOMY 
 
3899#.  SHRI DAMODAR AGRAWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy framework to promote textile recycling 
and the concept of a circular economy in the textile sector;  
(b) If so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether any incentives have been provided to industries adopting textile recycling 
technologies; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof including the number of beneficiary units?  
      
                                                                  उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (d):  The Government has undertaken several initiatives to promote textile recycling, 
adoption of recycling technologies and the transition towards a circular economy in the textile 
sector: 
i) In the Union Budget 2026 –27, the Hon'ble Finance Minister announced the „Tex -Eco 
Initiative‟ to promote a globally competitive and sustainable textiles and apparel sector. The 
initiative aims to support innovative technologies for the circular econo my, including textile 
waste management, recycling and value addition, development of recycled fibres, new materials, 
sustainable packaging and other high -value products from discarded textiles, in collaboration 
with research institutions, Textile Research Associations, Centres of Excellence, industry, start -
ups and other stakeholders. 
ii) The Ministry of Textiles has undertaken a study titled “Mapping of Textile Waste Value 
Chain in India”.  The report estimates the generation of textile waste from pre -consumer 
sources such as manufacturing waste as well as post-consumer waste.  
iii) The Government has also constituted an Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Task 
Force to deliberate on sustainable production, certification and exports, besides facilitating 
industry-centric programmes such as Circular Samvaad and the Cluster Exchange Mechanism. 
iv) The Government is also promoting textile recycling and sustainable manufacturing through 
policy support, research, innovation and capacity-building initiatives, including:  

 The UNIDO -Global Environment Facility (GEF) project on eliminating  hazardous 
chemicals from the textile fashion supply chain;  
 The UNEP supported In -Tex India Project for Accelerating the Transition of the Indian 
Textile Sector towards Circularity using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product 
Environmental Footprint (PEF);  
 Support for environmentally sustainable research and development under the National 
Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM);  
 Development of a sustainability framework for PM MITRA Parks; and  
 Promotion of upcycled products in Government procurement through an MoU among the 
Textiles Committee, Standing Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE) and 
Government e-Marketplace (GeM). 
  
These initiatives are sector -wide and are intended to facilitate technology adoption, research, 
innovation, sustainable manufacturing and circular economy practices across the textile value 
chain.

(c) to (e): Government is implementing the Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH),Centrally Sponsored Scheme for holistic development of the

is provided to assist farmers in the adoption ofprotected cultivation technologies. Such 
support is provided through State Horticulture Missions, TechnicalSupport Groups (TSGs), 
Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of Excellence (CoEs), ICAR 
Institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other

       As per information received from State Government, Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH) is being implemented in all 75 districts of Uttar 
Pradesh, including Sitapur and Lakhimpur Kheri. The marketing-related components 
available to farmers under the scheme are as follows:

ended subsidy at 35% of the project cost is provided to eligible beneficiaries. 
ii. Static / Mobile Vending Cart/Platform with Cool Chamber – Subsidy of 50% of the 
total project cost is provided to eligible beneficiaries. 
iii. Modified Retail Reefer Van with Retail Counter (to be linked with an Integrated 
Pack House) – Credit-linked back-ended subsidy at 35% of the project cost is 
provided to eligible beneficiaries. 
 
 Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component 
under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which are 
perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). The 
objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making 
distress sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices 
tend to fall below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 
percent decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is 
implemented at the request of a State/UT government.

†3904. Shri Ashish Dubey: 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the funds allocated and disbursed by the Central Government under 
the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) Scheme during the last three 
years;  
(b) whether monitoring mechanisms are being implemented to increase credit flow in 
districts with low financial inclusion under the recently launched Pradhan Mantri 
Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana;  
(c) if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) the extent to which the credit targets set at the grassroots level have been 
achieved by commercial banks and rural cooperative banks? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी     (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 
(a):      In the last three years viz. FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, an amount of more than 
₹1.85 lakh crore has been disbursed. In the latest 23rd instalment released in June 
2026, 9.54 Crore beneficiaries received the benefits of the Scheme. 
  

(b) & (c): The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) was 
approved by the Union Cabinet on 16th July, 2025 to cover 100 districts and was 
formally launched on 11th October, 2025. The 100 districts covered under PM-DDKY 
have been identified on the basis of 3 indicators of low crop productivity, low cropping 
intensity and less agricultural credit disbursement. DDKY envisages convergence of 
existing 36 schemes of 11 Departments/ Ministries with State Government Schemes 
and private participation. The scheme aims at facilitating both short-term and long-
term credit in the identified districts through activities such as credit extension through 
Kisan Credit Card (KCC), support for infrastructure creation under the Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund (AIF) and the provision of Revolving Fund (RF) & Community 
Investment Fund (CIF).  
 
 A structured monitoring mechanism is in place to strengthen institutional credit 
flow in all districts, across country, including those identified under the Pradhan Mantri 
Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY). NABARD prepares Potential Linked 
Credit Plans (PLPs) for every district, which form the basis for District Credit Plans 
(DCPs) formulated involving the Block Level Bankers' Committees (BLBCs), District 
Consultative Committees (DCCs) and State Level Bankers' Committees (SLBCs). 
Based on these plans, Ground Level Credit (GLC) targets are fixed and monitored 
across agencies and regions. The progress of credit flow is regularly reviewed in 
District Level Bankers' Committee (DLBC) and State Level Bankers' Committee 
(SLBC) meetings to identify bottlenecks and take corrective measures. These are 
further reviewd and monitored at NABARD and government.  
 
Progress on various Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), including agricultural 
credit, in PMDDKY districts is also monitored through the Scheme's monitoring 
framework, which includes a dashboard-based monitoring system, monthly ranking of 
districts based on progress and outcomes, periodic reviews by the Central Committee 
and NITI Aayog, and regular field visits by the Central Nodal Officer (CNO) assigned 
to each district. 
  

 Further, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has identified low-credit districts 
requiring focused attention to address regional imbalances in agricultural credit, 
through a system of differential weighting framework under Priority Sector 
Lending (PSL), whereby higher weights are assigned to credit disbursed in identified 
low-credit districts to incentivise banks to expand credit outreach in underserved 
regions. 35 districts of PMDDKY districts also falls under this category and are being 
monitored by RBI. Special efforts are also undertaken in these districts through 
targeted interventions, including support under the Financial Inclusion Fund, 
awareness and credit saturation campaigns, and close coordination with banks and 
State Governments to improve access to institutional credit. 
 In addition, the Government of India digitally monitors the progress of 
agriculture credit through KCC through periodic reviews using the Kisan Rin Portal 
(KRP), enabling district-wise tracking of credit flow and timely follow-up with States 
and lending institutions including to improve expansion of KCC. These measures are 
aimed at improving financial inclusion and enhancing the availability of institutional 
credit in PMDDKY districts. 
 Between 30 April 2025 and 30 April 2026, the number of beneficiary MISS 
accounts in PM-DDKY districts increased from 70.87 Lakh to 75 Lakh. During the 
same period, the loan disbursed has increased from Rs.1.27 lakh crores to Rs. 1.78 
lakh crores.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3907 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11th August, 2026 
 
PREPAREDNESS FOR EL NINO AND PMFBY 
3907. SHRI RAMASHANKAR VIDHARTHI RAJBHAR: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the emergency measures taken by the Government to protect Kharif crops in 
view of the likely EI Nino situation; 
(b) the average time taken to settle insurance claims under Pradhan Mantri Fasal 
Bima Yojana (PMFBY) during the last three years; 
(c) the special relief package proposed for rain-fed farmers of Deoria, Ballia and 
Purvanchal; and 
(d) whether the Government is contemplating to provide additional financial 
assistance for drought affected areas? 
 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): The Government reviewed the preparedness for the Kharif season, including 
the likely impact of El Niño conditions, at the National Kharif Conference held on 28–
29 May 2026 with Agriculture Ministers and senior officials from States/UTs. The 
Conference reviewed crop planning, seed and fertilizer availability, water management 
and region-specific challenges, and advised States to strengthen preparedness 
through timely availability of critical inputs, efficient water management, close 
monitoring of weather conditions, dissemination of advisories to farmers, and 
implementation of contingency measures in coordination with IMD, ICAR and State 
Governments. Further, the Government has undertaken the following measures: 
(i) District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) have been updated for 15 
States covering 342 Districts which are likely to receive below normal rainfall by the 
ICAR Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) in consultation 
with the States for implementation. Further, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) 
have also been issued by ICAR for Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) for mitigation of El 
Niño-related risks.  
  

(ii) Weekly meeting of the Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG) is being held with 
the representatives of India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water 
Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National 
Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), Indian Council of Agriculture Research - Central 
Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA), Department of Fertilizers, 
Department of Food & Public Distribution and the State Governments to review rainfall 
situation, reservoir storage, groundwater levels, crop sowing, input availability, market 
situation and pest/ disease incidence for timely intervention. Meeting with State 
Agriculture Secretaries and Relief Commissioners held under the chairmanship of 
Secretary (DA&FW) on 27.04.2026 to review availability of inputs like seeds, fodder, 
drinking & irrigation water, fertilizers and general preparedness. Further, a meeting of 
the Crisis Management Group had been conducted on 17.06.2026 to assess and 
strengthen preparedness for the monsoon. In addition, the National Disaster 
Management Authority has also reviewed the preparedness of below-normal rainfall 
conditions emanating from the likely impact of the El Nino conditions on 19th June 
2026. Review of the situation has been undertaken by the Agriculture Minister, 
Government of India with the State Agriculture Ministers for Kharif preparedness amid 
El Nino conditions on 23.06.2026. 
 
(iii)  Adequate availability of seeds has been ensured, against the demand of 
172.80 lakh quintals from the States, there was availability of 192.25 lakh quintals of 
Kharif crop seeds. States have maintained 1% seeds i.e. 1.74 Lakh quintals as 
National Seed Reserve.  
 
(iv) Special emphasis has been laid on promoting crop diversification, promotion of 
short-duration and drought-tolerant crop varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, water 
conservation practices, micro-irrigation, mulching, inter-cropping and practices of 
other climate-resilient technologies.  
 
(v) A nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyaan was organised during 1-30 June, 2026 in 
which 80,67,300 farmers participated in 1,14,567 programmes which were organised 
to promote water conservation, introduce efficient irrigation and climate-resilient 
farming practices. Simultaneously, an intensive Kisan Credit Card (KCC) saturation 
drive is being implemented in the vulnerable districts.  
  

(vi)  Government has been implementing the yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal 
Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and the weather index-based Restructured Weather Based 
Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) since Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to 
farmers against crop losses arising from natural calamities and adverse weather 
events, thereby stabilizing farm income. PMFBY provides comprehensive insurance 
coverage from pre-sowing to post-harvest against widespread and localized risks. The 
schemes are voluntary for States/UTs and farmers, with implementation based on 
districts and crops notified by the concerned State Governments. In the identified 
vulnerable districts, awareness and enrolment drives are also being undertaken to 
enhance insurance coverage. 
 
(vii) The Central Water Commission and State Governments have been advised to 
undertake advance planning for optimum utilization of reservoir water and promote 
efficient irrigation practices. Assistance to farmers is available through ongoing 
schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana: Per Drop More Crop 
(PDMC) with a focus on enhancing water-use efficiency at the farm level through 
installation of Micro-Irrigation systems. Department of Rural Development is utilising 
Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB G Ram G) 
funds for rejuvenating water structures – such as farm ponds, check dams, canal 
desilting, and bori bandhans – to trap every drop of early or residual rainfall. Further, 
as part of the climate resilient agricultural practices, the Department is also 
implementing various Schemes viz. the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), 
Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), 
National Food Security Mission (NFSM), Integrated Scheme on Oilseeds Mission, 
Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses and other existing programmes across the 
country. 
(b): Further, in respect of average time taken to settle insurance claims under 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), it is clarified that majority of the claims 
are settled within the stipulated timelines under the Operational Guidelines of the 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) i.e. within 21 days of the receipt of 
requisite yield data from the concerned State Government by the insurance 
companies. However, during the implementation of PMFBY, some claims remained 
pending, primarily on account of  
 Delay in providing State Government share of claims. 
 Incorrect/delayed submission of insurance proposals by banks and 
unverified bank account details of enrolled farmers. 
 Discrepancy in yield data & consequent disputes between State 
Government and insurance companies, etc.  
The pending claims on account of these issues are settled after their resolution 
as per provisions of the operational guidelines of the scheme. 
  

(c) & (d):    As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures at the 
ground level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake 
relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of 
the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the approved 
guidelines. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from 
the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of 
disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an 
Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). The financial assistance provided under SDRF 
and NDRF is by way of relief and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed.  
The details of fund allocation under SDRF State-wise during 2026-27 to 2030-
31 (under the XVIth Finance Commission) as provided by the Ministry of Home Affairs

Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and number of rural households registered for wage 
employment in Peddapalli Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b)  the number of person-days generated during the last three 
financial years in Peddapalli, Mancherial, Jagtial and 
Jayashankar Bhupalpally portions of the Constituency;

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

SOIL CONSERVATION 
3909.  SHRI RAMBHUAL NISHAD: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to address the problems of sodic land, 
waterlogging and soil erosion in Sultanpur district; 
(b) if so, the details of the schemes implemented to increase productivity and support small 
and marginal farmers; 
(c)whether the Government proposes to expand schemes such as organic farming, Seed 
Village Scheme, water conservation and crop residue management in the said district; and 
(d) the details of the assistance being provided to encourage allied activities such as dairy, 
poultry, goat rearing and fisheries in Sultanpur district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b):  As per information received from the Government of Uttar Pradesh, steps 
have been taken to address the problems of sodic land, waterlogging and soil erosion in 
Sultanpur district. To control soil erosion and increase productivity, under the Pandit Deen 
Dayal Upadhyay Kisan Samridhi Yojana, bunding and check dam construction, along with 
land levelling, are carried out on the fields of small and marginal farmers of the district. In 
the following year, crop production activities are undertaken by the Agriculture Department 
on the same fields to support these farmers and enhance productivity. 
 
(c) & (d): As per information received from the Government of Uttar Pradesh, Organic 
Farming and the Seed Village Scheme are not implemented in Sultanpur district. Under 
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) 
micro-irrigation is promoted in the country including Sultanpur district and an area of 7615 
ha has been covered since 2015-16 in the district. Further, under the Central Sector 
Scheme on Crop Residue Management, being implemented in Uttar Pradesh including 
Sultanpur District. Under the scheme, financial assistance @ 50% is provided to farmers 
and @ 80% to Rural Entrepreneurs/ Cooperative Societies/ FPOs for crop residue 
management machinery and Custom Hiring Centres. Rs. 911.03 crore has been released 
to Uttar Pradesh under the scheme since 2018-19. 
 
 The Government is taking up various activities for holistic development of allied 
agricultural sectors such as dairy, poultry, goat rearing and fisheries in the country including 
Uttar Pradesh through Centrally Sponsored/ Sector Schemes. The schemes are 
implemented by State Governments as per the development planning in different districts. 
As per information received from the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the details of 
assistance provided in the Sultanpur district to encourage allied activities is as follows: 
 
(i)  Dairy: State Government under the Swadeshi Gau Samvardhan Yojana, farmers/ 
animal husbandry practitioners are encouraged to purchase 2 milch animals to increase 

milk production, with a subsidy / assistance of upto 40%. Further, under the Nandini Krishak 
Samriddhi Yojana and Mini Nandini Krishak Samriddhi Yojana, farmers are encouraged to 
purchase 25 and 10 milch animals respectively to increase milk production, with provision 
of subsidy assistance @ 50%. Formation of dairy cooperative societies and infrastructure 
support such as furniture, milk testing equipment, cattle feed, mineral mixture, data 
processing and Dairy Processing & Collection Milk Units (D.P.C.M.U.) and training to milk 
producers for clean milk production are also taken up Dairy Development Department of 
State Government. 
 
(ii)  Poultry, Goat Rearing and Sheep Rearing: To support economically weaker 
sections, the Department provides 50 chicks, along with feed, medicine and shelter 
arrangements, worth Rs. 425, free of cost to women beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled 
Caste category in the district. Beneficiaries from economically weaker sections are also 
provided assistance for purchase of 5 goats and 1 buckling (male goat), with free insurance 
and medicine. Assistance is also provided for purchase of 20 sheep and 1 ram, with free 
insurance and medicine for beneficiaries from economically weaker sections. 
 
(iii)  Fisheries: Fisheries development activities are supported under Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) of Department of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying in the country including Sultanpur District. Under the scheme, 306 beneficiaries 
have been assisted with subsidy amounting Rs. 258.69 lakh for fisheries development 
activities such as Backyard RAS, Biofloc Ponds, Pond Construction, Small & Medium RAS 
units, Small & Medium Feed Mills and transport support through Cycle/Motorcycle/Three-
Wheeler with Ice Box.

COMPUTERISATION IN UTTARAKHAND 
  
†3910. SHRI AJAY BHATT: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the funds allocated by the Government for the development of Gram Panchayats 
in Uttarakhand during the last five years, district-wise and year-wise; 
  
(b) the details of the Gram Panchayats computerized in Uttarakhand, district-wise; and 
  
(c) the total number of Gram Panchayats computerized in the said State? 
 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
  
(a) “Panchayat”, being a “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of the State List of the 
Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operated through the 
respective State Panchayati Raj Acts, which may vary from State to State, subject to the 
provisions of the Constitution. As per Article 243H of the Constitution of India, legislature of the 
State may, by law, authorize a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls 
and fees in accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits and assign to the 
Panchayats such taxes, duties, tolls and fees levied and collected by the State Government for 
such purposes and subject to such conditions and limits as may be specified in the law. 
  
However, Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides the basis for the Central Finance 
Commissions to assess the status of finances of the Union, States and their respective local 
bodies and recommend sharing of taxes as well as grants for various purposes to the States and 
Local Bodies. The Finance Commission grant can be used by Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) for 
location-specific felt needs under 29 subjects enshrined in the Eleventh Schedule of the 
Constitution, except for salary or other establishment expenditures.  
  
The year-wise details of the grants allocated under the Fifteenth Finance Commission to all three 
tiers of panchayats including Gram Panchayats in Uttarakhand during the last five years are as 
under:-
